title: Good App but Key Features Missing if you share finances
content: I have been using this app since April 2021, and it worked great for me while I was single. However, I’ve been married since 2023, and now that my partner and I share certain finances (not all, but some), this budgeting app has become really difficult to use effectively.  The biggest missing feature is the ability to automatically split transactions for specific shared accounts, transaction types, . My partner and I have a shared credit card and a few shared accounts, and Rocket Money makes it extremely difficult to maintain an accurate budget because I have to manually split every single transaction myself.  As a result, my budget data is constantly skewed. It appears that I spend far more money than I actually do simply because I have not gone through and manually split transactions yet. At this point, the budgeting aspect of the app has become essentially useless for me, aside from allowing me to see all my purchases in one place across all my accounts.  And yes, that the worldview of my spending is nice, but unfortunately not enough to justify continuing to pay for a premium subscription that is meant for budgeting.   I was recently told about another app that already offers the type of automatic transaction splitting I’m looking for. I really do not want to switch platforms after using Rocket Money for so long, but the amount of manual work required has become unbearable for a paid budgeting app.  Plus I KNOW this feature has been asked for years based on the rocket money “request a feature” forum for years… but no dice. So I may have to move on sadly..

title: Monarch Made Taxes & Biz Ops So Much Easier!
content: If you’re looking for a budgeting app that is the complete package, this is it - it has an elegant design (+1–orange is my fave too), a UX that is easy to navigate and customize, for both quick glance features and in-depth info with charts, filters, tags, colors, etc.  My personal fave features are the Recurring section where it lists all your monthly recurring income and expenses and shows you a calendar with dots on the days and notifies you in a few days in advance so you’re always prepared.   The other is the Create Rule feature that allows you to take a transaction and customize it to automatically have attributes you assign for all future transactions. Say you have a business expense for supplies every few months that you want to tag (label) as business-related and/or as a tax write-off - any time you make this purchase in the future it will now have those tags. You can also edit the merchant name to better match what it reflects and much more.   Lastly I recently had to fill out 6 months of profit & loss forms for legal purposes and I used the new AI they’ve implemented to automatically gather the items I specified, itemize them, and give me totals so I could simply plug-in the numbers (after double checking them for accuracy, of course 😉).   I know there’s a number of good financial budgeting apps out there right now, but I’m glad I decided to try Monarch and it’s been so helpful with taxes and other legal uses that I’ve decided to keep subscribing at $14.99/month.   At times, I wish it were a little cheaper, but when you consider the real-life implications of financial organization (or lack thereof) and how the practicality of an app like this changes the game for those things, the value you get in return is worth a lot more than $14.99 a month.   Highly recommended app if you’re serious about your financial life.

content: I’ve been a long time subscriber. The constant UI changes are getting on my nerves. Once you get used to them, the devs completely change the app for no increase in functionality or purpose. I would consider different budgeting apps

title: Used to be great…
content: The new changes were unwanted, not intuitive and threw me for a loop with trying to figure out how to put in a credit card payment. The clear button used to be so easy, now it’s an extra click. It seems YNAB forgot to do usability testing.

title: June 2026 update
content: You now have to do multiple clicks to clear a transaction. The interface was good, now it’s clunky looking. I wish they would keep it simple. It wasn’t broke before, it didn’t need to be changed.  Update: 6/15/26 well their customer service is run by AI and doing a poor job. I emailed asking a question about wanting to cancel but I wanted to make certain I would avoid a refund back on my original form of payment that I no longer have the account for. Their “customer service agent” did not answer my question nor confirm if I wanted proceed with cancelling my subscription. They CANCELLED my account and I didn’t even have time to download my latest account file. It would have been 9 years down the drain had I not downloaded a copy 3 days before. Customer service is a joke.

title: No more spreadsheets!
content: I’ve been using YNAB for around 5 years now and it has been such a useful tool as I’ve become for financially literate. Highly recommend checking out their podcasts and YouTube videos along with the app.

title: Over 100 bucks
content: Wouldn’t buy unless you are ready to spend over 100 bucks to use… kind of counter intuitive to my goal downloading this app

title: Great but getting expensive
content: See title

title: Great Budget
content: Love this budget program. I wish I would have had this many years ago. Are bill are payed each month and we owe no one. Our credit score is 838. The highest it has ever been. Thanks to my daughter who helped train us on YNAB. There is a learning curve, but after 6 months we have it down.

title: It’s the Best!!
content: I’ve been using YNAB for over 10 years, it’s the best way to manage spending and budgeting I’ve ever found. I used spreadsheets and then quicken prior to this. Other methods could tell me where the money went, but they didn’t help me save for future expenses like unexpected car repairs or gifts or travel. The difference is that YNAB helps plan where the money will go in real time and helps me make decisions about spending going forward - as in do I want to spend on travel vs clothing. The only downside is that there is a bit of a learning curve, but it’s so worth it. I’m over 60 and recently retired and it’s been great to help me feel comfortable with spending in my retirement years. I also used it to manage spending for a small business.

title: Buggy Issues
content: When deleting old targets and creating new targets the “money needed by…” doesn’t reset.  Also, no inflow transaction is showing in any categories even when clearing it.

title: Latest updates make this unusable
content: I’ve been using YNAB for almost 10 years now, but will have to look for an alternate. The last few rounds of design updates make the app almost unusable. Gratuitous UX choices make the key components difficult to find and add taps where they don’t need to be. Not sure what they’re trying to prove, but it’s certainly not that they’re thinking of their users.

title: Used to be the gold standard
content: The app and platform used to be the be all, end all for budgeting, but over the past few years has gotten progressively more expensive, and even more convoluted.  If you are already in the YNAB environment, the app is well made, but if you are looking for a budgeting solution as a new user, I would implore you to look elsewhere, to a company that still cares.

title: Great expense tracker
content: Great expense tracker

title: YNAB
content: I love this program. It keeps me on track with my money. I now am a few months ahead so I no longer worry about money. I like living each day knowing all my bills are covered.

title: Updates are getting worse!
content: Why do have to do more clicks now! It used to be simple and intuitive, now the UI has gotten complicated! Boo! Not a happy customer!

title: Used to be good but increasingly annoying updates
content: Every unnecessary update makes a previously simple task slightly harder for no reason. Things that used to be one click are now 3, menus get rearranged, the layout is reformatted, all these compounding inconveniences result in an increasingly unpleasant user experience. Every time it’s arbitrary and adds nothing but is clearly change for the sake of saying it was updated. Looking into alternatives after years of use.

title: Transaction Screen and shortcut Issues
content: Please remove the “more” extra tap on the transaction screen so we don’t have to do extra taps to clear a transaction. Also Apple Shortcut integration is not functioning properly since the change to Spending/Inflow on the transaction screen from the previous choices of Outflow/Inflow. The YNAB shortcut of “Add transaction for” in shortcuts still has Outflow/Inflow as the choices and if you send the output as an Inflow to YNAB the app is treating it as “Spending”. Also please stop pushing your book in app I pay over $100 a year for.

title: UI/UX Breaking Point
content: YNAB doesn’t listen to users. Period.   The iOS UI/UX gets worse with every update. More friction, more clicks, appalling what YNAB has become.

title: Method works. App is ok.
content: YNAB Method is still 5/5.  The app however, continues to have updates that require more clicks for previously easy to use functions. I don’t think it’s one singular update, but rather the trajectory of the past few updates while of course raising the subscription price in the process. Find myself using the desktop more than the app.

title: Too labor intensive
content: Had high hopes for this but it is way too labor intensive and requires you to go to Through every line item on your spending to assign it. The UX is very weak. I’m disappointed and will not renew.

title: Does nothing unless you pay
content: Very sneaky making me give you bunch of info, then make me sign up with email, then finally asking for money.

title: Does the design team use the app?
content: What is happening here? Every update moves buttons, it keeps trying to auto populate the wrong categories, it fails to sync for days and then slams me with 30 transactions to link. Just recently it reloaded the budget from like 3 days ago, then went to the actual current correct state, then said I was -$600 to budget, then I had a surplus. Why isn’t this done on device THEN reconciled in the cloud? I have gotten people to use this app and I’m nervous the updates are screwing with them. You shouldn’t have to check your bank app every transaction to make sure YNAB did its job - that is the whole point of YNAB! Enter in there, it checks your bank, done! Truly bad. Our subscription just renewed but I’ll seriously consider leaving next renewal period. I’d rather go back to paper and at least know what’s available to spend.

title: Moving in the wrong direction
content: New leadership is backwards. Degrading app updates, a reduction in content, and overall out of touch with users. Used to be amazing, now it’s garbage.

title: Progressively Worse
content: While I like YNAB, it has managed to get both worse and more expensive over the years. The UI changes too often and sadly in ways that make it more difficult to use. The “updates” sometimes introduce bugs. I’d rather they keep the application stable and usable than try to justify the price hikes by constantly tweaking the user experience.

title: Getting Worse
content: Been using YNAB for years and the app just gets worse. The price goes up and all we get is “blurple” and a more confusing UI. Every change makes the workflow in the app less efficient. Read your reviews. You are alienating your customer base. You’ve pushed me to look for alternatives and I’m starting to test them in hopes of finding something better. The concept is so good and has helped me so much. Stop ruining your own product.

title: Update Clearing ?!?
content: I love YNAB but this latest update is not it! So many extra steps just to clear a transaction - I had to ask the chatbot just to figure out how to do it, and even then, it took me a while to see it. It’s not even remotely intuitive, multiple extra steps, and a huge hassle. I am disappointed because I am trying to get my family to budget and recommend this app but mine and their confidence to do this simply is now diminished with all these extra steps. Just put it back on the transaction screen, PLEASE.

title: App is Getting Worse
content: YNAB keeps going backwards.  The app is worse than it used to be, hiding necessary options to “reduce visual clutter”.  It also no longer syncs with banks it used to connect to.

title: Disappointed fan
content: It’s become harder and harder to recommend this program to folks, due to an insane amount of pointless changes to the app and website over the last couple years - on top of increased cost. Little to no features have been introduced, yet the user experience gets worse with every update - routine actions that were previously easy to see and required 1-2 taps are now hidden behind menus and require more interaction. Reports haven’t been meaningfully improved on desktop in the 4 years I’ve been using YNAB, and neither have targets. It’s been mostly pointless renaming of terms (budget became ‘plan’ because of social media reasons?). Plus, they just laid off arguably the most enjoyable medias of their social media team, so I don’t know what metrics they’re trying to hit but apparently they’re not good enough for whatever CEO they have now. Plus last week we had our first pop up ad for the founders’ new book! Great, we’re shilling paying members now! Only gets 2 stars because it has historically been a very helpful app, but I think we’re seeing a shift towards a much worse platform in the future.

title: The Best
content: Couldn't be without it!

title: Going consistently downhill
content: The YNAB mobile app designers and developers have entered the phase of "change for changes sake". So many of the UI/UX changes that have been made recently violate basic principles of UX. More scrolling and more taps for what used to take one tap. Most recently, approving a matched transaction. You now have to scroll down, tap a widget to expand hidden details that used to be in plain sight, and then approve. Just one example. Ridiculous. We are preparing to cancel our subscription, a lot of good alternatives out there now who don't seem to hate their users.

title: What is happening here?!
content: I’ve been a user since the YNAB 4 days and have struggled to watch the cost of the app tick higher and higher. It’s hard to recommend the app to folks I know who could really benefit from it because it’s so garsh darned expensive.   There have been UI changes - some that I’ve loved, some that are just fine - but whatever recent one made entering transactions so hinder some…..I wish I could undo it. No longer a toggle for income/expense, have to drill into More Options to access the Cleared toggle…  I’m all for change when it’s needed, but what in the heck is happening at YNAB? Such frequent updates that have led to inefficient and clunky UX.

title: Give us meaningful improvements instead of trivial changes.
content: It would be nice to have meaningful updates instead of trivial changes. I’ve stuck with the product for years, but it seems to no longer give me a reason to stick with it. Look at what your competitors are doing and give us real improvements.

title: Great Budgeting App
content: Long time user of YNAB for zero based budgeting. Love it.  Happy with the continuous improvement, and lately the feature that enables me to share with my children so they can own and manage their own budget in YNAB.

title: Useless, confusing updates pushed out constantly that change the layout and functionality
content: Unfortunately I have to update my YNAB review again. User since 2019, preached the YNAB way to dozens of my friends and used it to get out of debt. This company does not value user feedback, user experience, or its employees. I thought being a beta tester would help shape the direction of the app, but they don’t even send major UI updates to the beta testing pool before shoving them into the official app. In the past 1 year they have pushed several major, confusing updates to the app layout and interface, where each one has changed the location of buttons (right side to left side), the flow of major tasks (opening to a home page instead of the budget), and required more clicks (half of the transaction screen options hidden by a “See More!” tab). Entering a transaction is the backbone of daily use, but has been made more difficult and time consuming. Many changes were obviously flawed in ways that proper beta testing feedback could have prevented (for example, extremely poor color differentiation between future and past transactions), but since user experience isn’t a priority, they ended up rolling back and fixing these issues after they were released to the general user base, causing more updates and layout/color changes that were completely unnecessary. They have not added popular requests such as spending reports that users have requested for over 10 years. There used to be “Four Rules” of the YNAB method, but they quietly removed those and replaced them with gimmicky made-up words such as “spendfulness.” YNAB spent several years building up an online community for users to interact and teach each other, but they just inexplicably fired some of their most popular social media staff and class trainers with 3 hours notice - after sending us an email survey asking how we feel about using AI in our budgets. Apparently there is a new CEO, and I think the shutdown of their main competitor Mint has given them a god complex. All major signs of active ensh*ttification are blinking red, as they destroy all of their community goodwill for the sake of some arbitrary user engagement metrics. It’s the perfect example of the antisocial rot festering within tech companies these days.

title: Change it back!!!
content: I’m really disgusted with the update. I have been a YNAB user for a decade. I really hated giving up my YNAB Classic but stuck with it. This latest version is absolutely trash.

title: UI continues to get worse
content: Every update is worse. More and more clicks. More things hidden. Less intuitive. Ads popping up. Very frustrating as a longtime user to constantly get worse and worse UI updates

title: Price hike HORRIBLE updates
content: They doubled the price - shady shady shady - move to something else.  Constant updates that make the  Product worse.  You have to click a separate screen to CLEAR a transaction.  HORRIBLE RUN AWAY CHOOSE SOMETHING ELSE

title: Mobile app is not great
content: I use the desktop version on YNAB, way simpler and easy to use. The mobile version gets constant updates and seems to just be getting worse.

content: App is going downhill. Lake of reporting and forecasting make this a no go. title: Life changing
content: I worried about money before YNAB all the time. Now I don’t. I just know what I can spend and then I do, unless I change my mind.

title: Can you guys stop messing with the app out of boredom?
content: Like why are we trying to fix something that’s not broken? /: come on

content: I’ve been using YNAB for coming up on a decade, and the system and way of thinking behind it is great. However they’ve been making some crazy decisions lately and the user experience is going downhill fast. I plan to transition to one of the many competitors in the space now

The leadership team has gotten greedy and are sacrificing the customer experience for $. I no longer recommend this budgeting app to others.

title: Cool idea, terrible execution — poor customer service model
content: This financial model this app is trying to go for is a great concept and I really wanted to love it so I could justify paying after the free trial, but I kept having an issue with the balance of my accounts not being accurate even though my accounts were linked. This is a pretty big issue for me because to justify paying for this is because of the supposed “ease” that they can allow when everything is linked and automatically recorded, meaning you can just categorize and look, but that wasn’t happening for me. The issue was a little complicated to a point where their ai customer service assistant couldn’t figure it out and wanted me to email customer service. I asked to call, I felt like I could do it in 5 minutes as a call, whereas it would take hours to days to resolve this issue with written communication. They have no way to schedule a live chat or phone call, solely email… and it took multiple days to receive answers. So, no, I’m not going to pay for this. Also, if the other option is to look through a large amount of long videos that usually don’t answer the specific issue I’m having for the hope that after hours I’ll have an answer is also not a good response to the customer service aspect that this app/company has.

title: Changing just to change
content: Their latest UI updates are garbage. Whoever designed it should be fired because they literally made it take longer and be more inconvenient to use. Genuinely amazing how they manage to ruin a product for no reason.

title: Stop with the changes
content: Product team is bored and keeps making useless changes which complicate the UI for no good reason.

title: Changes
content: Please stop making changes for the sake of making changes. First you took the most useful information(cleared, uncleared, working balance) and hid them behind menus. Now you’ve made it so creating a transaction is so painful I don’t even want to use the app anymore. Now when creating a transaction I can’t easily select inflow or outflow. 1 click has now become 3. Then on to selecting a category. The main source of money(my bank) is now all the way at the bottom. So instead of two quick clicks it’s a click, scroll past all transactions I only use once per month, down to select the thing I use most. Now for the most egregious change, why did you move the cleared and repeats behind the more dropdown. Now photo and memo is in its place, probably the least used option. Now entering a quick transaction that’s cleared is multitudes more clicks more than it should be. Why are yall making changes for the sake of making changes. The new overhaul with main functions spread across multiple redundant screens was already too much, now this nonsense? Yall have a good product, but you’re going to push me to find something better if you don’t think hard about the viability of these changes.

title: Terrible Changes
content: Normally I don’t leave any reviews but with so many UI changes and price increases without adding any additional value over the last year, I felt that I had to leave this as a warning.   Not only did they start introducing pop up ads to promote additional products such as a book despite this being a fully paid annual subscription (and not a cheap one either), but they’ve been making UI changes that complicate the input of transactions instead of simplifying and streamlining.   Instead of adding and improving the analysis tools, they added redundant “spending” and “home” tabs which complicate the app when it used to do just fine without those additional tabs. They’ve added a “goal” tracker which is redundant since every single budget item is technically a “goal”. Actions that should take one or two taps now require multiple taps and drop down menus.   We’ve been users of this software from the one time purchase YNAB 4 days and even continued to use it when it became this annual subscription service because it promised to be the best budgeting software.   What used to be an excellent and straightforward system to track your money based on the envelope budgeting method is slowing becoming a bloated mess that is almost becoming the same as simply using an excel spreadsheet. We really hope that they can right this sinking ship.

title: Another horrible UI update
content: Another update that added more taps to enter transactions. Why is there multiple taps to go from intake to spending? What was wrong with the old enter transaction screen?

title: I’m out

title: Quit ruining your own product
content: I have been using YNAB for over a year now and it has definitely helped a ton. Now with the recent moves the company is making I am starting to look at alternatives. title: Fantastic app!
content: Hands down worth the yearly cost. And every time I think this is already the best budgeting app I’ll find, they make it a little better.

title: Stop frustrating manual-entry users with these updates
content: Response to the ynab response: My goodness, it is not a muscle memory problem. Is that the narrative to justify bad UX upgrades? If the original design of the app had several tap interactions, and a new upgrade introduced less taps, I would be posting a glowing review of how the latest upgrade reduced friction. Please stop infantilizing your users.  Original review: To manually add an entry that is a deposit, I used to just tap on the amount and it would turn green from red. Now I have to make one extra tap to another screen.   The money movement type didn’t factor in the user experience before this change. Now to make a credit card payment, or to make a transfer, I have to go through several screens.   The option to mark the entry as cleared, or to do other tasks, now requires another button to see those options.   I don’t understand the rationale behind frustrating users of this app who still use it in a barebones manner. I don’t care that there is now a cool slider to make money move from checking to credit card. I simply don’t want to log into this app with dread each time there has been a significant update. Please value less taps on the app.   At this point i am willing to pay more a year just so you guys can hire more competent UX designers.

title: Latest Update

title: Garbage changes
content: They keep adding unnecessary taps, for no reason.  No way to revert back to a useful UI.  Avoid this product.  It’s no longer magical.

title: Insanely bad UX changes
content: I’ve been a YNAB user and subscriber for about six years. The YNAB service itself is fine, but I hate the app. The only thing that has really been consistent in all this time is the frequent changes made to the app that completely discombobulate the UX way more often than should happen. Having worked in product management and design myself, I get it, you always want to experiment with improvements and users aren’t going to love every change. What I find frustrating about the YNAB app team’s approach is that they keep making major changes to locations of frequently used functions in the app or completely changing user flows with little to no explanation. I find it hard to believe that these changes are improving anyone’s experience with this app. I feel like every time I sort of get used to the current workflow, they redesign it again. This most recent update has tucked a bunch of frequently used functions, like marking transactions as cleared, behind an extra click inside the transaction summary. It is an infuriating extra step and unnecessary friction. Why would you possibly need to make it harder for people to mark their transactions as cleared? That isn’t a destructive process that needs to be hidden.   I find myself using the app less and less these days and just going back to the website which changes much less often. Maybe that’s the developers’ goal? Who knows. I find it especially frustrating that the experience on the app does not mirror the experience of the UX on the website, and that is probably the biggest sin that these developers have commit committed. As a user, I should be able to seamlessly switch back-and-forth between desktop and Mobile and the UX should be an afterthought. I should not be having to consciously think about and dissect the user flows to re-orient every time I try to use your product. Budgeting is annoying enough as it is, stop trying to reinvent the wheel and just keep the UX consistent. PLEASE.

title: Extremely long time YNAB user
content: I have been around since day one. When YNAB came to mobile I was beyond excited and I loved it for a decade or so.   But now they changed the UI/UX EVERY OTHER WEEK. It’s awful. Years and years of of muscle memory has been continuously undone by adding unnecessary changes just for the sake of making changes. Single clicks are now 5-6 clicks. This becomes extremely old very fast.   I have referred dozens of people to this app both unofficially, and officially. My wife have our finances tied into it together. And I’m at my breaking point.   They either need to make it customizable, or STOP WITH ALL THE CHANGES. I am currently building an automated Excel sheet that replicates YNAB minus imports and I’m very close to switching full time over to it. I pay annually for YNAB because it’s how I learned finances, but now I’m considering leaving it for good because it’s attempting to complicate all the rigid structure it has taught me throughout the years

title: UX Leaves a void for more
content: The June 2026 UI update is poor at best. I don’t need or want all of my accounts linked and so I do a good deal of manual entry. The most recent update ruins the experience for those that put a little bit of manual effort in. There was no testing and no user survey. title: Latest update makes things more complex
content: This is a budgeting app. Why do you have to click more than once to be able to choose if it’s an inflow or outflow? title: Ugh, everything is uglier
content: The new update removes all the colors and makes important things smaller. It keeps getting harder to use. It used to open in your most recently used account (ie checking); now you always have to pick an account. More clicks.

title: User Interface Disaster
content: Every update is adding more clicks and removing workflows I’ve done for years with YNAB’s software.  It’s making me consider moving away from YNAB - and I’m a 13 year customer.

title: Love it but latest update has me nervous…
content: Love this app, our family runs on it and has for a long time now. The latest update makes me a bit nervous as they’ve chosen form over function… the screen where you add a transaction now looks cleaner but if I want to log an inflow I have to click on a drop down menu and select it where before it was always right there. One of my two most common transaction took one tap and now it takes two. Certainly not a dealbreaker, but it makes me wonder what form over function choices will be made in the future… little Choices over time add up. UPDATE January 2026: YNAB is not as sleek or as quick to use as it once was. However, their customer service email staff did respond to my problem quickly and fixed my issue quickly. title: My Favorite App…EVER
content: I honestly can’t tell you how long I’ve been using YNAB, but I could not live without it now. title: Keep Planning!

title: Helping me for years
content: Using this app has helped me manage my money on a regular basis for over 5 years by now. It’s been a crucial tool for major decisions in my life: deciding whether we can afford a car, managing household maintenance costs after we bought a home, student loan paybacks, saving for vacations, and more. It’s like a purpose-built smart spreadsheet for managing the money in your accounts. Using this like picking up journaling habit, but for your finances. It can be life-changing and worth every penny over time. There’s an adjustment period while getting used to tracking regularly. The YNAB method is more manual than other apps out there. But, I prefer that about it because it makes me more proactive about my money as soon as it hits my bank account instead of just tracking it after it’s already been spent. I highly recommend this app if you want to take real control of your finances, pay down debt, and build peace of mind, self-awareness, and empowerment for achieving financial goals. Speaking from experience, the right tool can make a huge difference.

title: Using for years

title: The only budgeting app

My partner and I have different money personalities, and this has helped us have good conversations as well as become more purposeful with our funds and aligned on our goals. He likes to spend money and I don’t. This app has brought harmony to our marriage showing him the advantage of pulling back some and allowing me to see that it is OK to splurge every now and then. There was definitely a learning curve when we first started. The tutorial videos on YouTube are both incredibly helpful and funny! Also, the support chat within the app is fabulous. I hit a few brick walls with frustration and not knowing what was going on and it was wonderful to also have the their team ready and able to quickly log in (with my permission) and help me figure out what was going on when I was too tired to figure it out myself. They both explained it clearly and fixed it for me. Gold stats all around!!

title: Keep coming back to YNAB
content: I am an obsessive budgeted. I was “about to be evicted” broke in my 20s and ever since then I have been obsessed with my personal finances. YNAB would have been really beneficial to 20 year old me but the only smartphone on the market at the time was a the BlackBerry.  This app really is designed for those who are living paycheck to paycheck. For this app to work you have to take an active roll in your personal finances. Might sound tedious but this will keep you on top of your spending.   Now that I am on the downhill slide to 50 my financial situation is much different. I have been on the search for a budgeting app. I like YNABs zero budgeting method. I find the interface easier to learn than other Apps.   My favorite feature is their YNAB together feature. I can invite up to 5 people to use the app.  I settled on YNAB for this reason. I was able to create a budget for my mom and help he maintain it. I’ve recently created budgets for my two stepsons.   There are two things that I find lacking. YNAB only allows you to see your budget as far as your cash on hand will allow. I would like to see what my monthly targets are in the future. I’ve set up targets for just about everything but I can’t see past the months I have funded.   Also, we use our credit cards like debit cards to maximize rewards. It helps reduce financial stress, build discipline, and create a stronger sense of stability. The platform is clear, user-friendly, and empowering for anyone who wants to manage money with purpose. title: 1 Year with YNAB - great budgeting app with solid interface

Now, I’m never worried about bill deadlines or expenses because everything is tracked. Linking the app to credit cards and bank accounts was also simple and intuitive, and the live updating is fantastic. (Note that due to bank processing time, sometimes the app is a day or two behind on transactions, but that’s normal).  Be aware that the app has a bit of a learning curve but YNAB has a ton of guides and information on its website if you get stuck on something. Trust me, it is worth the relatively minimal effort to learn the app. The interface is also beautiful, and there is something very comforting about knowing exactly how much you have available to you at any given time.   All in all, highly recommend.

content: What a phenomenal app. I thought I was fine with money, managing credit cards, and bills, and savings. But using YNAB I now have complete clarity on every single dollar I spend and this has supercharged everything.   The app does have a pretty steep learning curve. I’ve been using it for 6 months and it’s only now I feel like I’ve gotten into a good routine with it. If you’re thinking of quitting during the free trial, highly recommend paying for another month or 2. And the subscription easily pays for itself.   Incredible, incredible tool.

title: Fix your finances

It also triggered shame spirals whenever I failed to log into the app and categorize things. “Fixing” the app would take HOURS.   I do not recommend this app at all and regret the money I spent on it.  I needed to reduce my cognitive load. Not add to it. title: Steep learning curve but amazing

There was a steep conceptual learning curve for me, and it took me a couple of gos at it before it finally ‘clicked’ (how YNAB handles credit card was the most challenging aspect for me to learn). Now that I’ve got the hang of it, though, I can’t imagine ever going back to living without YNAB. What they say is true: you do become a fanboy of YNAB.

title: Best budgeting app
content: This is the best budgeting option out there, hands down. Not just for its budgeting philosophy, but its general ease of use and high reliability. Well worth the monthly fee to use, and would highly recommend it.

title: I love budgeting, now!
content: I used Mint years ago, then kept a cash budget for a while. This is the best of all worlds. This app allows you to do anything: make a budget, split a transaction into multiple categories, cover one category with another if you go over budget in one area, plan for the next month, and keep track of every expense from every bank account and card. I appreciate this tool so much. I am finally able to make and keep goals consistently because it’s so easy. Once you get to know how to use the app, that is. It takes a week or two of just using it, but it really does come easily once you start living life and using the app. It’s so awesome. Tracking every penny was never more fun. I love budgeting now.

title: Too expensive

I did and cancelled it that way, but I still had the entire year $109+ taxes auto drafted out of my account. Not cool, and I need a budget because I’m poor already and barely making it so I CANNOT afford an extra expense when it was not anticipated.

title: Very complex, glitchy

I had several support issues and the support wasn’t very helpful - for example - my bank accounts weren’t pulling in the correct amounts. This app doesn’t allow for forward planning and is very focused in the present

title: Update Fixed

title: I wish I started YEARS ago.
content: I couldn’t love YNAB more. I’m so grateful for what it has done for my husband and I’s mentality around our money, spending, and lifestyle. We were astonished at our spending reflections after a whole year of tracking and budgeting; we anticipate doing even better this year with that knowledge. I love the online website, I love the app, and I love YNAB.

title: Excellent budgeting method, slow UX
content: Update: This apps user experience is going downhill. Since OS 26, the amount of clicks to get things done is a lot more than it used to be. I’m pretty much resorting to using a desktop experience and not my phone. I understand some of this may be Apple’s requirements but if there’s any way to reduce the clicks and add multi-select options to things like assigning and categorizing, that’d be great. Also, I think the targets aren’t working currently.  YNAB’s budgeting method is the envelope method with a unique “ready to assign” addition that makes it one of the best budgeting apps. It’s a learning curve, but helps users to understand what every penny is doing for them.  The app itself is clean, has a light/dark mode option, and a few other options like icon and budget bar display choices. Even though the app looks somewhat basic, clicking longer over a budget unlocks all the detailed features like category activity and targets. You can also add accounts a sync them to your bank. This app is slower at syncing than other budget apps, but I’ve not found that to be an issue since you should be adding transactions manually to keep your accounts as up to date as possible.

title: Long time user
content: I’ve been using YNAB since about 2008. I took a brief break from maybe 2009-2010 (not for technical reasons). I’ve been using it ever since. It’s saved my bacon about being on time and having cash aside for emergencies and unexpected events. It’s very useful, they continue to innovate, so it is worth the cost.

content: I’ve been using YNAB for years. The system itself is great and super helpful for managing your financial life and bringing intentionality to spending. HOWEVER, the annual fee keeps increasing to support automated transaction pulls from 3P accounts. I’d be fine with that if it worked, unfortunately for Fidelity credit cards it’s extremely hit or miss and recently stopped working all together. There is a “status page” they had been posting updates on their progress to resolve, but recently stated “this is a long term issue.. we’re going to stop posting updates about this”.   Basically a “pound sand” message to paying users. I wish they cared more about long term users vs just new user growth. Extremely disappointed

If you have to have an hour long introduction video, that should be an indication that there’s too much going on and it needs to be streamlined. The buttons are not intuitive and I find myself clicking in three or four places before I figure out how to add or rename a new category (I’m Gen Z so that’s saying a lot). The main thing that makes the app unusable is the fact that it NEVER shows the correct amount that is in my account. It takes a long time to reflect desposits/transactions so it will constantly put me in the red or say I have more money than I do. It also gets mixed up with my savings account and when the amount in that account changes, the whole thing gets skewed. I never considered myself spreadsheet savvy but I found a free ynab-inspired spreadsheet online that is easier to use and allows me to enter everything manually, reflecting my remaining balance I have immediately. I find it much easier to use this spreadsheet in tandem with the Google Sheets App than to log things with YNAB. For such an expensive app, I expect a streamlined experience where that can be easily customized. The one thing I like about YNAB vs sheets is that it’s easier to see how much you need to save per month to have a certain amount by a certain date, but if you’re ok with working it out on a calculator and adding it as a note in your spreadsheet then Google Sheets is the jam

title: Great Tool*
content: We’ve been using YNAB for almost four years. It’s been a beneficial platform for helping us give concrete structure to our financial goals and then provide an easy yard stick for measuring how we’re doing. The mobile app makes it easy to fit in the categorization and approval process whenever there’s available time (rather than feeling like budgeting has to be a dreaded weekend morning activity). Some of the improvements to the reflect features in the app also make it easy for us to get answers to questions we have and talk through decisions while we’re in the car together. The auto-import transactions feature is absolutely worth it. Even as people who don’t have that many subscriptions, the app made it easy for us to identify unwanted recurring charges and take action to cancel.  I do have one pet peeve with the app that it would be great to see fixed:  In the transaction pop-up form, the top field above category is always labeled “Payee” but for inflows, it really would be more helpful if the label changed to “Payor.” Based on the web interface’s reflect page, it seems like that’s the intent because it labels the summed values “Income Sources” and has different lines for each.  Other features we’d love to see implemented are:  1) Reimbursement Tracking—when we have an expenditure that is going to be partially or totally reimbursed, it would be great to have a fluid way for tracking that within YNAB. These could be for expenditures that an employer is going to reimburse in full (e.g. airfare, event registration, hotels, meals, etc.) or for situations where one foots the bill for a shared expense: purchasing a gift for parents that other siblings are going to contribute to, or shared accommodations for friends trip. Perhaps this looks like a “to be reimbursed” flag that can checked on in the transaction pop-up. All such flagged items could then be queued in a list for tracking what still needs to be settled up.  2) AI search and sum—for informing future budgeting and even planning, a small chat bot that could take queries like “how much did we spend on food, lodging, rentals, and transportation for that friends trip in the summer of 2023?” which could then semi-reliably aggregate those costs (even if they were associated with different categories/targets and across multiple months).  Thanks to the YNAB team for all the work on a great app!

title: Feedback
content: YNAB is an excellent budgeting app with strong potential. It’s one of the best tools for organizing your money flow, understanding where your money goes, and becoming more mindful of your spending habits. In terms of concept and budgeting philosophy, it’s a five-star product.  However, I’m giving it three stars for two reasons:  1. Bank Integration Issues (Minor Issue) The app doesn’t integrate seamlessly with bank accounts. There are frequent errors and odd glitches. Sometimes the sync works, sometimes it doesn’t, and it’s not reliable enough to trust fully. This inconsistency forced me to enter many transactions manually.  2. No Way to Resolve Monthly Discrepancies (Major Issue) The biggest downside is the lack of flexibility when dealing with small end-of-month discrepancies. After a full month of purchases, returns, transfers, and hundreds of transactions, it’s unrealistic to expect users to hunt for where a $20–$25 difference occurred. If YNAB shows a –$20 balance but my bank clearly has that $20, there’s no simple way to correct it. The app doesn’t let you manually reconcile and reset the balance to actual balance so you can start the next month clean. Because of this, I eventually stopped using the app.  Great concept, strong budgeting philosophy, but the missing reconciliation flexibility is a deal-breaker.

title: Pretty average
content: Overall this is an excellent budgeting tool, but there are a few areas that are not good.   Credit card support is poor, as you can’t just assign money to the account for payments. It’s easier to just not link them and make a payment category instead.  Bank support for Chime is poor just like every other budgeting app. They reduce pending payments from the account balance, but that is already factored in, so you end up with a temporary double reduction per transaction, which can lead to inaccurate allocations.  Investing account support is poor. It only shows my paper trading account, not my actual investing account, resulting in an inflated and inaccurate net worth.  Transaction auto-mapping is poor. If you routinely spend in various categories from the same store, it auto-assigns the wrong category. Those instances should ideally start as uncategorized, or it can accidentally result in misallocation.  Hidden due dates after funding a target is a hindrance to planning. I need to know when to move money into what account, as I manage multiple bank accounts. The result is this app being non-functional if you work with multiple bank accounts. It’s geared for a single account. It could be better by assigning which targets come out of certain accounts.  I’m removing two stars for these failures.  Update: Taking another two stars off. Transactions aren’t always showing up, imaginary transactions that didn’t happen and don’t exist are showing up, and general unreliable importing is making this fundamentally useless.  Overassigned categories, even by accident, become permanently screwed after correction. You have to delete them and create new ones to get correct targets.

title: Great, but…
content: YNAB has been a GAME CHANGER when it comes to managing my finances. As somewhat of a budgeting nerd, there’s nothing like it. I started budgeting with pen and paper, switched to spreadsheets, tried a few apps, and then started using YNAB which I’ve used for 15 years.  It makes saving for different things extremely easy with “categories” without needing a bunch of different accounts or to transfer money around. With YNAB I’ve gone from 18+ bank accounts down to 2, making my finances so much easier to manage. With YNAB, I’ve also been able to use credit cards wisely without going into a single penny of debt for the first time in my life, which has allowed me to earn points and travel more, improving my quality of life. YNAB makes it easy to track my investments, and I love the ease of reading their graphs and watching my net worth grow. I love the ability to customize things like which categories I view on the “home” tab when the app opens, so that I can have my most used categories right there and I don’t need to view all of my categories, which also helps me with saving because out of sight, out of mine.   Now for the “but…” part:  YNAB has been doing a lot of changes to the app over the past year or so, some are great, some you just deal with even though you like the old way better, and some make using the app more complicated than it needs to be- one of which is the new “spending” tab where you can see all of your transactions individually. The view of transactions is now a lot to take in with EVERY transaction as the default, and to view only uncleared or reconciled takes a bit more extra button pushing; as do many of their latest updates. As someone who is neurodiverse, making something go from pushing 2 buttons, to 3 or 4 may not seem like a big deal but when those changes multiply across many tasks, it makes it unappealing.   Overall, YNAB is the only thing I’ve found that helps me successfully managing money, pay off debt, and reach my financial goals.

title: Used to be 5 stars
content: maybe a year or two ago I positively reviewed this app but sadly I need to revise my opinion. There is still so much good that this app does for our family. It taught us how to manage our credit cards and avoid unnecessary or unmanageable debt. Our savings and investments have increased, and our expenses have gone down. I do feel a better sense of control over our finances. But there are areas for improvement. First of all, I still wish that I could create sub categories. right now you have category groups and categories, but I need at least one more tier. My workaround is to create additional categories that function as   Headers Secondly, I still never enter transactions manually for linked accounts because it always creates duplicates when the imported transaction does not match up to the manual transaction which I then have to tediously search  for because my accounts don’t reconcile Thirdly, I would love to access the same income verse expense report on the reflect tab of the app that is available on the website I want to emphasize that I have watched every single video I could find on YouTube and through the app itself start to finish, and these issues are unresolved. I’ve even gone through the written material. I saw all the negative reviews from other users about the last update and although I don’t like the home tab, I did appreciate where it clearly showed me money that I have assigned to future months But as of today 10/3/25, I am super frustrated with the platform. I rely on this app and use it every single day, but it has never been particularly user-friendly and now it’s creating problems The other day I entered a transaction for an unlinked credit card and when I assigned money to cover the expense five dollars kept disappearing I spent so much time trying to figure out what was happening in so many different ways and finally all I could do was delete it and create a reconciliation balance adjustment instead, which I don’t like to do because then it doesn’t come up in my spending report as an expense for the category Two days ago, I transferred money from my checking account to a savings account at a different bank and today that transaction imported twice for some reason and the second transaction got assigned to one of my credit cards presumably because it’s also a synchrony product. I had to check all my accounts to make sure that it wasn’t actually duplicated in real life and that there were no transactions to that credit card then I deleted the duplicate transaction Lastly, I don’t know whether it’s because I’m having to jump between screens more than I used to have to do, but I am finding that when I try to cover overspending that it’s not going where I intended. It’s a little hard to explain because I don’t really understand what’s happening, but what I do know is that I feel constantly confused and frustrated and I’m tired of having to work backwards and undo things that should not have happened in the first place. it really defeats the purpose of the app entirely and if I’m gonna go about it in this way, then I might as well go back to spreadsheets, which are free. I don’t want to do that, and my fingers are crossed that the developers are paying attention to our feedback.

title: So Close To Being Really Good
content: I really wanted to use Copilot and tried to make it work, but there were too many little annoyances that finally made me give up.   One of them was having to manually create two transactions for things like my car payment. For whatever reason, Plaid couldn’t connect to my car loan account, so I had to manually add it. The rigamarole of having to create manual transactions to debit the money from my checking and the create another transaction to my car loan account to show the payment was time consuming, frustrating, and quite frankly unnecessary. Being able to transfer money from a payment account to a loan account should be one transaction.  I had three loan accounts I would have to do this for.   I also found the iPad version of Copilot slow, sometimes unresponsive, unintuitive, and quite inferior to the iPhone app.  Things in the iPad app did not work the same and were missing features. For example, when entering a manual internal transfer, the “incoming” or “outgoing” selector buttons were not available. Sometimes clicking on a field would bring up a numeric keypad while other times in would bring up a full keyboard.   Finally, Copilot relies heavily on Plaid for connecting to banks. Unfortunately, this system was much less reliable than what I found in other finance apps.   I would be willing to give Copilot another shot once they are able to update the iPad app and fix a lot of these issues.

title: Great Potential, Puzzling Deficiencies
content: I run a sole proprietorship. For what I need, Copilot Money does mostly a great job. It lacks some functions, however, that I feel should be standard on any financial app.   For instance, there is no way to export the results of a filtered search, INCLUDING BY DATE. If I want to see how much I’ve spent in a specific category YTD, there is no way to do that natively in CM. I have to export ALL my transactions, dating back to when I first started using the app, to a spreadsheet, then filter my searches there. This is particularly vexing at tax time.   Other, less-pressing problems (for me) have to do with look-and-feel issues, and so are completely subjective.  Navigating to text fields within the app has never felt intuitive.   Year-end summary does not allow me to page to whichever category I want to see - I can only move forward-back one page at a time in the order Copilot has arranged for me. If you’re going to include a “feature,” fine, but design it in a way that anticipates users wanting to do more with it than just passively follow the directions onscreen.  There was an issue with my PayPal account needing to be re-synced daily. This seems to have been fixed recently, but other accounts also lose sync occasionally.  Again, for the price, this app is a solid choice for tracking and organizing finances. But it could be so much more if the designers made up their minds to do a better job of meeting the needs and expectations of their users.

title: Clean design, easy to use, powerful
content: Indispensable. This is one of my top 3 apps. I’ve never budgeted before but Copilot makes it easy. I finally have complete visibility into my finances in a way that Mint or others could never provide. Support is also fantastic.

title: Great app but…
content: When adding recurring bills, can we get an option to upload a screenshot and have it read the details and generate the recurring bills?   Peace and love!

title: Missing credit card rewards management
content: Would be ideal to see credit card rewards management in this app since they already have all my banking details

title: Relies too much on Plaid services
content: Started a yearly subscription in the beginning of 2026. Halfway through, my accounts stopped syncing and ruined all the tracking of my investments, categories, and cash flow. And they blamed it on Plaid, the company they used to track your accounts. Shouldn’t build an app that relies heavily on another company that they can’t control. Tried to get a refund, but still haven’t heard anything. Hoping this review gets to them. 👎

title: Feels Like A Community - Don't Stop
content: Despite its hiccups, bumps and tools-still-in-development, Copilot is a smart, fresh, human-customer-centered little powerhouse well worth its weight in $ubscription .  I just pray that Copilot stays creative, a little scrappy & Customer focused for many years.  I just don't want it to go the way of NerdWallet, Facebook, Zaadz, Gaiam, OKCupid, Twitter, Tumblr... among so many others- companies that started off as similarly creative, conscientious, service & people-centered startups but were bought & sold out to mega-corps & holding companies.  Which turned them into yesterday's news, addiction psychologized, formulaic cash cows that were milked dry into broken senescence, and remain only in name as tragic zombies of their former selves.

title: Best Budgeting App in the World
content: This is the #1 app to manage your finances, budgets, bills, etc. I’m someone that is very meticulous with finances but also try to optimize at every corner. I have multiple credit cards and multiple other financial accounts. I also do a lot personal cash flow planning and projections. Without this app, managing all that be a full-time job on its own. But with this app, it’s super easy (and weirdly fun!). What I like best is that everything is super intuitive and has the easiest interface. Not to mention they also have integrations directly into the accounts you would need. No manual efforts in importing or tracking individual transactions. The folks at this company continue to improve the app with features that you didn’t even know you needed! I’m really impressed by the copilot team and the app they have created. I’ve been using it for 3 years and I can’t imagine living without it!

title: Way better than Microsoft’s Copilot
content: Way better than Microsoft’s Copilot

title: the best budgeting app out there
content: i love copliot! i have been using it for 5  years and it's changed how i think about my spending, tbh. i used to avoid my bank account apps entirely and now i actually enjoy looking @ my account. no more avoiding, lol!

content: Great, now I can’t blame the software when I’m over budget

title: Not intuitive

title: Essential For Life

title: Love it

title: Pretty App, Slow Updates
content: It's a truly beautiful app, but they take forever to release bug fixes and new features.  The Goals feature does not work. content: By all means download this app if you enjoy sync errors, debits marked as credits, incompatible accounts, and missing transactions.  I spend more time making corrections than I do analyzing my finances.

title: Used to be good, WOULD NOT RECOMMEND NOW
content: I’ve been a Simplifi user for years now, ever since they shut down mint. The app had been working okay for the most part, however, in the last few months it’s gotten worse and worse. Nothing is categorized correctly, even after I manually update the category multiple times. The rules are completely broken, and nothing gets split or categorized correctly. Honestly, this app is a hollow crappier version of its former self. I’m actively migrating to something else, and I advise everyone else to do the same. This had the potential to be good, but given the numerous price hikes, I wouldn’t recommend this to anyone. Garbage.

title: Needs usability testing.
content: This could be a really great app but falls apart on usability for most of the little things.

title: New user to Q
content: I always thought I had decent financial literacy. After putting in all my financial information and letting Q crunch it all together, I realized how much I didn’t know! My financial literacy has shot up with the powerful tool of Q. If you’re serious about managing your finances, use Q. The cost of this product has already paid for itself many times over for me.

title: Buggy
content: App is very buggy.

title: Great Web based Financial Product
content: I love the comprehensive subjects that are recorded, downloaded and/or reported on. It truly is a time saver and reference point to analyze & document personal, Contractual and Self-Employed finances.  If I may add a "wish feature" or 2, it would be: 1. Add Horizontal scroll bars along with the current Vertical scroll bars. 2. Add an "instant back" link to my previous page. Currently, I must use menus to navigate back to my previous page.

title: Poor replacement for Mint
content: When Mint shut down I was forced to look elsewhere for a budget tracking app. Quicken Simplifi is begrudgingly what I opted to use based on other reviews and it has been an incredibly frustrating experience. I am constantly having to correct how it categorizes purchases, it doesn’t seem to automatically categorize at all based on words in the purchase or even based on the merchants that I’ve made purchases with previously. Frequently I’m having to direct recurring bills or payments to the ones I’ve asked it to track. The process of having to set up my accounts and budgets all over again in another app is the only thing keeping me on this one. Please, developers, DO BETTER TO IMPROVE YOUR PRODUCT.

title: Not good
content: Was working alright but randomly would stop working and i would need to reset all my recurring bills etc. then suddenly stopped connecting to my bank account and wouldnt reconnect so im left with the wrong info and no way to fix it.

title: Biggest pain to cancel
content: Do not get if you’re not sure, to delete your data you have to fill forms, call customer support, and jump through sooo many hoops just to delete your account. DO NOT recommend at all.

title: Not bad - meets my need
content: I’m a long time Quicken user, since it was on a 5.25 floppy disk (LOL). I stopped using it about 15 years ago due to lack of parity on Mac with Windows version. About 5 years ago, I started using it again but was disillusioned by how clumsy it was on Mac and how often it lost my data whenever an update arrived. I started to revert to my old way of tracking on spreadsheets and was fumbling along looking at alternatives when an offer to use Simplifi came up. I thought I’d give it a fair shot and did - after about 2 weeks of using it, it meets my needs. It’s not fantastic but I have one tool to look at all my accounts at the same time. Thats actually quite helpful.

title: Decent until recently
content: Very long time Quicken user. Simplifi was decent until recently. I lost my connection to Venmo last year and have never been able to reconnect. It’s been 9 days, and is a much bigger deal since i do most banking through Robinhood. I have seen multiple people posting online having same issue. Wish Quicken would take a more serious response to the issue, like sending an email addressing the problem. Quicken assist, the automated assistant is no help. Disabled accounts and tried numerous times to reconnect, but keep getting the same error… FDP -101.

title: Accounts Lose Connectivity by the Day
content: Quicken Simplifi has been a huge disappointment. I have multiple high-usage accounts that have lost connectivity, and there does not appear to be any real resolution in sight. On top of that, manual accounts are calculated incorrectly, which makes the app unreliable for tracking my finances. For something that requires an annual subscription, the service is abysmal and nowhere close to acceptable. I expected a paid product to be stable and responsive, but this has been frustrating and unusable.

title: Not consistent or easy
content: Don’t believe the other reviews. This program is glitchy at best and problematic at worst.  Doesn’t maintain connections to accounts - constantly having to reconnect. Way too expensive for the countless issues and lack of truly valuable information. Does not recognize payments made and shows late payments.  Terrible. Really.

title: DO NOT BUY
content: After uploading five months of transactions into Quicken Simplifi, Budget, I discovered that there are no memo fields to identify transactions within the software. For instance, PayPal transactions come through as PayPal transaction. But gives you no hint in Simplifi what the transaction was for. And there is no editable field to indicate the vendor. Also, the reports are very limited in Simplifi, and you cannot print out category lists or account lists. I also just found out that there is no way to transfer transactions from simplify into quicken classic deluxe so I will have to start from scratch in order to get memo fields. I am not happy!

content: Great if you don’t mind reclassifying transactions every couple months. Not sure how it has 4 stars. I have used it for more than 2 years (since intuit killed mint). I am ready to try something new.

title: Limited for Detailed Budgeters
content: Mostly this program is fine for what most people need. However, there are a few functions that highly-detailed users might need. One, I’d like to track my credit cards based on the size and due dates of the statement; this does not always match the month that charges are made, and it’s the paying of the card that actually affects bank balances. I’d also like to see my Planned Spending as unspent money, similar to how the former Mint app allowed you to see what was left in your budget. I am docking a star because the auto-classification of charges has been getting progressively worse for months. The fast food chain ‘Cava’ gets tagged as a bar. title: Not a safe place for your money.
content: The lack of basic security controls in this app is surprising.  Simplifi does not require login or biometric authentication to open the app and stays permanently logged in. Anyone with access to your unlocked device can see your entire financial picture.  This may be acceptable years ago, but not today. Most financial apps provide: • Face ID / biometric lock • Session timeouts • Re-authentication options  Relying solely on device security is not sufficient for an app that aggregates sensitive financial data.  Until this is addressed, I cannot fully trust the app with my financial inform

title: Ruined a great product
content: Incompetence and greed have ruined a good company and product.

title: Needs Additional Reports

After downloading the app and subscribing to the service I immediately realized that Simplifi lacks in many areas what Quicken Classic does have. I find the app very disappointing and will most likely figure out another option at the end of my subscription.

title: Nice Tool

When splitting a transaction, you don’t get to put a description for each line item. I quite often like to put in the description of what I was buying and only being able to do that for the summary amount is just not helpful to me.

title: Getting better maybe
content: Frequently need to reconnect to my accounts. Constantly fails to sync all data. Will be moving to a more reliable app.   Update:  Giving Quicken another chance. Took some time and effort, but I think I have resolved my issues.

title: App has some bugs to work through
content: I have noticed that this app hasn’t held up its promise to its customers.  I got this app and the subscription because I wanted to move away from having to manually enter transactions daily.  So far I have needed to return almost daily to edit the messed up and misplaced transactions. Not that big of a deal I guess until I do have to manually enter transactions and the $ amount displayed not changing. Reached out to a live agent who gave me many steps to do, as I was doing them and updating her she ended the chat after 2 minutes of no response as I was trying to get through multiple steps to solve the problem and after having told her that it was taking me a second. title: Does everything

Nice retirement planner. Net Worth dashboard widget. Split transactions. “Watch” buckets. Tells me how much I have to spend for the month after subtracting all bills, predicted income and planned spending buckets.  Highly recommend

title: Good Financial Tool
content: Everyone should have a budget and watch their finances.  This is a great tool for that.

title: Doesn’t Give True Financial Picture
content: The spending plan feature includes a pseudo envelop like system and a “left to spend” surplus bucket. The problem is the “left to spend” doesn’t include any overages in the envelopes. It could mislead you into thinking you have more left to spend than you actually do. The envelopes’ balanced rollover each month, but there isn’t a clean feature to allow you to replenish them from your surplus, which feeds into the notion that your left to spend is not real. Also, if you receive one-off cash from a bonus or commission, it will reduce your left to spend for that month only. If you don’t deploy it immediately that month, it does not carry forward. So the spending plan feature makes it look like you lost it. Bottom line, it’s not really helpful for true financial cash flow management.

title: Almost doubled the price on us
content: It’s a decent app - nothing special. Lots of issues with connections to various banks/ accounts/ etc.   But it gets the job done.   Now they significantly raised prices out of the blue. They know we have our data and budgets and investment history here and it would be tough to move.   If I were choosing a finance / budgeting app again today I’d find another option.

title: Poor Policy and Customer Service
content: I was using the personal annual subscription with one account, and then started using the Personal and Business subscription under a new account to get the discount. Shortly into it, I canceled my subscription to the original account. Well, I just had the original unused account auto-renew. Apparently the cancelation didn’t stick. I did this all sometime earlier last year.  I just attempted to chat with a “Coach Kevin” to get a refund for it, and they said it is not something they can do—even though it’s obviously an unused account and I proved the email to my current Personal and Business account so they can check that I’m honest.  Hopefully this review hurts their bottom line enough to revise policies and enable better service.  Their response was: “…sadly we are not able to process the refund as this one is out of the 30 Days Guarantee we offer for the subscriptions for more than 7 Months, so what i can offer to you is to cancel the subscription so once this one ends we will not charge you any more and this one can expire.”

title: Love this app!
content: I use it every day. Although I wish I could have widgets that could show how much per category I have to spend vs overall spending.

title: Never updates
content: This app looks fantastic. The user interface is clean, modern, and very intuitive—honestly one of the better-designed budget apps I’ve used. Navigating categories, viewing spending trends, and setting budgets all feel smooth and well thought out.  Unfortunately, the core function of a budgeting app—accurate, up-to-date bank information—is where it completely falls apart. My linked accounts frequently failed to update, transactions lagged by days (sometimes never syncing at all), and balances were often incorrect. I spent more time manually checking my bank than trusting the app, which defeats the entire purpose.

title: Frequent connection issues

No flashy UI helps when connections with major/popular banking institutions like Venmo, Merryl, Fidelity keep breaking and take several weeks to fix. They have just a couple (excellent) support personnel in their user community, who are clearly under-supported and over-worked. The Simplifi tech team really needs to get their act together.

title: Love it
content: Love seeing at a glance my portfolio balance on my phone. Some days fun, many days not so much but in for the long haul!

title: Quicken versus Rocket
content: Still not what I hoped for. I switched to Simplifi frustrated with Rocket having duplicated transactions and the difficulty of editing categories. I’m used to being in control, sorting by spreadsheets, and having my own budget in Excel, where I can also calculate things.  Simplifi allows me to edit categories, which is great. It has, however, not “learned” categories very well as of yet. Rocket asks when you change a category if you want it on future transactions. In Simplifi you have to dig into the menu to set a rule.  Quicken does not seem to allow for easy updates to manual asset entry. You have to set up some sort of transaction rather than just simply editing the balance. I’m not trying to create auditable records, I’m just trying to track income, expense, and asset values. If I remodel my house, and it’s worth more, I should be able to simply change its value.  I’ve not yet been patient enough to try and set up a budget in Simplifi. It’s just too hard, when Excel is so easy. I think these softwares “overthink” things trying to be easier to use. I’d love a software that has the advantages of downloading all my transactions, but also lets me simply define categories, and then asks “How much do you want to spend in this category this next year? Based on last year, you spent $Xxxx.”  I have one account that is two factor authentication that needs to be reconnected every time I open Simplifi. That’s frustrating.   And one morning I woke up to all my manual asset opening balances duplicated. title: Cash transactions
content: The app is very helpful overall, but one major limitation affects real-world use: cash transactions cannot be closed automatically within a series unless they’re linked to a digital payment.  In many everyday situations, cash is still the only acceptable form of payment. For example, I hire a lawn-mowing service in the summer and a snow-shoveling service in the winter. Both providers only accept cash, which is very common for seasonal or independent workers. Because the app forces every transaction to be tied to a digital payment, there’s currently no way to close these entries properly unless I link them to something that doesn’t exist.  Not all transactions in the world will be cashless, and the system shouldn’t assume they are. It would be extremely helpful if the app could allow cash-based entries to be created, recorded, and closed automatically as part of a series without requiring a linked digital payment.  This change would better reflect real-life financial scenarios and make the app much more flexible for users who work with both digital and cash payments.

content: I signed up for Albert hoping it would help with my financial needs, but canceling the service turned out to be an incredibly frustrating and unnecessarily difficult process. They bombard you with multiple questions and verification steps, including requiring your full Social Security Number and the last four digits of your debit card. I had to completely exit out of the cancellation flow multiple times just to go dig up my card details. On top of that, the debit card verification process takes a long time, so by the time everything finally goes through, the original issue you were trying to resolve has either passed or gotten worse, leaving you in an even deeper situation. This level of friction feels intentional and really leaves a bad taste.   I wouldn’t recommend Albert if you’re looking for something simple and customer-friendly. Very disappointed with the cancellation experience.

title: Intentionally Difficult Cancellation…
content: They don’t accept Discover Debit cards unfortunately. So after having been a long time user I needed to cancel by subscription. However, to do this you need to drain your savings account and regular checking account in the app. This requires you to transfer funds out of your accounts as a condition of cancelling. Not only this but it feels like they intentionally move the “continue” button in each other screen toward cancelling this meant I accidentally closed the form a few times. From a UI perspective it’s clear they’re trying to confuse you so you give up on the cancellation…asking for information that requires you towards the end to exit the form you’re in. This means you need to restart. ALSO, you have to wait for the funds to move out of the account so actually cancelling your subscription can take longer than a week. This is an FTC violation and I did file a formal complaint out of sheer spite for the process. Left me with a bad taste in my mouth, it felt intentionally misleading.

title: A fun scavenger hunt!
content: I downloaded this app to track my money. Unfortunately, it appears the app has adopted a more philosophical approach to finance, focusing less on where my money currently is and more on where it was 1–5 business days ago. This however, was quite exciting because every login felt like opening a mystery box. Had I spent too much? Was I secretly rich? The app wasn’t saying.  The real adventure began when I made the mistake of using the savings feature. I naively assumed that if I ever wanted to leave, I could simply cancel my subscription and withdraw my money. Instead, I discovered a delightful scavenger hunt in which I was required to move funds, close accounts, complete various administrative tasks, and repeatedly revisit the app before I was finally permitted to stop paying for it.  For those keeping score at home, the process took approximately four weeks, six separate visits to the app, and 37 f words before cancellation was possible.  There is nothing this app provides that cannot be found elsewhere for free- What it does provide, however, is a unique opportunity to experience the emotional journey of trying to leave a timeshare.  For those looking for a secondary bank account tracking service, do not use this app. If, however, you’re looking for a remora fish that quietly attaches itself to you and slowly siphons $19.99 a month while providing little to no actual value, I cannot recommend this app enough.
