title: Not Ready for Users that Won’t Rely on Faith
content: Origin has quietly removed the fundamentals of financial software — budgets, income confirmation, assumption review — and replaced them with a one-way, opaque “AI-first” interface. There is no way to see how your income is classified, how expenses are normalized, or what the system is uncertain about. There is also no real back-and-forth with the AI to correct errors.  The result is blind trust. You’re shown confident-looking outputs without any audit trail, which is unacceptable in a financial app. Anyone with irregular income, retirement cash flow, insurance, taxes, or medical expenses will find the system making silent assumptions with no way to validate them.  The recent $1 annual subscription price is the tell — this feels less like a production-ready product and more like users are being subsidized to train a model while the UX and documentation are unfinished. AI can be useful, but replacing transparency and controls with faith is not progress.  Until Origin provides visible assumptions, confirmation loops, and basic financial controls, it’s hard to recommend this to anyone outside a narrow, young, salaried demographic.

title: Great budgeting tool
content: I’ve tried a lot of budgeting apps over the years, and most of them fall into one of two extremes: either they’re glorified spreadsheets, or they’re so automated that you stop engaging with your money altogether. Origin feels different in the best way.  What I love most is how intentional the app feels. It’s not just about tracking where your money went, but about helping you decide where you actually want it to go. The categories are flexible, the interface is clean and calm (not anxiety-inducing), and it works especially well for couples trying to build shared habits without constant friction.  I also appreciate that Origin doesn’t shame you for spending. There’s no red-alert guilt when you eat out or go over in a category. Instead, it encourages awareness and adjustment, which honestly makes me more consistent long-term.  The onboarding is thoughtful, syncing accounts is straightforward, and the design makes you want to check in regularly rather than avoid it. It feels like a tool built for real life, not just perfect spreadsheets.  If you’re looking for a budgeting app that balances structure with grace, and clarity with flexibility, Origin is easily the best one I’ve used.

However, like many other personal finance apps that don’t really meet customers” needs, it fails to give you the tools to plan/project  your spending and cash flow in the short term, i.e. weeks to months. The app shows your upcoming transactions but only shows daily totals for two weeks at a time- no impact on cash flow. Meanwhile, a lot of us shopping around for personal finance apps are trying to answer the question “based on my planned future bills, transactions and expected income, how can I adjust my monthly outgoing transfers to savings to keep my checking account balance positive?”. Another important thing I don’t like about the app is that it’s always locked in landscape view on an iPad!!! I really don’t like being forced to using apps in landscape mode, not everyone uses landscape mode all the time. I don’t understand why developers continue to do this, if it’s because of space then give users the option of moving the sidebar away in portrait mode.

title: Better Than Monarch?
content: I’ve been through the personal finance carousel: YNAB first, then nearly two years on Monarch, a brief stop at Copilot, and now I’ve landed on Origin. After using all of them long enough to see the cracks, the shine, and the real differences, here’s the bottom line: Origin is the most ambitious product in the space right now, but it’s not perfect.  Functionally, Origin and Monarch share most of the same foundational features. You can link every account imaginable, track your net worth across cash, stocks (however I was not able to link my public brokerage in Monarch), crypto, real estate. Both give you clean analytics and enough charts to make you feel productive. Where Origin starts to separate itself is scope. It lets you invest directly in the app and even set up an estate plan or trust. Monarch doesn’t touch this territory. Origin clearly wants to be the full stack of your financial life, not just a budgeting tool. Like myself, I’m not sure if most people will switch their brokerage. But in an ideal world it would be nice to have everything all on one platform.  The real story, though, is AI. Most companies are going to bolt AI onto their product like a hood ornament and call it innovation. Origin actually built around it. The AI is connected to all your data, and because of that, it gives advice that isn’t generic. I’ve run some of the recommendations by friends who work in personal finance, and the accuracy is surprisingly strong. The daily market updates and long-term forecasting tools are genuinely useful, and something I’m finding myself going back to. Could it be even more tailored to your specific investing philosophy? Absolutely. But Origin is miles ahead of the competition here, and they shipped something that doesn’t feel rushed even though they clearly rushed to be first.  Design-wise, Origin feels modern and premium, while Monarch is clean but a bit more traditional. My only gripe is that some of Origin’s most-used features feel buried under extra menus. It’s hard to tell whether that’s because the layout itself is less intuitive or because I’m simply conditioned from years of using Monarch, but either way, it slows you down. If Origin lets users customize their dashboard or pull high-use items to the surface, that friction could go away.  Now for the part they need to fix. Origin doesn’t let you change or remove their built-in categories (at least I wasn’t able to). Once you add your own custom categories, the list becomes long and disorganized. Categorizing transactions takes more time than it should, and Monarch handles this far better. Editing, hiding, and reordering categories shouldn’t be optional in a premium finance app—it should be table stakes.  And here’s one more thing I wish Origin offered: a budgeting mode similar to YNAB. I have variable income, and budgeting based on money I actually have, not money I expect to receive, is simply more realistic. YNAB’s “assign every dollar” approach shines for people who don’t have predictable paychecks. If Origin added an optional YNAB-style budgeting method, it would solve one of the biggest blind spots in their otherwise comprehensive platform.  Final take: Origin feels like the future. Monarch is steady and familiar; Origin is where the industry is heading. If they clean up categories and introduce a YNAB-style budgeting option, they’ll be the dominant player in this space. As it stands, it’s still the strongest overall option if you want automation, modern design, and legitimately useful AI instead of marketing fluff.

title: Try Origin today!!!!
content: In my 20s, I treated money as a way to get what I wanted and enjoy life freely. Now, in my 30s, I’ve realized it’s time to get serious about my finances. I needed to finally look at where my money was going, track my net worth, and figure out how much I need to retire. For a long time, I was afraid to even open my bank accounts. The anxiety and panic were real.  I’d heard countless financial experts say I needed a budget, but no matter how hard I tried, I couldn’t make one that worked. Budgets are living things that change every month, and that alone felt overwhelming. On top of that, I had recurring charges across multiple accounts, which made things even harder to manage.  Then I saw an ad on Instagram for Origin to try it for $1 for an entire year. I couldn’t pass that up. From the moment I started using it, I was hooked. The interface is clean, intuitive, and beautifully designed. Once I linked my accounts, Origin automatically categorized my transactions, which saved me so much time. I added a few custom categories, but I love that it comes with solid defaults.  The suggested budget feature blew me away. The app analyzes your spending and creates a realistic budget that actually makes sense. No more guesswork or spreadsheets. The only small issue I’ve noticed is that I can’t change a transaction’s category while it’s still pending. It’s minor, but I do hope the developers fix it soon.  My favorite feature by far is Recurring Charges. Being able to see upcoming payments helps me prepare for the week ahead and avoid surprises. The AI assistant is another highlight. It summarizes my portfolio weekly and even answers personal finance questions with helpful insights and tools.  Overall, I’m thrilled I gave Origin a try. It has completely changed how I feel about money management. I actually enjoy tracking my finances now, and my husband uses it too. I can’t imagine managing my finances without it.  If you’ve ever struggled to budget or felt overwhelmed by your money, I highly recommend Origin. It makes financial clarity not just possible but enjoyable.

I would gladly pay $100/year for a product that lets me aggregate all my bank accounts, credit cards and investment accounts, and provides the full suite of financial planning tools that Empower offers. I’d say that Origin does very well with respect to the first part (aggregation), but fairly poorly with respect to the financial planning aspect.   For example, there’s no way to categorize investment accounts by taxable status (eg taxable, pre tax or post tax). This doesn’t seem to be taken into account with respect to forecasting. The forecasting tool is bare bones and the methodology appears very incomplete with the assumption of a fixed rate of return for all accounts rather than one based on underlying investments. A lot of investment holdings get incorrectly classified as “mixed” although they’re not, and even mixed funds and ETFs should classify according to their underlying holdings. Etc.   I’m hopeful that these investment and planning tools will greatly improve over the next year, but at present I can’t yet recommend Origin as a replacement for Empower.

title: TLDR - There are way better options, like Monarch.
content: When Mint went EOL, I, like many others, migrated to PocketGuard. I find budgeting very difficult and Mint worked extremely well for me. I read that PocketGuard was the most similar, and they have released updates that made it more similar.   UNFORTUNATELY, PocketGuard has several fundamental flaws that make it so irritating to use that I stopped using it entirely and my finances suffered as a result. I’ll start with the good.  The good: you can set budgets and roll them over into the next month. This rollover feature was not an offering when I started using it, somehow. You can also now set rules to categorize transactions automatically which was not the case when I started using it; I initially had to recategorize every individual transaction if PocketGuard thought it belonged in a different budget. (This is still the case if the payment issuer name changes but I can’t really fault them for that.)  The bad: one of pocketguard’s selling points is its bill tracking feature. Unfortunately, this feature is actually a drawback, as whenever PocketGuard says something is a bill, it breaks it out from your budget entirely and does not let you set a monthly budget for it. This is fine for rent, but it is utterly broken for things like quarterly water bills, when the app says “scheduled for [month]” and does not count a portion of that quarterly or yearly bill towards your monthly budget. Instead, when you hit that month, suddenly you’re completely over budget because your entire quarterly water bill or annual Strava subscription or property tax is counted towards that month alone. Many times I tried to figure out a way to make this feature work for me, but it just does not. It is also a pain for the purpose of tracking things like streaming subscriptions, because even if you set an entertainment budget and categorize Spotify as entertainment, the app then DOUBLE COUNTS that recurring payment as a) a bill and b) part of your set entertainment budget. It also does not automatically deduct recurring payments such as these from your budget so that you can easily see the actual amount you have free to spend. Most of these issues have been immediately fixed for me by moving to Monarch instead. I only wish I had done so before my annual PocketGuard subscription had pinged.

title: Useful for month-to-month budgeting, but not much else
content: I switched to PocketGuard after Mint closed down, and had high hopes for the app. Indeed their basic month-to-month budgeting tools function well, can be automated to a decent extent, and provide useful insights about where you are in the month. The two issues that have caused me to stop using the app are as follows:   1) While their institutional syncing works well on the whole, if you do have an issue it puts all of your past transactions - all the work you did to categorize and name them - in jeopardy. For example, when my credit card number was switched due to fraud, it created a duplicate account and the “old” account lost all of its categorizing and naming data which I had worked on over the months. This happened again with a separate syncing problem. Which leads to my second issue…   2) The retrospective analytics are not very robust to begin with - you cannot “slice and dice” your data to the extent you could with Mint or other services - but that becomes a moot point when your data is often being reset in the first place. For myself, half the point of using an app like this is to have analytics to look back on, discover trends, and answer specific questions (eg how much did I spend on rent back in 2022?). Without great analytics to begin with, and without faith that my data would be preserved over time, the app only becomes useful for month-to-month, in the moment budgeting. Which, as I mentioned above, it does excel at to a fair degree.

title: Looking for a new budgeting app
content: I paid for premium and once my subscription period is over I think I’ll be cancelling this. I was looking for an app that could replace Mint and PocketGuard hasn’t held up for me.   Pros:  - You can create your own categories of spending budgets - You can rename merchants and transactions and reassign dates  - You can keep track of reoccurring bills and whether you were charged   Cons: - Biggest complaint and draw back: The app will show you how you’re doing in your own personal budgets you’ve customized DURING the month, but once that month is OVER you can’t see that data anymore. So if I want to know if I continually overspend or underspend in one budget, that info is gone. For previous months, it will show you broader categories in a pie chart and tell you your overall spending, but it won’t tell you how you did compared to what you wished to spend. I want to see a bar graph of my spending in each budget I created month after month and know which ones I’m overspending/underspending on to understand my habits. - Once you’ve grouped your budgets, it’s really unclear if the number at the top is your estimated total spending, or your actual spending for the month  - It doesn’t always remember a merchant and a category I assigned it very well - it’s also bad at guessing what a merchant is (grocery, gas station etc.)  - It’s difficult to “budget” savings into your monthly “expenses”. The app doesn’t seem to like assigning a positive balance to it. There is a goals function that you can use for savings but it doesn’t show in your monthly pot of money then.  - I’ll reconnect the app to my Fidelity account and it works for like a month and then it looses a connection again. I finally stopped reconnecting it to those accounts.

title: MFA for PocketGuard
content: I’d like to see PocketGuard implement MFA (possibly authenticator enablement)

title: Our favorite free finance app
content: My wife and I tried 4 other free finance apps (the one built into our bank app, Mint, HoneyDue, and I can’t think of the 4th), and this one takes the cake for us. The others were glitchy (HoneyDue), overly complicated and not customizable enough (Mint) or too basic for us (Bank), but PocketGuard offers a very clean and user friendly interface, while also doing all the things that we wanted our finance app to do. It is very customizable, and the notifications are timely and correct.

title: Has helped me a lot
content: I have had the app about 6 or 7 months and have really liked it. I’m an accountant and someone who checks my bank accounts every morning and my goal was to pay off my credit card debt. I’ve done that now and this has helped me do it. I always was someone who used to use excel or paper budgets but my issue was I would lose track because I didn’t want to carry my budget with me. I paid for the premium and I have a few different banks, a few incomes, and I love that you can edit the transactions. I noticed at couple months ago some of the bills were glitching a little but they updated it really soon after that and it has gone back to normal which has shown me that although there are sometimes little bugs they are prompt to fix them. I will continue to use this and do recommend it to people who are wanting to get more serious about managing money.

title: Getting better and better!
content: I recommend this app to everyone! They have taken my recommendations and included them in the app for instance adding an ability to roll over budgeted amounts to the next month. Every update gives more utility and usefulness. I love the fact that they have an option to outright buy it rather than continue to pay a monthly or yearly subscription and for that reason I am writing this review!

title: Spam email
content: Don’t sign up.  They will bombard you with spam email and will make you click at least 20 options just to stop.

title: Bait and Switch
content: I assumed there was a free aspect to this but once I got to the end of the steps, I had to choose a plan, paying for it. Either make the app free, or make the app be purchased. Now I have wasted time trying to use an app that I cannot financially afford right now.

title: Could use more features but it's the best I've found so far
content: Works way more simple than rocket money, ynab, etc. does and I have TWO jobs which means, have you guessed it? TWO sources of regular income. the biggest reason I got rid of the other budgeting apps I tried out was because you couldn’t have more than one scheduled repeatable income source, which means my projected weekly budgets were not correct and I had to mentally remember to add the income from my other job to every budget because inevitably all the budgets would end up projecting negative amounts in them because half of my income was missing. it’s nice that this app lets me have both of my jobs.  However there are two issues I have with this app: 1. this app doesn't have a calendar function. I really like when the budgeting apps have a calendar built into the app so you can open it and visually see what your bills are going to be for that week with your projected income to see if you'll have enough money. A basic check list of my upcoming bills is about as useful as me writing out a list of my upcoming bills on paper which obviously didn’t help me much or I wouldn’t have bothered downloading an app. 2. There’s not an option for a light theme. I cannot stand dark themes, I personally find them annoying and difficult to read because I keep my screen brightness down fairly low to avoid eye strain and conserve battery making it irritating to try and navigate around a dim black phone screen.

title: App stopped working out after I already payed for the year. I’m still waiting on a refund.
content: I was excited to use it at first. And it worked perfectly well. Then it starts having syncing issues, shortly after I’ve already purchased the year subscription. According to support, the app is incompatible with my bank. Something I was not told, even though I hadn’t had any issues prior. I was unable to use the features promised for months. And when I contacted support about the issue and requested a refund. I was told to contact Apple support. After following the instructions of their support agent, I still had no resolution. Contacting support again led me here, as I was told to contact Apple support again, because there isn’t anything they could do.  Frankly, the app has many major selling points, it’s why I was willing to invest. However, the way customer support has worked at resolving an issue for a customer who payed for a year subscription and only got a month. As a consumer please beware. And if you bank with Redwood Credit Union, just save your money. Support won’t help you get it back. I’ll update once I’ve heard back from Apple.

title: better than all the others
content: The perfect budgeting app for me. Fits all of my needs and is super user friendly. I was using Rocket Money before but it was lacking some features that Pocket Guard fills and more. I love it, actually makes me excited to budget and work towards my financial goals.

title: Poor platform
content: If you were looking for somewhere to quickly and simply tell you how much you’ve spent in each category and how much you have left to spend in layout all your finances and an organized manner. This is not the app for you. Everything is hard to find and buried the information that it gives you upfront as you open the app is not the information that you need

title: Has its ups and downs but it's going the right way
content: Has its ups and downs but it's going the right way

title: Bait and switch
content: No longer offers a basic option.  This app does nothing without the premium subscription.

title: Good
content: Love this app I always seem to leave and come right back because I have found another app that lets me sort out my budget for which  bills I’m paying for each paycheck like this does .Would be nice to be able to see more of the credit cards in the account section. Where we can see what’s available to spend and not just the statement balance.

title: Life changing
content: I’ve meant to get a budget for so long I’ve been using pocket guard for about 8 months and it has had an incredible positive impact on my spending. I feel so much more in control of my life

title: All in one place
content: This app has really helped me to organize and track my finances in real time. I love the ease, accessibility, and accuracy of the app. Highly recommend if you are looking for middle of road financial planning and budgeting (not too expensive and has all of the basic features).

title: Good Mint replacement
content: I subscribed to PG after Mint shut down and have been happy so far. It has most of what I need from Mint and in some ways is more streamlined. I think the UX can be more polished (mostly little things around clearer verbiage, how many clicks is needed to do things like recategorize a transaction, etc). The team puts out updates at a good pace so I trust things will continue to improve. Wishing the team success.

title: Made me pay and now won’t open
content: Was looking forward to using but now the app won’t open and keeps directing me to the AppStore to update my app but there’s nothing available to upgrade to

title: Sudden Subscription Change
content: With two days notice, the switched from having a free version, to suddenly all my financial data being hidden behind a paywall and limited responses to my questions. As a company whose mission is to help individuals gain control over their finances, they really should take the own advice. Be wary of sudden changes that will cost you hundreds of dollars.

title: Still having issues…
content: I bought the year subscription. It worked for about a week and now none of my accounts are syncing.  Makes this totally unusable. And I have to wait 2-3 days to get a response from anyone at PocketGuard.   Why do you not have a customer service number???

title: Keeps improving
content: I was a power user of Mint.com and at first this app was disappointing, but they regularly release updates with gradual improvements. They have sent me surveys and respond to me about what I said in them. I definitely feel they are trying to make this a great product, and I definitely recommend it now.

title: Unreliable
content: Transactions appear and then disappear, and I get an error when I try to categorize them. These issues make it impossible for me to continue using the app.

title: Easily the best
content: Worth every penny. Easily the best app and I’ve tried all of them.

title: forced subscription
content: you used to be able to use this app for free but now you’re forced to choose a subscription plan if you already had an account before. The only options other than that is contact support, log out, or delete profile. no where does it say that you data will be deleted along with it. this was a great app without the subscription which is honestly one of the reason i downloaded it. it does help a lot with budgeting but $13 a month isn’t worth it let alone $75 for a whole year when the whole point is for me to save money.

title: Great app
content: Now that they include roll over budgets it’s exactly what I need

title: Great app
content: It’s a lot to take in at first but after a month or two of it tracking your expenses and making sure you catagorize things in a way that makes sense to you consistently it will become a very helpful tool to have to keep you on track. I am a buyer of the premium on this app but I waited to write this review until after buying it to make sure I experienced both types of the app. In my personal opinion the premium is worth it.

title: Not user friendly
content: I want to like this app! I paid the $75 so I plan on using it but it is not user friendly. I’ve had several questions and contacted them but no one ever gets back to you. I’m frustrated. I’m not saying don’t get it.. just be aware it might be hard to figure out.

title: Keeps locking me out of my bank
content: PocketGuard has acknowledged that an issue with their data provider is causing a sync problem with one of my banks. This started more than a week ago. The impact of this issue is that the bank is locking me out every single day   due to failed login attempts. The app does not provide an option to delete banks. After asking support how to delete the back and getting no acknowledgement of the question, I discovered on my own that you can log in to the website through a browser to delete banks. However, the delete option is grayed out on the bank with the sync issue.  Tech support just tells me they’re working on it, no ETA, they’ll let me know when they learn something, but does not acknowledge my question any deleting that bank so I stop getting locked out while they work on it. This is completely unacceptable.   I generally like the app, but it’s not worth being locked out by banks.

title: No More "In My Pocket"
content: I'm really disappointed that you got rid of the "in my pocket" feature. I stuck with this app, despite its shortcomings and frustrations, due to the in my pocket feature, which as far as I know was unique to this app. Now I have no reason to continue using it and I will look for a new one. No, the "leftover" feature is NOT the same.

title: Too many crashes
content: The app keeps crashing with ‘Request Failed : Forbidden (403)’ error in a red banner on top.   Switched to this app after Mint shutdown, regretting the choice.

title: Best bang for your buck
content: Incredibly easy to use once you get the hang of it, offers all the services of the more expensive budgeting apps.

title: Free Trial Ended charged for year subscription 14 day return is a joke
content: I forgot to cancel on the 14th day. I actually was going to continue with using the app but on a month to month basis. Once I realize I forgot to cancel I tried to get a refund. I have been denied on all fronts. I feel scammed now I do not want to even use the app anymore. Do not sign up for the free trial, they will not give your money back.

title: Good but
content: PocketGuard is very good and easy to use. It could be excellent and will deserve a five star if it can give a bar chart for monthly expenditures and report expenditures for customized period.

title: Clunky but effective
content: The app overall is great and their customer support is quick to respond. I love that it helps get basic budgeting answers done. My biggest problem is the lack of compatibility with other banks. For months, my Marcus accounts refused to sync, and even though Pocketguards customer service was responsive, the issue took literal months to fix. Everything worked fine for another two months, and then my local bank stopped syncing, and the customer service gave me the same response.  I appreciate the communication and hard work, but when your banks constantly don’t sync with the app, the app becomes ineffective. Whenever the app finally reconnects to my bank, I’ll have to go back and play catch-up on all my transactions while operating in the dark in the mean time. Now, with this happening twice, I’ll just be paranoid when the next time one of my banks no longer syncs up with PocketGuard.   Again, it’s a good app, so maybe I’m just unlucky, but when your app doesn’t sync with the banks, it becomes pointless, especially when you spend a large chunk of money on the app itself.

title: Couldn’t sign up
content: My IP looks suspicious.  On both my laptop and phone.  No VPN…

title: Awful app
content: The app shows net worth per month as bar plot, which is terrible and calculation is incorrect. All apps I used or tried before show net worth as line or area chart, which is more appropriate. Also the app freezes most of the time while loading new transactions and I have to close the app and re-open it again. Some of its features like “Plan” are useless because it’s so confusing to use.

title: Glitchy but nicely structured
content: I really hope that they can fix the glitching. We just installed this a few days ago, both me and my husband are having issues of needing to close out of app because of loading

title: Does not work with iOS 16!
content: I’m so frustrated and disappointed.  App freezes constantly with latest iOS.  Also cannot log in via web app either.  If not fixed I have to Churn.  Totally hope they get it fixed.

title: Very buggy
content: This app is so frustrating. It is great for the services that it offers, such as budgeting and tracking spending, but when you go to update transactions it gets stuck loading and I constantly have to exit out of it and half the time it won’t reload when I reopen it. I’m frustrated that I paid for the year subscription and now I have to deal with a very buggy app that makes it impossible to use most of the time.

title: Hard to Use!
content: As a career banker and someone with an MBA, I found this app extremely difficult to use. It double counted many things which was an effect of using both the recurring bills category and budget tracking. This was not apparent at set up and I could not get it to right itself, even making recurring items inactive and asking for assistance from customer service, who also was not helpful.  At the end of the month, it showed that I had a negative number left in my pocket, which was incorrect, but then when I added a paycheck as income for that period it went negative thousands more…how can that even occur mathematically and in a user-friendly experience?  Do not recommend! Going back to the Dave Ramsey app.

title: Broken
content: This app rarely opens on my phone and if it does it crashes quickly. I’m not sure if it’s not compatible with the new iPhone update, but I’d really like my money back for my subscription if the app is not going to do anything but take up space.

title: Worked for just over a month…. UPDATED
content: Worked for a month and I decided to purchase the premium version. A week after I purchased a year subscription one of my banks no longer updated. I contacted support and they explained it was something on their end and they could not provide a timeline as to when it would be fixed. It’s been two months now and it’s still not fixed and it’s too late to request a refund for purchasing the premium version. I would not recommend PocketGuard and if you do go month to month so you don’t run into the same situation I did. Regards.  06SEP2024  I wanted to provide an update to my previous review. After working with PocketGuard support for a little over a month, he resolved all issues that I had. I no longer have any connection issues with my financial provider in PocketGuard has also provided updates to budgeting which I couldn’t find more useful I couldn’t be happier to have stuck with the PocketGuard with the help from their team.  I highly recommend PocketGuard to anyone wanting to do spend tracking in budgeting. Thank you to PocketGuard in the support team for all their help!!

title: Great app, so easy to use and efficient
content: I find this app to be the best yet in helping me organize my finances, spending, tracking each purchase, keeping everything in one place, and ability to categorize spending.

title: Get This App
content: I am loving this app and I have tried several. All of my banks and credit cards link up to the app without any errors and the interface is very user-friendly. I was already planning to keep the app because of how easy it makes it for me to analyze my spending, but then I got an email from warning me I only had two days left on my free trial and warning me to cancel before I get charged I don’t love the app. That is proof right there of how confident PocketGuard is that they have a quality app, and they are right! Great app, download it for yourself!

title: AMAZING
content: Now with Apple Card support. Just. 10/10

title: Love it for the most part.
content: I really like the user interface and tools within the app.  The only reason u give it 4 stars not 5 is that, I cannot log on to multiple devices at one time, nor can I share my budget.  My spouse and I use this together and it would make things so much easier if we were able to share it that way.  When I tried using the “share” option in the app, it just send a link for them to create their own individual budget/profile

title: Could be great
content: This app *could* be great. But they have some real issues with getting it to remain connected with normal, every day banking institutes. I suspect it has something to do with 2 factor authentication on my banking side. Obviously I won’t lower security measures to get an app to work.   There’s very little by means of support. I of course was asked if I had the correct password, as if I was stupid. Then I was encouraged to change my banking password via pocket guards “change my password” link again like I’m stupid. There’s nothing wrong with my banking login, I can access it all fine. A few days later I received another email from support telling me it was all a mystery & they’d forward it to the engineers. So it’s anyone’s guess when it’ll start working properly.   Is pocket guard great? Nope.   Is it good? Meh  It’s passable at this point.

title: Not sure what’s wrong
content: I categorized all my transactions and then somehow the next day they were all uncategorized again

title: Fantastic!
content: I've been using this app for about 6 months. It's fantastic I didn't really need an app to plan my financial future, I just wanted to conveniently see what our family is spending money on across all credit cards and bank accounts. This is exactly what this app does in a clear, concise way.  Transactions are automatically assigned categories with good accuracy and you can edit them, create your own, and  include or exclude categories in calculations.  Actually one of our cards was fraudulently used for 2 airline tickets which I was able to notice immediately and rectify thanks to the app.    I also wanted an app without a monthly subscription which most other top rated apps have.  I paid for the premium app which is a one time, very reasonable fee.    One issue is the app really isn't set up as well to track year to date spending. Easy fix though- I have an excel sheet which includes all the categories I enter in less than 5 minutes once a month. This actually leads to another positive though.  The app team is absolutely fantastic about responding to issues and suggestions for improvements. I believe they are about to add a year to date feature and just recently Apple cards are now trackable.

title: A lot of promise, but cannot get help with the most basic items
content: I really like this app, however, getting any assistance from customer support seems almost impossible. After telling it to not use one of our accounts and to ignore it, it continued to use items from that account in our budget and planning. I contacted support for help, and after a week of still not hearing anything I guess I will cancel my subscription and remove the app from my phone and go to another app.

title: Very bad
content: I have paid for the subscription. The interface is very complicated. I cannot filter exact days and see how much I have spent that month. If I can not see what I spent and you cannot categorize it automatically what is the point of the whole app? Do not even consider uploading it

title: Poor customer support..
content: I paid for the lifetime subscription. It has been mixing up my bank accounts they are labeled as they would be at my bank, but if you look closely two of them repeat the same account number. So transactions from my most used account are not showing up. I tried contacting customer support some time ago but have received no response.

title: Overall great but a bit confusing
content: I just started using this app and I love it OVERALL. The issue I’m having is that I think some items in my budget are being double counted but I can’t quite tell. The confusion lies in the fact that there is a total for recurring bills, a total for monthly savings, and then a list of budgeted items and how much I’ve spent on those items… However, many of the recurring bills are IN the budgeted categories and there is no TOTAL for budgeted items that are not recurring bills. Pretty sure some of these are being double counted but it’s hard to tell.  I wish the app would have a simple total for budget (including savings), a total for income, and a total for actuals right next to each other so I can compare each month and see where I am at throughout the current month.   Am I not understanding how this works?

title: Garbage:  Constantly Unable to Sync
content: This app has been very disappointing.  It’s constantly unable to sync up with your external accounts.  It’s often displaying sync errors and asking you to reverify credentials, and then when you do, it’s usually unable to sync and asks you to try up to 5 times a day to provide data for a fix, and this usually goes on several days.  Then finally it will sync, so you assume the “bug” has been fixed, but then a week or two later, the same issue with the same account reoccurs and you need to repeat the cycle.  Don’t buy this App!  I will not be renewing my subscription.

title: Better then Mint budget app
content: When mint announcement came, I searched for a another viable budget app. Wish I knew this one sooner, would of left mint app long time ago. Paid for lifetime membership & don’t regret it.   Ease of use, minimal to no glitches, positive list goes on. Running it on iPhone 14 Pro & IPad Pro

title: App keeps crashing
content: This app was really amazing. I used it all the time but it crashes every once in a while and it’s been weeks I cannot add any new transactions. Unfortunately I will have to delete it today

title: Does not integrate with PNC bank.
content: The app initially worked with my bank PNC. But after a few months stopped. The pocketgard support people had no resolution.

title: Terrible Support
content: Can’t even get logged in! Can’t receive an email from support. Support is terrible!

title: Really good budget app!!!
content: I was so sad when Mint went away, but this has replaced it without skipping a beat. I even like a few of the features better.

title: It’s ok
content: Would be 5 stars if it didn’t disconnect from the bank every week. You have to reattach to your accounts every week. When I had mint it didn’t do that. And of course you cont reconnect on the weekend. So frustrating.

title: Frustrating
content: Couldn’t link some accounts. When I tried to manually enter the accounts it wasn’t doing anything. Found it frustrating to just get it set up. 7 days is not a long enough trial period as it takes time to get everything set up & learn how to use. I might have given it more of a chance if trial period was longer, pref 30 days.

title: Liked until my bank’s change stopped it from syncing
content: I used and liked the app for a few months. It currently does not sync with my bank because if a change they made so I stopped using it.

title: Pretty good with room for improvement
content: 1. Please add other periods 1yr and YTD vs just one month  2. Weekly reports doesn’t seem to work  3. Developers engagement much better during the trial period so enjoy the honeymoon phase of the free trial period

title: No free tier like previously advertised
content: Had to use trial but then first two banks I tried to connect failed.

title: Not a great start
content: I loved Mint. I used it for years but like many I was left wandering the web finding a new financial planning tool after Mint’s questionable business decision.  I thought YNAB was too complicated and other planning apps are subscription based. I stumbled on this app after searching for “Affordable Budgeting Tools”  I thought I could manage with the free version of the app but I was shocked that they limited the number of accounts that can be linked to 2: one credit card and one bank account. For some this may be manageable but I had student loans and investment accounts I needed to link as well so I sprung for the yearly plan; if it’s good I’ll swap to lifetime. If it doesn’t, I’ll drop it.   So far, I’ve gotten a rocky impression. My first 2 links must have been flukes because linking all my other accounts has been nightmarishly slow. This app doesn’t use Plaid which is like the go to service for linking financial services. Instead it uses some other method by Mastercard which fails on the first try. I’d give the app a 1 but the developer was wise enough to include Plaid as a secondary. I’m still linking accounts after a couple days; usually it takes a couple hours to set up my finances on a new platform. Overall I’m not impressed but I’m hoping they can change my mind before the year is up.

title: Amex Bank Accounts Don’t Sync
content: Buying the annual membership for this app was the worst mistake of my life. This app has CONSTANT SYNCING ISSUES with banking institutions rendering the app worthless. I noticed my Amex account not syncing since the beginning of March however I decided to be patient to see if devs would fix the issue and they never did. After looking at these reviews it appears other users have had the same problems and the developers have been aware since March only to add insult to injury. The app does not function as advertised and I’ve requested refund. I’ve contacted support for PocketGuard and have received no response. Please don’t waste your time this app and go look at Copilot or YNAB for budgeting.

title: It’s almost perfect
content: Out of all the budgets apps I’ve had, I like this one the best. Trust me I’ve downloaded them all, I’m a zero based budgeter so a lot of apps don’t allow for paycheck based budgeting and this is one of them.   I like this one because it auto calculates your debt payments to what works for your budget.  Things I wish this had:  •linking Bills - some bills fluctuate, I wish there was a way to sign in to my electricity acccount and have it auto populate how much I owe so I can see everything In one place.  • income budgeting, there’s a place to input your income but since it’s AI I was hoping that it would calculate or let me select which bills, debt, budgeted items,  I wanted to pay with that paycheck.   For $80 bucks I just wish it did more

title: HUGE price increase
content: I downloaded the app on a recommendation specifically because the prices were a good value, $80 for lifetime access. However it seems that a few months ago the prices doubled for everything. Now $80 for only a year and $150 lifetime. Big difference!!

title: HIGHLY recommend
content: I’ve been using this app for about 6 months and it’s incredible. The free version has everything you need to track your expenses and categorize your purchases. I highly recommend to anyone wanting to get control of their finances.

title: Promised but never delivered
content: Only reason I paid for this app because their roadmap supposed deliver rollover budgets in January, now it’s mid may and we still don’t have feature available. Regretting now for paying for lifetime subscription, should have gone to simplifi.

title: Major Sync Issues
content: I wanted to like this budget app and I actually preferred it to some others. However, after my free trial ended, 2 out of my 3 accounts stopped syncing. Not only that, but I went to re-sync it, something in their software triggers a security notice at the bank and the bank locked me out of my account. Ironically, the best tool you have is to NOT purchase this app. I have requested a refund because this app is actually unusable for me at this point.

title: Unimpressed
content: Ok, I admit that I’ve only spent about 2 hours with the app trying to get things set up and understand how things work. What has become obvious from the start is that there appears to be no tutorials available whatsoever on how to effectively implement this tool. PocketGuards YouTube channel shows one promotional video. How are people finding the help they need to get set up?

title: Great Oversight, but Robinhood Integration Falls Short
content: As a premium user of PocketGuard, I've found it to be an invaluable tool for managing my finances. It offers excellent oversight of my accounts, helping me stay on top of my spending and savings goals effortlessly.  However, there's one persistent issue that has been bothering me for quite some time now: the inability to connect and display balances from my Robinhood investment account. No matter how many times I try to refresh it, the integration simply doesn't work. This problem has persisted since I became a premium user and hasn't been resolved despite my efforts.  Overall, PocketGuard is a fantastic app for financial management, but the ongoing issue with Robinhood integration detracts from its otherwise stellar performance. I hope the developers address this issue soon to provide a seamless experience for all users.

title: Categorized Budgets
content: You can only add two categorized budgets for free and to me, that defeats the purpose. It doesn’t even tell you that until after you’ve completed the first three or four steps, where it seems like everything will be good and fair.  Been trying to find an app to replace Mint but so far, none are nearly as good (for free).

title: Great tool - simple and easy to use
content: I love that it is customizable for categories, and whether or not a transaction should be counted. The budget is simple and easy to see where the money goes, and where you can make adjustments. The updates from bank accounts with merchant info and the ability to split the receipt into multiple categories. Just a well thought out and user friendly app. Only suggestion is to make it available to adjust a future budget, i.e. the coming month. That would make it easier to plan for certain expenses.  Still love it!  Helped me budget for a big purchase without as much stress, and it is helping me save for future vacations and extra house payments (4/28/24)

title: App is useless for AMEX and others
content: Their sync tool makes it to where some banks, like PNC, won’t actually sync and cards like AMEX need to be re-synced every time you log in (which takes 5 minutes). Their customer service team blames it on AMEX but Mint, Credit Karma, Intuit, and several others don’t have this issue. They’ll refuse refund even just a week later.

title: Terrible start up
content: They trick you into selecting a “trial” instead of making it obvious that you can start a free account. I cancelled my account to try and start again and now it’s not allowing me to open an account. What a waste of time

title: Works Great
content: I switched to PocketGuard like a lot of people when mint was integrated with credit karma and they didn’t offer budgeting anymore which was my primary use for it.  PocketGuard works really well and is user friendly. I wish there was an option for quarterly, bi-monthly, or annual budgets. I have a few and it can be frustrating to get an accurate depiction of my finances and monthly spending. Hopefully that’s something that is in development.

title: Buggy updates
content: The latest update has made the app buggy and slow. My categorizations keep getting reset!

title: Don’t do it
content: I don’t get all of the good reviews, this app is one of the worst.  The UI is from the 90s, all features require a subscription, and those features aren’t actually that good.  Lastly, they way they connect your data means that Plaid is taking your information and selling it.  See the $58 million settlement for Plaid.  I’ve requested a refund, through Apple and their customer service.

title: Decent App, doesn’t synch with Apple Pay
content: Disappointed that it doesn’t synch with Apple Pay like Monarch does.  Would consider switching back if it did.  Synchs with all the other bank accounts and loans nicely.

title: Almost a Mint replacement
content: I’ve been pleased with the user interface as a recovering Mint user trying to move on. I can’t give PocketGuard 5 stars though because it’s missing some obvious features. They seem like possible easy fixes so maybe there’s hope! Pros: Mint Import, split transactions, manual cash transactions, nice monthly trends, Web access, Wise account connects (using Plaid link). One time purchase (find in iOS for $80), shared user for Budgeting.   Cons: auto categorization is poor - most of my transactions have to be manually changed (supposedly it will learn tho as I creat rules. The worst part is that there are NO SuBCATEGORIES?! The graphs are nice, but you’ll need a lot of custom categories or just general overview with no subcategories, seems like an odd miss for a tracking app. Also no multi Currency (unlike Wallet and Spendee), rollover budgeting still in roadmap, no iPad oriented App (unlike Buddy and Wallet). Accounts are sometime not updated - it seems like it does not have manual refresh for all accounts?

title: Bad experience
content: All the budgeting plan charge you monthly. This is not a free app. Don’t even bother downloading.

title: Mint was way better
content: My biggest problem with Pocket guard is that when I go to check my accounts, I can’t view them all on one page, I have to scroll down to see them all so I end up writing them down on paper which kinda negates the advantage of having them listed on an app.      Secondly, I can’t check my latest transactions in each account. The transactions are listed but it is not easy to see which account they were made from or what category they might belong to.      Thirdly, I find it would be more helpful to have my accounts listed in ranked order from greatest to least.      Fourth, the option to log out should be on the main screen, or at least at the top of the drop down menu.       I miss Mint.

title: Free trial is a SCAM - you can’t cancel
content: Literally spend FOREVER, sent three emails and deleted several points of detailed data in order to cancel this free trial before I was charged and YOU CANT! It’s a scam. Period. They claimed I needed to delete the subscription from apple (purchase on the App Store) but the only thing purchased through app was the FREE trial. They charged the subscription on my card. Nothing listed as even possible to refund because nothing was purchased through apple. Deleted EVERYTHING from the app, followed all the cancelation instructions and email THREE TIMES to insure I was all set. Silence.  Listen, this is a scam.

title: Unfulfilled Promises and No Refunds
content: This app promised several updates that kept getting pushed back. I was very patient in waiting for them to provide the updates they promised. However, when I finally reached out after months of waiting, I was told they still were unsure of the expected updates. I asked for a refund and they were unable to process it. I was told to go through Apple. However, Apple said that I waited too long and they were no longer able to refund me for the subscription. Long story short: don’t believe PocketGuard when they say they are going to make updates. And don’t wait too long for them to make these updates before you request a refund!

title: Cannot link/authenticate TD Canada account
content: 3 weeks ago, perfectly valid TD Bank login credentials started failing in this app. It’s useless.

title: Subscription Trap
content: Making you pay for another subscription after paying $75 for one year is insane.

title: Just ok.. lots of syncing errors
content: I have an American Express card and recently it’s started to disconnect from pocket guard and is the biggest hassle to log back into.   I also noticed that at least once a week my transactions are moved out of the “Budgets” I assigned them to previously, so I have to go back and do it again. It’s a good concept of an app but there are many bugs that make it frustrating.   I’d also like the ability to see from month to month where I’m at versus just one single month… rename certain transactions differently.. several things like that that just don’t have the customization.

title: Love this app
content: I’ve always been a Mint user but found PocketGuard and haven’t skipped a beat! Really like the functionality of this app with the best support team!

title: Full budget armor
content: Anyone seeking financial confidence should look no further. This app gives you the tools to take control of your financial health.

title: PocketGuard no longer supports Amex
content: Purchased the full version, worked for a month until it had sync issues with credit cards (Mastercard and Amex). They rolled out Plaid to try and fix the integration, however this has not worked. In discussions with support they have responded   We hate to tell you this, but American Express credit card doesn’t allow our data provider to build a sustainable integration with PocketGuard, which resulted in the issue you face. Resolution turnaround is unknown.

title: Bank Connect Didn’t Work
content: I don’t know what verification service they use but it didn’t work with my bank couldn’t use the app unfortunately, maybe if I change banks in the future i’ll try again

title: Expected more
content: There are simpler ways to do about things that I had expected. Sort of give more options to the users who wants it.  For one, there is no easy way to access any categories that I made without getting deep into each layer. I like to just categorize into whatever category I made but thats so so hard to access.  Second, for each category, there is no ‘money in’ tabs and ‘money out’. So i dont know how much I received money on a particular category or so since there is no distinction.  Third, I like to see my spending details by month. I selected January then I saw my self made category and clicked it and I was presented with all the items that are in that particular category up till this day.  Fourth, if I don’t include a certain spending in any category, it will automatically put it into its own generated category (which is fine by me) but it is not shown in the ‘overview’ tabs which is very frustrating.  I was giving this a try but now Im just contemplating into going back to just an excel sheet. I used Wallet by BudgetBakers before and I liked it except the fact that it can’t import csv pretty well w/o its own issues and some minor bugs.   I just want more choices to those who wants better control of their finances instead of expecting the app to do it for them. Everyone is different.

title: Not able to get free version
content: If you have read online as I have reviews in Jan 2024 that there is a free version, there isn’t. Apparently they saw all the prior Mint users (like myself) looking for a new budget app and decided to drive greater profit off it. If I am gonna pay, there are better options out there based on my research like Simplifi.

title: App Stopped Working No Support
content: The app stopped syncing with my bank more than two weeks ago. I contacted support and never received a reply. Completely unacceptable for a subscription based service.

title: Great for folks with many accounts
content: The only suggestion I’d have for improvement is to be able to categorize or add notes for multiple transactions at a time.  Really like the app otherwise.

title: Not delivering what they said
content: Switched over from Mint. Chose this app because lower cost then competitors and said they would create rollover budget in January 2024. However they did not create it and said to create a cash transaction. I will not pay and keep this app if there is no rollover monthly budget. Everything else seems it’s okay

title: Better than Mint
content: I came across PocketGuard when looking for a replacement budgeting app after finding out Mint was being shuttered. I had been using Mint for over 7 years and had got used to it. Although I was skeptical that I could get used to a brand new budgeting app I quickly found PG to not just be as good as Mint, but better in almost every way!  I like that they offer a one-time lifetime purchase as I despise monthly subscriptions. The best feature in PG is the recurring income and bills. With Mint I often had problems remembering those quarterly or yearly bills and they’d throw off my whole budget. With PG I never have to worry about forgetting them because they’re always scheduled. It’s also helpful to be able to see next month’s estimated bills and income.   Highly recommend PocketGuard to any fellow budgeters!

title: App stopped working (last 5 days)
content: App no longer updates accounts, tried refreshing, resetting, the web version fails to login. No access and seemingly no support.   Having just purchased a yearly subscription, I’m regretting now going month to month so I could cancel.  If the service doesn’t have dependable uptime (web or app) why would I pay for it or use it.   Very displeased.

title: Gorgeous but useless app
content: Looking for something to use instead of mint and found PocketGuard. The UI is gorgeous and colorful but what’s the point when it doesn’t work to connect a single bank? Also there’s not a single free option

title: Unauthorized Charges on my Credit Card
content: EDIT Updated Review (updated to 4 stars): My issue below has since been resolved. I was reached out to by support on February 5th, through the review that I left, not by my original support requests. Once I provided my account information they were able to find my support requests and they were able to send a refund to my credit card. I then purchased the lifetime option for PocketGuard plus and have not had any issues so far.   I give this app 4 stars because it works as advertised. The loss in a star is for my issues with contacting customer support and the inability to cancel a subscription online, which almost every subscription service allows you to do this day and age. I opted to purchase the lifetime option so that last point should no longer matter in my use case.   This current customer service issue is probably because of the current influx from Mint shutting down, so hopefully it will be a non issue going forward.   Original Review (1 star): The app itself works to my liking. However they have charged my credit card for the annual cost, which I never signed up for and support has been impossible to reach in my multiple inquiries. I signed up for the free trial/monthly subscription. Before the end of the free trial I logged in and followed all of the instructions on the website on how to cancel the subscription. My intention was to then purchase the lifetime option. I sent multiple messages through the website portal, and to the direct email. The only thing I have received is an automated response saying they will get back to me. Meanwhile, my credit card has now been charged for the annual cost of the app which I never agreed to pay (I signed up for the monthly subscription). I again sent another email to support about the issue and I have still not received a response. At the time of this review my first message to support was sent on January 25th through the message tab on the website and my last email to them was on January 28th. I will be more than happy to update my review if this gets resolved.

title: Total disappointment
content: I just signed up and found out that the price has doubled in the last few weeks and the non yearly full purchase is no longer available. After contacting customer service at least five times with no response, I dropped this app like a hot potato.  I can’t believe they charge anything with the poor service and random high pricing. I decided on Monarch and they seem great.  Good luck if you choose this app and before you sign up contact customer service and see how long they take to get back to you.

title: Great budgeting app
content: For the price PocketGuard is a great way to easily track your spending into either preset categories or new categories that you can make as needed.  As long as you stay on top of marking transactions you can easily see how much you are spending in various areas and make adjustments as needed.

title: The apps great! But.
content: The app itself works great. It’s the customer service that is lacking. I have been emailing nonstop for a week with no reply whatsoever. I got signed up for the one year I think. I was charged in the bank, but there is nowhere I can find to see the actual subscription I have been charged for or how to control it.  There’s nowhere in the app that says this is the subscription you have this is when your renewal date is or anything.

title: Old Mint User
content: I as addicted to Mint and leveraged it to help tackle debt and control spending. As a single mom with a house and two kids, my finances have to be right. This tool is phenomenal and the product team is very approachable and friendly. In My Pocket is an awesome feature.   Only suggestions for me after a couple months of near daily use: ensure the tab icons can be tapped to autoscroll back up - by nature some tabs have long scrolls so a quick jump up is helpful. On the donut chart and line chart for current spending it would also be helpful to show the diff dollar amount against 1 month ago spending, not just the full total from last month end against today.   Really well done folks.

title: Not customizable or user friendly
content: I’ve been using YNAB but need to find a different tool that’s more focused on just tracking spending. Pocketguard is not the one. It does not allow you to create broad categories and automatically assumes all inflow is recurring. Navigation is confusing. I would move on to a different software.

title: No multicurrency
content: App looks good, unfortunately it does not support multiple currencies and becomes crazy when a transaction is downloaded in another currency, showing the amount in dollars (eg. a transaction of MX$1600 is shown as US$1600, which is almost 20x more).

title: Do not sign up with this scam!
content: They will charge you and you have no recourse. Their support email addresses are literally fake and undeliverable. When we tried to cancel our subscription there is literally nobody to talk to or email or get a hold of. Along with that the app doesn’t even function properly or have a computer interface.

title: Removing from my device
content: It’s a great looking UI, and seems like great features. The problem is it just won’t register one of my regular paychecks I get monthly from the link with my bank. It gets one but not the second check. Because it looks like I’m over budget since it can’t see my full income it won’t let me make a budget or any goals. I’ve submitted questions through the help messaging and emailed and no one responds. I’ve had it for a couple months now hoping it would catch up but no such luck. So I’m not going to pay for anymore months on an app I can’t use. Good luck to others!

title: Double posting
content: Writing this review in hopes I receive a response from the developer. The app is double posting my transactions.  I try to delete but in able, try to hide one and both go hidden and then shows my bill not paid. Looking for assistance from the developer.

title: Another Use to Be
content: I used to love this app. Tracking was amazing but over the last few mo thank keep getting issues with updating or it deleting my info. I tried to connect my bank I don’t keep getting error messages then it tells me I got to wait 24 hours to check again. Or Info not updating at all. I’m over it I will spend my money else where.  PS. I ran out of daily available attempts because your system wouldn’t allow me. When I tried it would say oops try again and when I didn’t said I ran out. I find it funny that some one could respond to the review but no one has ever emailed me back about the issue I contacted you guys about. No worries, I have already cancelled my subscription and found another app.

title: It’s okay
content: The user interface for this is just okay. I was able to successfully connect accounts. Unfortunately it looks like they decided to cash in when Mint went down and there is no longer an option for a lifetime subscription. I don’t need yet another subscription in my life. I’m out.

title: Errors when connecting accounts
content: Repeated errors when connecting account. Removed the app and reinstalled. Same issue. Then was blocked for “too many attempts” and told to wait 24 hours. No thanks!

title: The BEST budgeting app out there
content: Can I just start off by saying I downloaded and tried using so many budgeting apps. I did lots of research to find the best rated apps and tried them all. I found this app and I will never look back!  I needed a budgeting app that would track my spending, track my savings goals, and clearly show me where I was going over. This app does it all. I also do a lot of transferring money from one account to another, I’ve had trouble tracking this on other apps. PocketGuard let’s you easily hide transfers so they don’t confuse your budget. Same goes for credit card payments or other random charges I don’t want counted towards my spending or savings goals. The app also gives you a breakdown of your month with pie charts and statistics. It also lays out all the information I need in a clear way that makes it easy to understand. My husband and I both love this app and plan on using it for many years to come.

title: Could be great
content: I will update the rating once syncing with regions mortgage actually works. It’s highly annoying to always have a “sync error” with no way to fix it. And why does it label ALL of my debit expenses as food?

title: Great mint replacement
content: Better than mint in my opinion. This app fits my needs perfectly.  Keeps my budget in check, and helps with future planning.

title: exactly what I wanted
content: I've been trying to keep better track of my finances and better prepare for bills and the like, but I've found it difficult to keep track of what happens when and make sure I don't miss any little charges. this app is exactly what I needed and has been a huge help!

title: 3 years of this life saving app!
content: So helpful to track multiple accounts at once, and visualize budgets.

title: Free?
content: This app isn’t free, when I went to sign up I had to choose a plan and both of them cost money, they were not free!  In the description of the app it says it’s a free budget app.

title: Cannot link AmEx High Yield Savings Accounts
content: I’m currently trialing a few finance/budgeting apps, and so far Pocket Guard is pretty good. It’s features and functions are easy and allows for a satisfying amount of customization (though I could use even more).  Where it is falling very short for me is the inability to link my AmEx High Yield Savings Accounts. The bulk of my cash are in these accounts making it tough to reap the full benefit of the app. Other apps seem to have this same issue, which is odd given I had no issue linking my AmEx credit card.   If I didn’t bank with AmEx, PG would be would be a no brainer for me to continue on with.

title: Not better than the free options
content: I regret paying for this. Too many financial institutions are not supported. The limit on the number of accounts you can add at one time (even with the paid version) makes the setup take several days. The lack of a credit score tracker is noticeably absent. Also, the interface could be a lot better. Overall, PocketGuard is not terrible, but you’re paying for a service that Credit Karma and Empower do for free. If you’re looking for a single app for all your financial data this just isn’t it.

title: Not even 5 hours in and I’m out.
content: I downloaded the app hoping to just pay a one time fee with no subscription. As it is advertised in their app page.   Web search’s turn up that they’re doing A/B price testing and playing around with subscriptions and pricing models. I’m good off that. I’ll be going back to the old ways of tracking my budget until I can find a simple one time fee that doesn’t require subscription and milk my budget for more money. The irony in the sales tactic is thick.   Now I’m just disappointed that I gave all my financial information to some organization that doesn’t have my best interests to begin with.

title: Couldn’t get started
content: App forces you to provide a phone number to get a confirmation code.  I went ahead and did that, even though I prefer not handing out my number.  Never received the text with the code, so couldn’t proceed.  Tried resend button, but nothing.  Then killed the app and started over with same result…

title: Phenomenal and Life Changing!
content: I’ve tried all the budgeting apps and felt that each one was missing a key feature that others had, but none had everything. I was just about to compromise and settle for one, but luckily I tried PocketGuard! If you took only the good features from all of the different budgeting apps and packaged them together perfectly, then you’d have PocketGuard! It has really helped me to see my spending habits, especially as a recovering “swipe now, worry later” kind of spender. Never trying anything else again and their prices are also much more affordable than other apps!   One feature I’d love to see though is the option for credit card payment due amounts being included as a bill. That way I can budget for money leftover after bills + cc payments needed. I know this isn’t useful for those that don’t carry balances, but for those of us that do, this would make budgeting so much more accurate.  Say you pull the minimum payment amount from each statement as they’re issued (since the amount can vary month to month) and it would show up as an Upcoming Bill and also deducted from In My Pocket. I’d also like to see the ability to mark smaller payments throughout the month as amounts towards the minimum payment amount so it shows the remaining.  Thanks and excited to see future updates!

title: Almost there  just a few more
content: This app is by far one of the best.  Love the goals and debit payoff. No other budget app has it.  A few things tend to throw everything off tho. 1. Not being about to mark as and “early pay” for the next month. A lot of times my pay post early in my bank, so most of the time toward the end of the month. It post the income in the wrong month that it should be in. 2. Rollover option should be available especially when trying to save up for goals and budget caps.  3. A better 3rd party partner for small banks/connecting accounts.  Most of my transactions come from a smaller bank doing everything manually kind of takes out the purpose of the app. These are  the only things  me from keeping my subscription. I’ll always check back and keep an eye on this app, though just to see if they have any good updates.

title: No team support
content: Several days before the free trial ended, I sent 3 emails to cancel my subscription and yet got charged for the life time subscription. They are so hard to reach and have terrible customer support and make it very difficult to cancel once you give them your credit card information.

title: Fidelity Customers: Do Not Use PocketGuard!
content: Former Mint user here. Thought I would give PocketGuard a try and avoid monthly/yearly payments. Unfortunately, if you have a Fidelity Cash management account, your transactions do not counts towards any budget/spending analytics. So the app is almost useless to me and I spent $100 on a lifetime subscription.  Worst part is, I’ve reached out to PocketGuard support several times and haven’t heard anything back for over a week. I’m incredibly disappointed, and wish I had known what I know now.  If they could fix this issue and/or actually respond to me, I would not have such bad things to say.

title: Good but support is unresponsive
content: I like this app but the “in my pocket” feature hasn’t worked for me. I’ve contacted support twice because my income is recognized in my transactions but not in my “in my pocket” estimate so it always says i’m like thousands of dollars in the negative. I have received no response from app support after contacting twice so I’m a little frustrated that I paid $80 for an app and the main feature is fully unusable.

title: No way to contact support
content: So, I bought this and when I discovered some issues I tried to cancel. It’s been 2 days of pressing the cancel subscription button in their app and nothing. Feels scammish. Finally found the support email. We’ll see.

title: amazing budgeting app!!
content: i’ve had this app for a bit and i can honestly say it’s perfect. the budgeting graphs are accurate, the bank accounts sync almost instantly, the tags system is quite handy; it’s overall a great app!! if you have the means, i would recommend the premium subscription!

title: Bank connectivity is great, managing while overseas? Not so much
content: I’m glad pocketguard has the best U.S bank connectivity out of all the budgeting apps I’ve used. I also love how the UI/UX is modern and minimalist. Problem is that I can’t access Pocketguard while traveling for business in Asia. And thing is I travel a lot. The only way to use Pocketguard is to turn on a VPN and then manually refresh my bank accounts to get the latest data which is a big inconvenience and that’s what stops me from paying extra. Other budgeting apps don’t have this problem

title: Solid App
content: I made the switch from Mint with it coming to an end and I appreciate there not being ads and being a little more user friendly. I wish there was an iPad version of this app. Reoccurring bills only being able to be tracked under bills or have them tracked individually in a budget line is inconvenient in my opinion.

title: Was hoping this my last budgeting app
content: I came over from Rocket Money because many of my accounts were not able to connect to Rocket Money. The good news is that all of my accounts connect to Pocket Guard. The not so good news is how Pocket Guard shows monthly budgets. I’m currently renovating my house and I’ve been transferring and spending savings. Pocket Guard doesn’t have the level of automation that Rocket Money does and so it is treating transfers and withdrawals as expenses effectively double counting.  Rocket Money does this for you, which is a time saver. I hope pocket guard enhances expense categorization. I paid for a lifetime membership and I’m starting to regret it.

title: Great app, complete and easy to use!
content: I love the app and it has all the features I was looking for in a budgeting app after switching from Mint. Only thing that would make it perfect is a bit more variety and content in the home page widgets. There is only one option which is not the best one for seeing all the information from my home screen as there are no numbers.

title: So simple, So good
content: This app has an In Your Pocket feature that is EXACTLY what I want from a budgeting app. You put in your income and expenses (with plenty of options to reflect the different types of both), and then you get to see what’s left “in your pocket.” If you want to know how much money you have to spend on ancillary purchases, that’s what this tells you. It’s the perfect thing to help you determine if a current purchase—for which an entire budget category doesn’t make sense—is reasonable or not. I highly recommend this app!

title: Don’t touch
content: Forced me to add payment info even though there is a free version and then gave me no option to cancel my premium subscription.

title: Best Budget App
content: I’ve tried Good budget, Every Dollar, Mint, YNAB… made my own spreadsheets… this is the best app I’ve found. It’s intuitive and makes the most sense. It isn’t dogmatic - several budgeting apps are very opinionated on how you should budget- this app lets you budget in a way that makes sense for you. Recommend.

title: Amex doesn’t work AFTER buying lifetime subscription
content: Amex has serious issues connecting for multiple days. I loved the app but I can’t connect my primary payment source it’s worthless.  I even paid for the lifetime subscription. Very disappointed.

title: Insisting on having me send sensitive account data over insecure email
content: I really want to like this app. In fact, I would sign up for the lifetime membership except for one issue where only a subset of my accounts in one bank show up.   I asked support for help and they will not get on the phone with me. Rather, they want me to email them bank account information. This is insane - if they are ok with sensitive information being shared by email, what else are they doing with my account information?  My bank literally warns me every month that I should never share by email the information that support is asking.

title: Syncing issues
content: Support is non existent, you pay 35 bucks a year to get crap support. Bank accounts don’t sync or have syncing problems. Just keep saying institutions under maintenance for weeks. What do we pay money for?

title: Accounts don’t sync
content: I purchased the annual subscription and then my accounts won’t sync anymore. Tried manually refreshing, deleting, and reinstalling and now my accounts haven’t synced in 3 days.   Was good until that point. Please fix.

title: Account syncing issues not fixed for weeks
content: I have been having intermittent sync issues with my accounts for months, and now my primary checking/savings accounts have not connected to the app at all for 6 weeks.
