I contacted support and was not given any information beyond basically ‘this is a known issue and we’re working on it.’ After several weeks with no updates, I reached out again and got essentially the same statement.   This app is useless without the functionality of automatically tracking transactions. I was finding the app really useful before the constant syncing issues, but I’m highly disappointed by the lack of urgency and communication in getting my account back in working order.

title: Love the App
content: Absolutely love this app. I am wondering if one day we are able to have main categories and sub categories for tracking expenses. Would that be possible?

title: This app is a disaster
content: I would be ashamed to have been the company who developed this. I feel extremely badly for the people who were trying to wrangle their dev team to produce something of quality. Most usability elements were completely tossed out of the window. Use Emma or Co-Pilot. Emma has separate spaces for business owners and Co-Pilot has great widgets. They really demolish this product.

title: Maybe a coincidence, but fishy.
content: After I downloaded this app, my boss got a scam email claiming to be me saying I had “changed my bank information”

title: Love the app
content: Love the app, but our account disappeared last night. Our email address doesn’t register as a customer account.

title: Ok app not the best
content: Longtime Mint user here, given the circumstances of Mint shutting down I’ve been on the hunt for a new budgeting app that allows me to gain insights into my money. Here are top things I did not like about this app.  1. My account aren’t organized. I’d like to be able to see a collapsed view of my checking and savings amount but also be able to see them broken out. On the accounts view tab I would see a credit card then a savings account then a checking account from another bank- just no organization. 2. There were a few credit cards I was not able to link. Using the premium version to limit all of my credit cards is critical for me as it allows me to gain a complete view of my finances- especially with subscriptions on certain cards. 3. Cancelling the subscription is NOT the easiest. I was still within the 7 day trial period to cancel but I still have wasn’t sure if I wasn’t going to be changed since I signed up on the web

title: Can’t even log in on a desktop
content: I selected “sign in with apple” when I signed up, then later tried to log in on my Mac, in the Safari browser (everything up to date). It loads forever. Not impressed.

title: Connectivity issues/limits
content: Setting up my AmEx was a nightmare and took almost a dozen times (finally, at some random point, switching to Plaid which worked perfectly). But they have stupid limits on adding accounts so now I’m locked out for 24 hours until I can test more bank account connections to see if they work. I’m willing to pay if it connects to everything and works well, but with my testing being limited by an artificially set restriction, I moved on to another app (and paying them instead).

title: No iPad?
content: Why is there no iPad app? It's almost 2024, this kind of disregard is unacceptable and ridiculous.

title: Love it
content: Been using this daily for the past few months. It’s changed the way that I think about and handle my money. Support has been super helpful, updates are frequent, and the app has an incredible feature set.

title: Avoid if you connect to more than 9 institutions
content: Just tried it and paid for a month. Within the same day I realized that it wasn't for me and I'm out $8. See below why.  If you have 9+ institutional accounts then it's a pain.  Only 9 will update in a 24hr window.  I had added two accounts, deleted got premium, and re-added, and this resulted in 2 getting double counted.  Treasury Direct also had trouble connecting, I tried twice to connect, and this too resulted in it counting twice.  Because 3 accounts were counting as 6, it made it a pain to add more accounts. Things got worse when. AMEX was trying to refresh more than once I'm a 24 hour window. AMEX would said error refreshing, and then I tried to fix the connection, Pocket Guard would say everything was OK.   I wish I had known about the 9 institution limit before paying for the monthly subscription.  Felt like a bait and switch. This was a deal breaker for me.

title: App needs some polish…
content: Plan page needs to have descriptions get a full line to themselves and the money should be below as a fraction of spent/budgeted: $122/$400. Also, the plan section lets you create a goal or budget at a section with Edit section, but then the new item appears at the bottom instead of in the section. There should be a way to shut off get out of debt for once you are out of debt or for those who do not want help. Great summaries and charts… but no way to dig into the data… clicking a chart portion should have a place where you can review transactions. It isn’t easy to see what account a transaction is coming from. Besides goals, there should be funds that float cash from previous months and have no date associated with them. The app is great about estimating the cost of something that changes over time, but if this month it’s $26 and next month it’s $30 I have to change my budget since it isn’t a fund (EveryDollar offers funds). Also it doesn’t support Landscape mode in a usable way.

title: Best budget app
content: While I’ve tried all other budget apps, this is by far the best out there. Very clean at reconciling and learning from past behaviors. I love that no matter what Harris Teeter grocery store I go to, it appears as Harris Teeter, not Harris Teeter store !785!, or whatever. The In My Pocket, which I wish they called, Left to Spend takes some time to learn, but it’s great once you do.   Only ask is try update the UI. While I’m not a fan of Mint, it looks much more current like my bank app. If you could update the fonts, get rid of the grey and use white with dark screen at night, that would be great!  Otherwise keep up the other updates. Five stars!

title: Sync Problems But Working Now
content: After problems syncing I got a quick response from the developer and it’s working great.  Went from a 1 star review to a 5.

title: Bogus app
content: I signed up for the plus membership so you have to pay the 9.99/month. After the first month they reset all the in-app features to basic subscription. Despite continuing to pay for the plus membership I was promted in the app to subscribe to the plus membership when I opened the app. I was also not given access to the premium features and a message would pop up saying I needed the plus membership to use those features. Definitely will NOT be recommending this app. It’s a scam.

title: Well…
content: I am not overly disappointed but disappointed all the same. This app offers all the same features my bank does. Only able to see reoccurring payments or transactions. And only able to use that data for bills. There isn’t a way to add other bills that are not automatically paid monthly. This will not work for my budget planning needs.   I do like how safe the app is with my data.

title: Android version runs faster
content: Great overall app. Coming from Samsung to the iPhone this app is a little annoying at times. Every time I go to the transactions list, it shows the animation for swiping and I have to wait for that before interacting. Then if I open one to change the category and save it, I’m back at the transactions screen and have to wait on the animation again. This didn’t happen on the android version and I could move much faster through the transactions.

title: FANTASTIC Budgeting App!!
content: This is an awesome app for keeping track of your finances! It’s very intuitive, and I love the zero-based budgeting approach. I also love that they offer a lifetime one-time purchase option for the premium version. This app has made managing my personal budget so much easier. I recommend this to anyone who is wanting to get a better grip on their monthly spending.

title: Best budgeting app by far
content: The only reason why Mint, YNAB, and the other budgeting apps with tens of thousands of reviews are rated so high is because those users have never tried this app. PocketGuard blows those apps out of the water with the ease of use and features.  The only thing missing is support for Apple Card but most apps don’t have that yet so no big deal.

title: There are better apps
content: Won’t work on desktop or any browser, you only can manage it through the app. Try Monarch

title: Great app
content: Use it everyday

title: Love this app!!
content: Absolutely love this app so far. There are a couple tweaks I would like to see, and the mobile navigation could have clearer paths to get to all the features, without having to just hunt all over, but overall it’s really great! I prefer using it on my desktop as I am more old school but the iPhone app works well when I am on the go.

title: No cancellations allowed on app
content: It takes an act of god to try to cancel your subscription

title: Changed My Life
content: I’ve used so many budgeting apps, and this is the first one that not only allowed me to understand my spending but also me to change my habits!! I swear by it.

title: Amex sync issues
content: Have to constantly sync amex multiple times daily. Don’t bother.

title: Eye Opener!
content: We are new to PocketGuard and while we are still learning we are astounded by it’s ease and love seeing everything in one place. Vlad at the help desk has been quick in response. We are on our way to staying within our budget since we can look quickly at all of our spending categories and see what we've spent so far each month!

title: Fraud
content: I paid $34.99 for the year subscription after the 30 trial it went back to basic stay away  Update Apple tried to get my money back and the developer refuse to give it back.

title: Not very impressed
content: Hi there, I’d canceled my pocket guard subscription and I’d prefer being taken off of the week trial fee as well.

title: Way too hard to set up
content: I’ve Ben trying to set up my budget for the past hour. It’s literally impossible. Despite having plenty of money in my accounts this stupid app thinks I’m -2,000 in my accounts.   Why does it think I will buy $1,000 worth of plane tickets every month just because i recently bought a plane ticket???  Why did it assume that cash i till out of an atn is a ‘recurring bill’??  The first time user experience is absolutely horrible. I was really exciting about automating my budgeting that I’ve been doing manually with another app; but this is impossible to set up!  This app needs a consultant to help the developers make it more ‘idiot proof’ because I’m so frustrated I’m about to give up and just delete it after less than an hour.

title: Spam
content: I just received an email stating I’ve been subscribed. I NEVER SUBSCRIBED!

title: 1 year subscription
content: Been using for about 1 year. I love the app. Took me a while to square my spending away, but this is a great app to help keep track.   Customer service is extremely helpful and very responsive. Highly recommend.

title: Overall great app, a few snags that almost seem deceptive
content: The ease of use and simplicity are impeccable. The app has great promise, but there are a few things that are not helpful: Account management- cannot clearly tell if you’re in the trial period or if you actually have the premium service. If you have the premium tier you can’t tell if you’re monthly or annual.   Bill name- cannot update the merchant name. I had to delete the bill and re- add it because I had a misspelled word.   Budget planning- my monthly paycheck comes at the end of the month and I use it to plan the next month. I can’t tell if the app recognizes that. It looks like it wants to count my March paycheck for March bills but the month is over. Thank you.

title: I live by this app
content: I have used every budgeting and spending app offered since 2003.  By far, this is the most straightforward and user friendly app I’ve used.  I hope it never goes away, I’ve paid for the premium version to get the absolute most out of the app.  My 81 year old mother now uses the app, she also loves it.    I reference the app multiple times a day, I can easily reference what bills are still outstanding without use of a calculator or downloading an excel file, although I can if needed.  I can easily show my husband our spending trends and cash flow.  I have gradually added more to the app and we are now tracking net worth.  It is a breeze.

title: Just no
content: The categories mix purchases into the billing category if you have both from the same company.  The Ipad version is a tiny screen iphone version. The  account worked for a while and is now broken.   You are much better off with a budgeting template for your favorite spreedsheet.  This is just half baked, occasionally functional and very frustrating to try to get to work.

title: No good
content: Downloaded pocket guard and input my income and expenses and when I got to the page where you can input your goals, it told me I did not have sufficient income even when my Income was 900 and my expenses were 700. Tried three times but got the same result. It said I needed more income and it gave me a negative amount. No good. I deleted the app.

title: The bugs, slowness, and lack of reliability aren’t worth it
content: This app is a really cool idea and if it worked well I’d continue my paid subscription. However, there are a couple big issues:  - It’s really slow - almost unusable. This seems newer. When I first started using it it wasn’t this slow. Just scrolling through transactions is so tedious because it freezes and then scrolls way further than you want  - It doesn’t always catch when your accounts are out out of date or not updating. For example, I have one account that just won’t seem to update any transactions from the last 6 months but PocketGuard isn’t showing any errors with the connection. This type of ‘silent’ failure to update really takes away from the value  because I can’t trust what I see in the app. -There also seems to be pretty frequent errors with accounts where I have to remove and re-add them or re-enter credentials. This is probably more related to the external accounts and their security but it’s still annoying.   All in all, I find myself using the actual bank apps more than PocketGuard due to these issues even though I’d prefer to have it all in one place and use PocketGuard.

title: Love this app!!
content: This app has been exactly what I’ve been looking for when it comes to budgeting. I love that I can see my spending patterns on a monthly basis too. I did decide to purchase the lifetime option, and love that I can change transaction dates (especially for end of the month transactions) creating my own categories, and being able to split my transactions. It gives me a much more clear and accurate view of my spending. The hashtags has been great too so if I’m paying via credit card I can know what that specific I transaction was for. All in all, I love this app!

title: Too many bugs.  Poor support.
content: This app has potential but it’s so flawed at this point that it’s virtually useless.  Many many transactions are duplicates so your budget updates are always wrong.  Some transactions are repeated two and three times.  I written to the support email several times but I always get the same bot response.  These developers have a good idea but a terrible execution.  Which is too bad.  I really wanted a portable budget app that gave me ACCURATE updates on my spending.  This app does the very opposite.

title: Limited
content: There’s no way to view pervious months budgets. Also, how do you save for things like car insurance that’s paid every six months? Support said to make a manual saving goal but because it looks like my budget is overdrawn from car insurance I can’t make any savings goals until my budget is balanced!   I like that I can customize categories. Syncing with bank is nice but takes several minutes to sync just a few transactions.

title: Good app
content: It is being very helpful in tracking expenses. The only downside is that it runs 1-2 days behind the time of the actual transactions. By the time the weekend is over and transactions load on Monday night or Tuesday, it’s hard to remember what we spent on Friday and why. I wish it was more real time, like a banking app.  However, I think for the most part, it is helping us.

title: App not updating account info automatically
content: Every day when I open the app I have to manually remind the app to refresh my bank account data to the current day. It used to automatically update around 5am daily. Also, it’s taking longer and longer (upwards of 3-5 minutes) for the data from the bank to cross over to the app. This used to happen within a few seconds. I have downloaded the most current version with the same issue.

title: Just get it!
content: Best budget app I have found. I have been using this for several years now.

title: Search transactions time range
content: Great job, this app is a great. I will like to request the developer to allow more flexibility when searching for transactions out merchants. It only allows up to 5 months. Some of us need up to a year. Thanks 🙏🏼

title: Signing Up
content: You can't sign up using only your email address, it has to be LinkedIn, Google or Apple. Feels very intrusive, I'm deleting it before even using it because of this.

title: This app isn’t ready to go to market
content: I constantly have to contact support to get missing transactions to show up in this app.  This app is supposed to make budgeting easier, but as of right now it’s too glitchy and unreliable to do that.

title: Could be better
content: Biggest complaint is the frustratingly long time it takes to update your accounts. It takes days for it to reflect past transactions whether they’re income or expenses.   The app itself offers plenty of features but it’s not very user friendly. Adding some tutorials would be nice. Getting rid of the Find Savings tab would be nice as well. Overall this app just throws a lot of information at you and doesn’t really show you how any of it is connected very well for you to actually manage your budget properly. You’ll find yourself trying to go back and forth between tabs and various options just to do a simple task.

title: Terrible
content: I paid for the lifetime and wasted my money. On the snowball debit plan … if your credit card company doesn’t participate in plaid you can’t do it. The only way to add it to your debit snowball plan is to add it as a cash account. And then the app thinks you have that money available to spend. I want to pay my credit cards down and can not use a credit card to pay another credit card. Which is what the debit snowball thinks you can do. SMH if I could I would give this a 0 for a review

title: Can’t link accounts
content: Tried linking my credit union. Got a text with verification number. App tries to connect with my correct log in but fails. App fails to allow user to enter verification text info as a scree never asks. App fails to allow user to connect credit union…tries to connect then fails. Look around, there are apps that are much more “user-friendly” and work.

title: Just borderline useless
content: They also send you unwanted emails, as many as they can! With no way to unsubscribe :)

title: The best budgeting app
content: I’ve literally never written a review for an app before, but I had to because I felt so strongly about the quality of this app. I used mint for a long time bc it was free and got the job done, but recently, Mint stopped supporting my bank (USAA). So, I was on the market for a new budgeting app and stumbled upon PocketGuard. I have to say, I’m extremely impressed. I love the ability to save for my goals without having to think about it. I love how it calculates my estimated monthly income so that I don’t have to do the mental math when it comes to budgeting. I love the notifications it gives me when I spend too much on a particular category. I love the customizable budget categories (not an option under Mint). This is truly the greatest budgeting app I’ve ever used, and I’ve been budgeting my money very persistently for about a decade now. Also, the customer service is probably the best I’ve ever come into contact with, across any business or platform. You have a question? Email them and you’ll get a response back within 24 hours. In fact I emailed them once with a question and received a response back within 30 minutes. Overall, this is a fantastic budgeting app and I couldn’t recommend it more.

title: Great Overall
content: Overall I love this app- once I figured out how to use all its functions, it’s easy to maintain and keep track of expenses and budgeting.   The main change that I’d love to see to the app is having a way to track infrequent large expenses that don’t fit neatly into budgets such as car maintenance, emergencies, yearly vet visits, etc. I’ve used this app for over a year and don’t see the need to change anytime soon!

title: Could be amazing
content: Macro vs Micro - App focuses on month to month budgeting, you can not future budget ahead, only for the month you are in. Would be great if we can get a more holistic view of financials over a given period and get more macro data. What does that past year look like? 6 months? What about the next 6 months? Trends and projections would be powerful.   Goals is messed up. I want to set up goals but not have it pull from “In My Pocket”  Also, it takes a very long time for my bank to sync. It’s been 17 days since my it has updated. I’ve reconnected and refreshed many times. We need better connectivity and near-real time syncs.   I bank with Lending Club and I was told the Native connection does not work and have to use Plaid which is suboptimal.

title: Great app!
content: As helpful as you make it, this app allows user to easily create and edit categories in order to track spending patterns. Exactly what my family needs!

title: Only 3 Third Party Providers Available for Signup
content: There’s currently only LinkedIn (???), Google, and Apple. Get using a 3rd party for security reasons, but don’t understand why you can’t just add Microsoft and/or just add MFA. Was excited about using this, but not going to signup until more options are added. Disappointed.

title: 0 if I had the option
content: There was supposed to be a 7 day free trial if you chose to try the app... I tried but had issues connecting my bank (not their fault). So I decided to delete my account and cancel the subscription, then come to find out that even though I had the app for 2 days I was charged the full year's price. Very nice of an app to do that claims to want to help you manage your money.. 🤮

title: Poor UX Design
content: I like the concept and visual design of the app but where it is lacking is the intuitive design. When I try to mark a bill as paid, it should be easy but it isn’t. A pop up appears telling me to create a new bill which is redundant. Canceling this subscription.

title: Don’t waste your money
content: This app shows u where to go in ur phone to delete / cancel membership they don’t do it for you biggest scam YouTube shows you that for free come on y’all

content: I paid for plus to be able to access the debt payoff plan. I’ve added a few accounts, but am no longer able to add credit cards or loans. The whole point of the payoff plan is to help me understand the order in which to payoff debts by using snowball or avalanche method through the app. I’m not able to get the full picture since I cannot add all my accounts to compare APRs and balances. Continually getting error codes 170, 940, and “contact your administrator if error continues” errors.

title: Can’t sign up with a e-mail.
content: There is only three choices of how to sign up for this. I don’t wanna sign up with a third party company. I want to sign up with a email other then the companies you have chosen. I guess I’ll go with someone else that will let me.

title: Great app
content: Visually appealing and easy to understand your spending. Easy to categorize spending and add income. I’ve been looking for an app like this for a while and am glad I found this. I like the pie chart feature and how up to date my accounts are. Please stay around to use forever! 😂

title: When you need a budget but don’t want to pay an arm and leg
content: Good value and does a lot but definitely a little hard transitioning from YNAB to this. One of my most missed features is sharing the budget with a partner- I haven’t figured out how to do this or if this is a supported feature yet.

title: Handy app, super-responsive customer service
content: I’ve been loving the app.  Super-easy to use.  Handy budgeting and categorization of expenses.  And the customer service is top-notch!

title: Pretty good…. Could be great
content: I really want to love this app, but the thought of onboarding all of my info from my cell phone gives me great pause. I would love to be able to set everything up from my computer then monitor and make adjustments from my phone. It is a great app full of useful features. I will still use it for a while.

title: Way better than mint
content: Tried using mint but it would never sync quickly with my bank and the layout wasn’t very intuitive.  Been using PocketGuard for about a month now and absolutely love it. It syncs with all my accounts super quickly and has a ton of customization options for your budget that make it super easy to track any sort of spending.

title: Wish it were cheaper.
content: We love it. I just wish it were a little cheaper, and maybe had its own built in savings. And I little easier to understand. New at this still- we’ll get there!

title: Exactly what I need
content: Finally! An app that let’s me track my expenses real time…and accurately! I have tried 14 other budgeting apps in the last year and each one had something buggy about it, or the process flow didn’t make sense. I used to use Mint but there are too many problems with syncing transactions, etc. This app does all the things I expected the other apps to do and has other cute features (icons for each budget). I’m sticking with this one from now on. After playing with it for a few hours I bought the annual subscription which is reasonable compared to the other apps I’ve tried. My only request is that the Spending and Budgeting screen should be easier to get to once the app opens, since I use it daily to make sure I’m staying within each budget category.

title: 10xs better than Mint
content: Mint was so frustrating because transactions took forever to update and would continuously have to remap accounts and reassign transactions.

title: Seems like a useful app
content: Seems like a useful app but I wouldnt know bc I haven’t been able to connect to my bank for weeks. Ive tried contacting the support team like 4 times and no response. Boooooo. Will just delete.

title: We se real result in our bottom line
content: Easy interface, effective expense tracking. Incredibly valuable to organize our family's financials. Great work, developers!

title: Close, but no Cigar.
content: This app looks like it has everything I want. Then when installing, and reinstalling, and again reinstalling, it wouldn’t set up my income correctly. No amount of troubleshooting or FAQs could fix the problem, so it looks like I’ll be moving on to a different app.

title: Neat, but start using on the 1st of the month
content: So far, the app looks like it can be super helpful. Unfortunately, it’s super difficult for me to start using in the middle because the app starts your budget over at the beginning of each month. So if you’re jumping in midway through a month, it’s hard to figure out how to give the app insight into your current financial status. To avoid a headache, I recommend starting to use the app at the beginning of a month so you can work from a clean slate.

title: Disturbing account creation
content: App and website did not allow me to create account with my own username and password. Do not want to log in with LinkedIn, Google, or Apple.

title: Cannot connect to my PayPal Debit Card?
content: Would have given a 5 Star if all my accounts would connect.

title: Awesome budget planner
content: I kept talking about keeping a budget for years but kept making excuses. I originally installed mint, but as pleasing to the eye as it is, it is not as simple and intuitive as I'd like and months passed without recording anything. So when I decided to finally start, I deleted the app and looked again and this Budget Planner was my first choice. I was surprised by how quick and easy it is to use, intuitive, with a customizable yet simple interface, and mostly, informative. Easily budget customizing, custom finance categories implemented, subscription-manager, expense tracker, the app works like a switherland clock. Pocketguard is an extremely good budget planner for everyday

title: Good app. Missing iPad support.
content: Also historical net worth is often wrong. Rest is great.

title: New User, Planning on Staying Awhile
content: *UPDATE* Been using the app for a few months now and multiple transactions from my citi card are frequently missing. It is an ongoing support issue that has yet to be fixed and makes the app useless.   I’ve tried multiple other apps for budgeting (Mint, YNAB, Quickbook, etc.) but found most to be either too complicated or more focused on working down debt. I wanted something that could: sync my accounts, keep track of transactions, and help me limit spending on different categories- and this app has been perfect for that.   Positives: Learning to use the app has been quick and easy, able to add multiple bank accounts, credit card payments are automatically excluded from calculations which helps organize transactions, easy to re-label transactions to different budgets, I can see the free version being sufficient for a lot of users, paid version is a reasonable one time fee instead of a yearly subscription.   Critiques: Would prefer the “spending & budgets” category as a tab on the bottom instead of the “find savings” tab (which is basically an ad you can’t get rid of even with a paid account), difficult to set up multiple “goals” if you only have one savings account, only able to set a budget for a month- would be great to set a yearly budget for big things like travel, home improvement, etc.,  difficulty adding one of my bank accounts (resolved by adding through website instead of mobile app), and this is very minor but aesthetics are a little dated. Being able to choose your own colors, light vs dark mode, updated icons, etc. could really go a long way.   Overall, I highly recommend this app and am planning on staying with it for the foreseeable  future.

title: Great, but has a few issues
content: I love using PocketGuard for tracking my day to day spending and making sure I have enough to cover my bills. It’s fairly intuitive and is better for day to day tracking than things like personal capital.   However, there are a couple things that don’t work quite right or as expected.   Firstly, pending transaction are taken out of your “pocket” but can’t be modified or attributed to bills. It can take quite a while for some transactions to be marked as cleared, which means that often times my “pocket” is wildly inaccurate, since it’s counting large bills like my rent effectively twice. That kind of defeats the purpose of the tool.   Secondly (and this may have more to do with the financial institution), but there are certain accounts that are listed as addable, but simple aren’t. My savings account, for example, hasn’t been able to sync for 6 months and the error is just a vague “something went wrong.” Mind you it syncs fine on other budgeting apps. So that’s disappointing.

title: It’s great
content: I really like this app. It has really helped us see where our money is going.   I do wish their was an option to turn off auto categorizing of transactions. I find myself searching all transactions for errors almost daily. If i could turn it off I could rest comfortably knowing they we’re always correct.  For example, we sometimes buy gas at a location and sometimes we just stop in for a drink. The app puts this stores purchases in one category always.  Not a big problem, can just be time consuming.  The app is completely worth it regardless.

title: Hi it great!
content: Please do not install this app! It took me over 2 years to stop the spying and malware this app causes!

title: Can’t create an account
content: I was really excited to start using the app. I go in to create an account and the only two options are to use google or apple to sign in. Both times it responded with error insecure password. It would be fine if I could just make an account through the app. Very frustrating.

title: Love this app
content: I absolutely love this app. I have been using the free option and it does so much. If you are wanting to set goals or attach receipts then you would need to get the plus but honestly it’s really inexpensive.

title: Best finance tracking app I’ve had
content: It’s a pretty great app! I am terrible with money and this has made it A LOT EASIER to track my expenses  and see where my money goes. And it’s been pretty revealing!  It’s made a huge differences in how and where I spend my money! Am gonna use this app for a long time going forward!

title: Pretty Slick
content: Wish the one time payment wasn’t so expensive though.

title: Almost perfect
content: This app was almost the white unicorn of budgeting tools I always wanted. Unfortunately the lack of one feature makes it unusable for myself and my family and that is manually entered transactions to be reconciled.   Other apps allow you to enter a transaction when it occurs, and will either automatically reconcile it from the bank if it matches, or give you the option to reconcile itself.   This app requires the transaction to clear the bank first, which can sometimes take days. The app implies that it’s showing you your actual working balance sans upcoming bills, but a holiday weekend of transactions hitting on a Tuesday will show you it was way off.   Fix that flaw and I’m a lifetime subscriber, but until then I have to use something else.

title: So useful!
content: This app has made it so easy to see where our money has gone and is going to go. My new husband and I decided to share accounts and we were struggling to relax into that after independently controlling our finances for so long… this has made it so much easier! I had to contact customer support one time and they were incredibly prompt and helpful. I knocked off a star because I wish it was able to do the following (but would have only knocked off only half a star if it was an option):  1) I wish you could choose to carry over unspent budgets to the next month. ie If I underspend this month on ‘home’, the budget is bigger the following month to purchase a more expensive item.  2) I wish it could learn and adapt. We pay two bills to Banfield Pet Plan each month that come up as BP. When we buy gas from BP, it goes into bills because it think it’s the same. So a couple of times a month, I have to manuallly change names and categories - sometimes I have to re-enter the banfield bills and then, when they are paid, they don’t register as the ones planned. This is a niche and minor issue but slightly annoying nonetheless.  3) I wish it was a little more prompt in identifying new transactions. Sometimes the banking app will detail transactions as no longer pending and it’ll take a day or two for them to appear on PocketGuard.  These are minor things that I’d like the developers to consider BUT overall I love this app!

title: Helpful App, I just don’t use it as often
content: I don’t have anything negative to say about the app, it works as efficiently as the person feeding it information and making adjustments here and there.   It’s smart, but certain things have to be edited by you, which is completely expected.   If I start using it more diligently, I may even like it more than I do.

title: We love it!
content: My husband and I love this app so much! ❤️ It helps us keep track of our finances and unwanted subscriptions. We will continue to use this app from here on out for our household

title: Won’t connect
content: Seems like a great app. Won’t stay connected to Citi so a bit useless for me.

title: Very good
content: I have enjoyed using this app. Their are a few problems with keeping accounts from not working at times but every one of these apps have the same problem. This has been my best experience with a budgeting app so far.  Helps me keep track of spending and gives me great insight and capabilities with tracking my budget.

title: Very good app

Super easy the way I have it set up, on the overview page I have a section that includes all my fixed costs for the month, easy to see and easy to categorize. Makes it super easy to budget what I have left over. - hashtags.I love the hashtags, never been easier to see how much I spent on back to school stuff , on my recent vacation, etc. -Love the easy comparison from one month to the next to see if I spent more than less than the previous month in a particular category. title: It had so much potential…
content: What attracted me to this app was that it would tell you how much money you have left over after all your expenses were paid.  I had hoped this would be the one and only budgeting app I would ever need.  Well where do I start? First off, while it automatically updates my chase bank info, it doesn’t automatically update my Navy FCU. I have request a code, then wait for this app to let me enter the code which takes at least a minute. Once it has the code then it takes about 20 seconds or more to update.  All other apps continue to sync whereas PocketGuard gets amnesia. This is a big fail which the company really needs to work on.  The second issue I have is the app predicting how much and when my next paycheck will be. I get paid by the law firm on the 15th and 30th of every month but if the day falls on a weekend then I’m paid on the Friday or Monday. You can’t program the app to adjust for this. Second, hours paid changes depending how many days are in a month. I.E. 30 vs 31st vs 28. While my hours are consistent, the payout varies according to the calendar. Simply put, some pay periods have one extra day or less a day or even. This app doesn’t account for those variations or allow to to program that algorithm.  In comparison to Mint, Experian, NerdWallet, and WalletHub, PocketGuard ranks in the bottom of my list. So far down the list in that when I’m done with this review, I will delete it and not recommend it to anyone.

title: Going on 2+ years: you will not regret
content: Let me tell you- all of the previous reviews are old. I’ve been on this app for the since 2019 & will honestly be here until I die. Hoping it lasts that long. 🙏🏽 I’ve been searching for a way to understand my spendings between categories, month over month & watching my budget. This is everything & more. I love the personalization that I can add my own catergories, mark a specific merchant as something once and never have to touch it again & even exclude things like transactions between my accounts. This is the app if you’re anal about how you spend your money & it even helps if I want to budget for let’s say shopping. I love it. Please note I am a premium user & to me it’s worth it. But I’m sure the free version is equally as good. The other apps mint, your bank, random ones only work if you have a goal. But for me, I want to know where, what & compare my spendings month over month so I can see how I’m doing. Or if I need to stop spending!   Anyway highly recommend. And two last things- 1) they’re IT or support literally responds within 48 hours. You’re never left hanging and no question is stupid. 2) the app is constantly evolving. It’s not the same as it was two years ago, it’s better! If there’s a bug, report it! If you have a suggestion, suggest it! I love all the latest updates & it really helps me think of how I’m spending my money which was my ultimate goal. Thank you!!

title: I want to love this app but transactions are too slow
content: I reaallly want this app to be my go to budgeting tool. It has the best UI/UX of any app I’ve ever tried, it’s so great to use. But unfortunately it just doesn’t sync up with your card transactions very well.   I have “pending transactions” from over a week ago that are definitely not pending anymore on my credit card. It also labels pending purchases with the incorrect vendor. I think PocketGuard has trouble with transactions that have tips? For example I went to a restaurant a week ago, but PocketGuard still says it’s pending and has the wrong merchant. It seems to mix up the merchant with previous purchases. Along with this, it’s missing some transactions from last week.  Mint doesn’t have this issue, all my transactions are there, none of them are incorrectly labeled as pending, and all the vendors are accurate.  There’s so many thing PocketGuard does right, but I can’t justify using it for budgeting when the transactions take forever to correct itself. I would gladly pay for a subscription if this wasn’t an issue. When it works, it works really well.   Maybe I’ll try again in a couple of months and see if anything improves. I really hope it does!!

title: Not as good as mint
content: This program is difficult to use. My wife and I both use it on our joint account, but our “in my pocket” amount rarely matches. It jumps around wildly over the course of the day as well so we literally never know how much we have. It’s difficult to figure out how to handle things like using your bonus from last month since finances reset every month. It’s also difficult to figure out how to handle periodic expenses.   Mint tells you how much you have left and how many days remain, so while it doesn’t give you a “daily number” you can easily divide cash remaining by days remaining. Mints balance matches for my wife and I and doesn’t have wild swings throughout the day. We feel much more confident using that program which just very simple math without any weird issues. It’s easy to see where money is and where it went.  I can not recommend this program.

title: The worst bill tracker app available

Why do I have to stay on that screen. If I leave, the app times out and I have to start over, staring at a grey screen wasting my life. title: Monthly: Expenses vs Income
content: I rarely write reviews for apps, but I felt this one deserved it. One of the biggest shortcomings is the lack of a simple monthly income vs. expense summary. I shouldn’t have to view my finances in three-month increments just to understand how I did in a single month. I want to be able to see exactly how much I earned, how much I spent, and what my net total was for that month. As a paid subscribed user, I expected much more user-friendly financial reporting. The data is there, but it’s not presented in a way that’s easy to understand or useful for managing my finances. A simple monthly cash flow summary and customizable reporting would make a huge difference.

content: Dave Ramsey, the founder of EveryDollar, has publicly expressed support for both Donald Trump and Israel.While the software product EveryDollar itself is an automated financial tracking tool without explicit political or geopolitical programming, its parent company (Ramsey Solutions) and its CEO hold clear public positions.

title: Limited
content: This ap is great as a budgeting tool. I don’t like that if I manually enter a debit or credit then it will duplicate and not match it when my bank feeds come through. This is a serious flaw if I’m supposed to know exactly what I’m spending! It also doesn’t have a normal ledger. It tracks the budget for the month and it shows transactions but it doesn’t show a running balance. I don’t like that. I left Quicken Online for the same reason. Our account just for our family expenses was all I needed to track in here and it was set up to track EVERYTHING. I didn’t appreciate the rigidity.

title: Truly the best

title: I used to use this app…and now I can again!

It’s great to see where expenses are piling up that I didn’t even realize before. Thank you Ramsey Solutions!  I knew you’d make it work.  I didn’t expect it to be fun

title: Game Changer
content: Utilizing EveryDollar with the Ramsey plan helped up pay off $34,000 in car debt in just 6 months and stop asking the question, “where is all of our money going?” We now see where we spend each month, set spending boundaries, and are seeing real progress with our money goals. All of this while also taking a $30k pay cut to do full time ministry. We are very thankful for EveryDollar and the Ramsey team!

title: Account syncing is broken
content: Some banks and accounts are not supported. When some banks are supported but experience significantly or frequent issues, the support team blame the bank and suggest switching banks. The app frequently pulls in duplicate transactions that have to be cleaned up every day. The app uses Plaid which doesn’t allow individual connections, such as mfa for me and mfa for my spouse for the same bank. If a phone number is removed from one bank that syncs through plaid, it removes the phone number for all banks that have synced through plaid. Line items cannot be moved between categories and if you’ve created a line item within one category you cannot recreate it in another category, even after deleting the first.

title: Never too old

A budget is not about restricting freedom. It is about telling your money where to go instead of wondering where it went. 💰👍

title: Game changer

Before starting this journey we had mounds of credit card debit, car loans, student loan debt for my son, and a mortgage.  We have been completely debt free including the mortgage for 5 years.    We have a net worth of $ 1.5 million and will be able to retire early in 10 years.  The small amount I pay every year for this app lets me see in real time where every cent is going and keeps me on track.   Because of the plan and the app, we were able to completely pay for both of our kids’ post secondary educations, help pay for their weddings, pay off and do great upgrades to our house, and enjoy yearly vacations with our family. title: LOVE the app…BUT
content: I love the app nothing else like it on the market especially the recent new clarity update BUT one thing I do suggest in the “income scheduling” section. I don’t always want to evenly split up my amounts for a budgeted item. I want to pay  different amounts on different dates, and I can’t do that. It causes me to pick a date for all of it that isn’t technically the budget I’m following, or pick dates with even splits I’m not technically following.   Manual fix: I create extra line items example “Tithe 1” & “Tithe 2” and “Tithe 3” because the amount I give for Tithe varies based on income (especially in entrepreneurship)  Which means I have to set up a “Net Pay Week 1”, “Net Pay Week 2”etc.    And when I do this instead of monthly income on one line and Tithe on one line my budget ends up so cluttered with lots of line items for the same thing at different dates….or wrong dates and wrong allocated amounts if I just pick one neutral day for all of it. I want the scheduler to spend how I’m spending my money otherwise the idea doesn’t help: don’t know where I’m over budget!

title: Easy to use.
content: I’ve been using this app for easily over 5 years now, and I love it. It’s easy to use, and I like the free version because when I started using it I was able to build a habit of tracking my expenses by typing them in myself. I had the paid version where it pulled my bank charges over, but I found for myself that having to manually enter my transactions when I bought something helped me to stay on budget and really feel the weight of every dollar I spent. I highly recommend this, as budgeting changed my life, and when/if I ever have kids they will only ever know the Ramsey Way. Debt free, investing, and living within my means.

title: Split broken, transfer needed
content: The split function for transactions is somewhat broken. It will accept it if you input the correct amounts but it will no longer do the assist in helping you input the remaining amount for the split.   Also in order to do transfers from one account to another i have to do a convoluted process to make it work because there is no transfer function. Like, if i have money in my savings account that I want to use for groceries, or baby things or anything like that I have to do an expense from the one account and an income into budget item i want to use. To put the money back however i can’t just do that in reverse… i have to expense from my checking and income into my savings, but the same budget item… then go to the budget section and have that same amount be in the planned amount to put in the budget line item in order for both my accounts to balance as well as the paycheck planner/balance of that savings budget item be correct.   Thats a whole lot of hoops to jump through for a function that 99.99% of other budgeting apps have as a function by default.   Also in order to see the updated amount in my accounts i need to exit and re enter the app. Ive seen a lot of improvements in this app since ive begun using it, but it still needs work.

title: User friendly, but slow

I end up having to use separate applications and notes to keep track of current expenses and budgets, and if I’m going to do that…. Then why have the dang app anyway? This would be a 5/5 app if they could just get the transactions to load into their system even within 24 hours. I hope they make these changes moving forward, because with the way the app is now, I honestly can’t recommended it to anyone.

title: Great concept, but poor account syncing.
content: I really wanted to love EveryDollar because the layout is clean, the budgeting system is simple, and the sinking fund feature is excellent. That sinking fund option is actually the main reason I started using this app. It makes it so easy to plan ahead for irregular expenses and stay organized.  But the constant account disconnections make it incredibly frustrating to use. I have four connected accounts, and they disconnect all the time. I’m constantly logging into my bank accounts separately just to make sure transactions actually went through. When the accounts disconnect, reconnecting them is a hassle and often forces me to recheck or redo parts of the entire month.  I ended up canceling my paid subscription because the connected account feature just wasn’t reliable enough to justify the cost. I switched to the free version, but then I was flooded with ads. Now I’m essentially paying for the subscription again just to avoid ads while still having to manually enter all of my transactions.  If the bank connections were stable and dependable, this would easily be a 5 star app. The budgeting tools, especially sinking funds, are strong. But until the syncing is reliable, it creates more work than it should.

title: Free Version
content: I really enjoy this app for its simplicity and customizability. It’s pretty bare bones, but you don’t need much if you are already fiscally responsible and just need a tracker. However, there’s one element that absolutely drives me bonkers: the funds. I understand the purpose of the planned category; that’s not my issue. Whenever you log a transaction against the fund, it updates the balance as expected (positive or negative). But It also updates the total remaining amount to spend for the entire monthly budget, and it drives me bonkers! For example, if I log an unexpected $1000 charge against my emergency fund (25k total), that fund will be updated to $24k but the monthly budget will say I’m $1k overbudget. Same thing if I have an unexpected windfall of $5000 that I add to the fund; it’ll say I have $5000 more to spend for that month. It can make it really confusing because I just want a snapshot of how I’m doing for the month excluding extraneous transactions. I just wish it would keep funds separate. I just log my savings as a line item and then do the funds in a spreadsheet because it’s so frustrating, Some additional graphs in the free tier would be a nice update too. (And it seems to be available in other free apps). For example, you can see the pie chart split by category for the current month (housing, lifestyle, etc) but you currently can’t scroll back to previous months. I can’t say if there are more features with the paid version, but these elements stood out to me.

title: Very simple application to use
content: I enjoy using this app, which I open almost every day. I've been an on-and-off budgeter for most of my life and haven't been very consistent. For years, I've maintained a semi-up-to-date budget using spreadsheets and tried several budgeting apps. However, this is by far the easiest one I've used for zero-based budgeting. I started using it a couple of months ago and figured everything out by watching one of their webinars. After spending a few hours setting it up, I felt very comfortable using it.   Pro:   It's a straightforward app to use, and the concepts of budgeting are straightforward. It focuses solely on budgeting, whereas other apps I used try to incorporate all of your accounts, account balances, including investment accounts, which complicates things if you only want to budget.   This app is very forgiving if you make a mistake, miscategorize something, or delete something. It's super easy to fix any errors. The interface and reports are simple to understand, allowing you to adjust your spending effectively.  Cons: The cost of the app is on the expensive side considering its simplicity of features. The only premium feature I use is transaction import, and it doesn't feel worth the premium price. I'd rather pay for the features I use than a set early price for all the stuff I don't use.   I didn't have any debt and have always lived within my means while saving well. My goal was to identify areas for improvement (particularly around monthly subscriptions) and budget better for long-term spending, like trips and remodels, while cutting back on eating out. I don't really need the coaching or baby steps, as I was already on step 6 when I started using the app.   This app imports all transactions but is primarily designed for debit card or cash users. I use a credit card and pay it off monthly, so features like the paycheck planner are irrelevant to me. I found it tricky to account for transfers, like my monthly credit card payment. I had to create a transfer budget item to track both the debit and the credit. I always have a weird zero-out line item every month, which feels clunky.   When doing your monthly reconciliation, it can be challenging to zoom in on a micro level to analyze spending patterns. For example, if you categorize all your subscriptions together—such as Spotify, Hulu, Netflix, etc.—they will only show up as "Subscriptions." You then need to click on a line item to view the individual transactions, which can be cumbersome.   I found it beneficial to break down all my subscription items into individual items rather than lumping them together into a single category. This allowed me to identify and cancel about five subscriptions quickly. I've been bad about canceling unused subscriptions in the past. This method is straightforward, allowing you to quickly review each month to determine if it's worth keeping them. That's the coaching item that would be useful in the app, helping with spending habits and transaction analysis.   Overall, I do recommend this app; it's excellent for first-time budgeting or people who want only a 'budgeting' app with no fancy financial/account balance/retirement management features.

title: Android Vs Iphone
content: I bought the app when I had an Android back in 2020, and I have been using it since then. I’ve not synced my accounts because I closely monitor my spending and like to catch any ghost charges or upcharges from companies. This means I manually enter all my transactions.  The reviews:  The app for iPhone is not as user-friendly as it is on Android.  > The Account Window View:  The account window view is different. On Android, you have all the accounts displayed in a vertical view with two columns, and you can see all your accounts on one screen. On iPhone, the view is horizontal, and you can only see the accounts in pairs of four, which is not convenient for users with multiple accounts. It would be nice to have the option to choose how you want the account view to appear.  > Entering Records:  While both versions have their advantages, the iPhone version does not memorizes payers. On an Android device, this saves time. Additionally, when entering receipts, Android allows you to crop the image to your liking, but iPhone does not.  One thing I like about the iPhone version is the planned payment window. I find it easier to access via the bottom menu.  I’m still acclimating to iPhone OS for this app, as I’ve invested so many years into using it and am not planning to switch to another wallet anytime soon. However, I would love to see these changes.  My recommendation for new users: Search around to see if there are more user-friendly apps that offer easy access and a more intuitive environment.  > My suggestion for this app:  Make it AI-powered to read receipts and create records simply by taking a picture of the receipt. This would be a game changer.

I’ve also reported several issues with the formatting which is inconsistent throughout the app. In some place commas and decimals are used and some not. Some places list the currency and some not. When I put in a ticket for this, support made it sound like I’m crazy and that there is no priority to have consistent currency formatting throughout the app. This app feels like a beta and isn’t polished enough for serious use.   Update: after a year of nothing being fixed, I lowered my rating and that caught the developers attention. They finally responded to my support ticket and addressed a few of the issues, but still refuse to fix some of the others like listing amounts as “USD 89.1” instead of “$89.10” to follow proper US formatting.   Re: developer response - you can “acknowledge” these issues all you want, but until the issues are resolved, I am not increasing my rating and will not be recommending this app to others.

title: No Cash App or Crypto
content: I am not sure if the premium version has the features I am discussing below, I am on the free version.   I downloaded this because I read a) I could upload bank statements if my bank didn’t link and one of my accounts is Cash App, which never does (side note: I don’t think this app uses Plaid, which gave me hope but whatever linking platform it uses also doesn’t accept it) and b) that I could track investments. Robinhood connected (after four attempts) but my investments didn’t show. I had to manually input each stock, the quantity I own, and current price to track them. It also doesn’t track any crypto you hold. So I can’t track my crypto holdings, it doesn’t automatically sync my stock investments (just the current prices multiplied by what I own, not if I buy or sell-that’s also manual), can’t track my usage of anything on Cash App.   Also, you can set bills as “planned payments” but can’t pay partially on them/set money aside out of your account (on paper) for them. If I pay a bill in the transaction record, it doesn’t mark it in “planned payments”, even if you’ve set the payee as a “rule”. You have to go into the planned payments portion of the app and do it from there. You also can’t pay a partially amount; it either marks it paid or not paid, after which you cannot edit the bill for that month.   Also…you can’t split categories for expenses. Spend $100 at the grocery store, $50 for groceries and $50 on pet food? Can only choose one category.   BeeWallet doesn’t have as nice of a user interface but it has bill tracking and the ability to split categories and that’s the app I ended up sticking with. It gives all the same metrics (maybe more). If you don’t have a lot of bills (which I’m sure you do if you’re downloading a tracking app), care about investments or crypto, don’t have a cash app and never buy things in different categories at once, this is the app for you.

Something that wasn’t clear before I bought it and an obvious win for a budgeting app!  When I sent a request about this, I haven’t received a reply after a day. At their subscription rate, either subscription sharing or a faster customer support (or both) should be warranted, in my opinion, small team or not…  Second, less than a month after I signed up for Premium, both of my banks disappeared from the syncing feature - basically making the app’s service much less convenient.  I can’t totally blame the app for this as my banks may be more restrictive or whatnot, but there was no warning, explanation or info about it.   Their refund policy is very strict, so now it seems I’m stuck with a mostly useless subscription for 75% of the time I bought it for.   It would be really hard for me to recommend the add-on service given my experience, but it is a well-built app with a very nice function and interface.

title: Annoying to use
content: I had high hopes for this app because I’m tired of manually tracking all of my expenses. But after trying to use this app for a few months I’m going back to manually tracking.  First off, the free version doesn’t let you connect bank accounts which was the whole point I got the app. So I payed for wallet premium so I could connect my credit cards and checking account.   After connecting my accounts, I started going through and categorizing my expenses 1 by 1. Everything was working pretty well at first.  But after a couple of weeks both my credit card and checking account connections had errors. I tried reconnecting them but I kept getting a ‘connection failed’ error. I contacted support and they said to go disconnect the accounts and reconnect them again.  This worked which was great. The problem is that all of the transactions from the previous connected accounts were still there so now all of my transactions were doubled up and I had to go through and delete them 1 by 1.  Once again my accounts were working and everything was setup. But I checked my account today and both of my accounts have connection errors once again and reconnecting them isn’t working. After 3 tries of hassling with this, I’ve finally given up. I can’t stay with an app that I constantly have to fight to keep working.  Also, the app itself keeps signing me out of my account so I have to sign in almost every time I want to check on it so that’s pretty annoying too.  Oh, and you can’t connect your brokerage accounts/investment accounts.

So the feature to select the start and end date is already there, which is great. I just wish theres a way to change the date once, instead of every single time. so basically set a specific period (like I can already do) but then you can add an option to make that period the ((default)) that shows on the overview, and removes the need to go to show more and change it agin and again. title: Revised review— Easy to use, responsive developer
content: After paying for a lifetime license, I accidentally deleted my account. I misunderstood the process of recovering my account and out of frustration posted a negative review here. The developer graciously and promptly responded to my review causing me to have a lightbulb moment and realize how easy it was to fix the issue. Accordingly it is only fair that I post a revised review.  I chose this app after testing out and discarding many other similar apps on the App Store. This app checked all the right boxes for me— nice aesthetics, ease of use, multiple currencies, informative charts, ability to import data from another app etc. Everything just works, with no glitches. After trying it out for a few minutes, I bought the lifetime license (which I think is pretty reasonable for what it offers) and I haven’t looked back. All was well until, as I said above, I messed up and deleted my account.  After I accidentally deleted the account, I again tried to find a replacement app. Discovered that no other app compares so happy that all is well again and look forward to continuing with this app.   For anyone who might make the same mistake as me— I was attempting to delete all the data from the app so I could start over. I didn’t realize that by deleting the data I would also delete my account. So when I tried to sign back into the app it didn’t recognize my email address. If that happens to you, just sign up again with the same email address as before and your account will automatically be restored.

But it’s not perfect yet either, although the shortcomings seem like easy features to fix (hopefully the developers are listening). In the search for a Mint replacement it’s a toss up with apps like Buddy Budget (great iPad App and nice subcategories), PocketGuard (good refresh, transaction rules and split transactions) Piere (does almost all the Cons listed below) and Wallet by Budget Bakers (all the same Pros as Spendee, but cannot link with all my accounts, so I’m giving Spendee a chance!) I appreciate Spendee's help center that answered some of my questions but there are still a few things that I can’t do in the Spendee App that seem like obvious features (I contacted support they were prompt in acknowledging my feedback): Things I love: - Multi Currency account integration (like Wise) - manual transactions even in multiple currencies(!) - Lifetime purchase (1/2 off right now) - shared with other user for manual entries (but this should include sharing the budget too) Things that don’t work: - rollover budgeting from month to month categories (at least from my initial test) - no sub-categories! Really? I know I can label, and the labels are sortable within each category in the overview graphs (but attaching labels is a multi step process more so than a subcategory feature) - no split transactions? - no iPad oriented App (the iPhone App does not work well on an iPad) - no Mint import, or any import to a linked account! - no reoccurring transactions in linked accounts (only manual), but the largest immediate drawback is the slow refresh for some accounts. The “refresh” button on the wallet says that it has been refreshed but it’s deceptive because some accounts can only update once a day and to get a manual refresh you have to go in the account settings and manually relink the bank! That is NOT a viable option. I might as well just open every one of my banking Apps to see the amounts - which defeats the purpose of a tracking App. Other Apps don’t have this limitation so Spendee really needs to figure it out.

title: What’s needed to make it truly usable
content: To effectively manage a budget, i have to be able to look at the budget DAILY and see that I am  on track. This is not feasible now because major purchases unnecessarily throw me off budget. For example, if I buy today a $5,000 family getaway including airline tickets and hotels, and the trip is scheduled to occur next year, I’d like to be able to spread the $5,000 across the specific days of the trip. Similarly, if I buy a sofa or a new iPhone, or a car(!). I now have this major purchase that unnecessarily throws me off my monthly, and possibly annual budget. If I could spread the expense across its lifetime, that problem goes away. This would enable me to look at the budget daily, and see how I’m doing. Specifically, what I need is: in the budget view the ability to set an accrual schedule for a transaction - when does it start, and across what period to spread it. At the top of the list I see tags I have never used for any income category, let alone the cure t one for example. Plus it takes an extra tap to start adding the tags, why???  The way all wallets are now grouped by default is so unnecessarily clunky, now to see the overview of one takes so many extra taps, which in turn means extra loading times, because this app sets a record for poor optimisation.  The pro feature set is insulting to anyone who buys it. Bank transactions are not editable, so if you want automated logging you can forget about detailed or even coherent descriptions. content: I love this app. I've tried them all but this one comes close to what I need.   1. Iphone, Android apps and web access to manipulate larger quantities of data.   2. You can import and export data  3. The wallets are shareable BUT limited To the shared wallet. This means Incan share 1 wallet with person A, 2 wallets with person B and keep everything else private.   4. Multiple currencies - I have stuff all other the place - but this aspect could be improved. They x-rates are automatic but from a true income-expense pov the app should save the x-rate for the date of the transaction. This means the expense and income is always the same and doesn't fluctuate each day.   5. This is the only thing missing for a perfect score: payee/suppliers. When you add a transaction you are not able to add WHO you are paying to. They should add a Payee field because that way I can keep track of my payees, I can see how much I spent in a specific store or restaurant in total, I can share my payees when I share my wallet so they are consistent through out. I hope they add payee fields!!!!  6. Another, but in my case less Important, are two missing fields that are paymemt type (cash, credit card, debit card, apple pay, etc), parent status (cleared, reconciled, unreconciled, void), and labels (custom label I can add to transaction so i can have my own taxonomy - they have hashtags but they are part of the note description)  7. Would be nice to set up goals so I can see how close I'm getting to saving money for a vacation or new tv.   Come on guys... add these last few things and become the best most complete money and budgeting app!!  A few weeks later I wanted to take the next step and purchase the app.   The purchase options (still visible as of today's date) listed in in-app purchase on the Apple Store page also offered the lifetime premium. But guess what guys!?! None of those actually exist anymore. I wrote the company and they just said, sorry doesnt exist.   I personally think that if they offer misleading and false advertising Apple should make them honor these offers. If they are too lazy to update the Apple Store page maybe they shouldn't be there.

title: Missing a key feature
content: While this app is really good at dividing up how much to allocate toward each bill or “envelope”, one key feature that would help this app meet my needs is the ability to rank each bill according to priority.   Like a 4 tier system because there’s an average of 4 weeks per month.  The bills in tier 1 are highest priority and the app can calculate how much to set aside to pay the tier 1 bills by their due date.   Tiers 2-4 can be considered respectively once each tier before it has been accounted for. This method frees up funds per week towards something else.  An alternative is to implement the ability to disable certain bills so that only active ones are budgeted. This is a manual version of the tier idea that would just require going in weekly and enabling/ disabling bills as needed.  Can be useful if a bill has been paid for the month already (maybe the user got a bonus at work or received a gift or something) they’ll have the option of getting ahead on the bill or reallocating those funds elsewhere.  Right now, the only way to do anything similar is to delete the entire envelope, which is not ideal.  I’m not sure if it’s common for people to budget for every single bill, every week, all throughout the month, with every check. But if there are people that, for example, budget on the 3rd week of this month for bills due in the 1st week of next month, in a staggered fashion, this feature would LITERALLY be a life saver.  I really hope something like this could be implemented because I like this app.

Pros: I love how the app remembers how certain transactions belong to certain categories. That saves a lot of entry time. it's pretty easy to dive into expenses per envelope or look at the pie chart for the current month or past month (more than 1 month previous requires you to input specific dates.)  Cons: the app is primarily set up by expense envelopes. They're "filled" every month with your budgeted amount and rollover excess or unspent dollars. I've never loved this feature but have been able to deal with it until today. I tried making a new budget for this year and for the life of me cannot figure out how to make each month reset with no rollover. I looked through my categories after I tried to change my budget and all of my expenses were completely wrong and didnt add up to the transactions within the folder. This could easily be user error on my part but if I'm not easily able to change monthly budgets with accurate expense tracking then I'm not able to use this app.

title: A loyal customer for a decade, but still lacking an iPad app?!

Today, Goodbudget helps make paying all the monthly bills possible and still have money for 401k and for whatever fun goals I set, such as saving up for an overseas vacation or a new car. I can’t recommend this program enough.   However, it’s shocking to me that a decade later, there still isn’t an iPad app. I would also like to see a referral program where we can be rewarded for bringing our friends and providing Goodbudget with new long-term paying customers. title: Best Budgeting App By Far!!!
content: I have never reviewed an app before and this is completely unprompted.   I have been using Goodbudget for over 3 months now and I absolutely love it! I have wanted to try an envelope budgeting system before but using cash for everything is not convenient for me. My main goals were to establish a budget, have data showing what my money is being spent on and for what general purpose, and to become debt free. This app allows my to tell every cent where to go! I can easily keep track of my bank account balances, student loans, credit card balances (which are all now paid off!) set goals, customize how often I budget, keep track of due dates, etc.  I highly recommend upgrading to Goodbudget Premium. I only had the free account for less than a week before buying a year of Premium. While the free version is an excellent starting point and much more capable than other free budgeting systems, Premium is a game changer and I have easily recouped the investment with this app. I mean, I was able to prioritize spending and pay off $14k+ of debt in 3 months. Something that I theoretically could have done myself but without the level of tracking and money management this app has provided me, I likely would still be severely in debt.  One major benefit of the Premium subscription is the Priority Support service. If you have any questions on how to set something in the app to suit your needs, priority support is always very prompt (within a couple of hours) and provide detailed solutions with examples.  Could not recommend enough for people who want to feel empowered by taking charge of their finances!

title: Room for Improvement
content: I started using GoodBudget for a class project a month ago, and I think that's it's not the best, but definitely not the worst budgeting app. I've decided to leave a review so I may be helpful to the creators, and see some improvements so I can continue using it. First, I really appreciate the different reports (the pie chart and Income vs. Spending). This feature helps me track and visualise my spending in a clear and precise way. Second, I like how it keeps all the different transactions in one area, and I can scroll down through past days and see my spending. I also like how, in the transactions, you can have planned transaction, such as an allowance.      However, some features in the app were confusing and not very user friendly. First, sometimes when I tried to make a transaction, the app crashed multiple times. It would not work until I reset my iPad. Second, I do not like how the envelopes work. When you spend above your budget, it shows all of the money in negative, not just the surplus you spent. Third, the app itself can be confusing to navigate. Finally, GoodBudget Plus is ridiculously expensive. It costs 70 dollars per year, and there is no way to sync your credit card to the app.     Some suggestions I would make for improvement would be; first, it would be great if the envelopes could be changed only to show the surplus spent. Second, maybe some icons to differentiate the different categories would be useful. The design for the app is rather monotonous and could be improved by graphics such as those icons. Finally, it would be amazing if GoodBudget could find a way to sync credit cards to the app, because it is a long process to manually upload each of these transactions.     Again, I wouldn't recommend GoodBudget to a friend, but there is nothing wrong with it. It just doesn't have some of the functions and features that I feel are really important for budgeting apps. It's just kind of adequate. It would be really amazing if they could make these improvements. Thanks!

title: It is really “good”
content: I’m giving this app a fiver because it really is good.   What this app does is it helps you to think before you spend. THINK. Other apps don’t do this, instead they connect to your bank and then show you nice graph of what you have been spending your money on. Nice but not really helpful or encouraging self-discipline.  Most people have a bad habit of waiting for payday then they spend it on what ever they want until it’s empty and they have to dip into savings or worse investments or even worse borrow from friends or family. That’s also a bad habit but many people do it. I’m even guilty of it at times. This app helps you to stop doing that. It has helped me and is worth the fee.  It will take a few weeks to adjust your plan and discipline yourself. But it does work and will balance out. Think of it as a game. You have to win by not spending over budget.  If you think it doesn’t work then you might have a spending habit you are unaware of. It’s up to you to identify it and balance what the app says and what your bank account says.
