title: I love this app- I wonder if one more feature is possible
content: I’m giving this 5 starts because it is amazing and even though there’s something I wish it had (which I’ll get into) that isn’t to say this app is lacking. It’s simplistic and shared in real time. My partner and I have been using it for a couple months. Functions well on both our devices- apple for me, android for him. I handle all the household finances so being able to see all the spending being done is great- I don’t have to constantly ask the s/o “did you get gas” “how much were the groceries” trying to stay on top of it all. Its so easy to enter in spending, and to name envelopes. It is all extremely user friendly, designed in an intuitive and aesthetically pleasing way, I could go on for a long time about all the positive aspects of this app. Try for yourself and see how well it works. It makes budgeting a little fun and a lot less stressful when everything you need to calculate your finances is right in front of you.     The feature I wish this app had is something no app I’ve found so far has- a bi-weekly refill section.  Our grocery/gas budget is sorted by when our paychecks come in (I think this is the case for many people who live paycheck to paycheck) so when we hit the three-paycheck month, it threw off number calculations in the app making it appear as though we were in the red when in fact things were on track.  Just as there are separate monthly/yearly categories, to have envelopes that have a set amount and refill every two weeks on a decided day (for us it is fridays, but not everyone gets paid on the same day everywhere) that would not only improve our lives and use of the app, but it would give this app a major leg up on competition because NO ONE has this function that I can find. Not one other app.  Aside from that, really spectacular app. Will definitely keep using, and will recommend to anyone who ever asks for a “good budget”-ing app.

title: Life Changing for the Ramsey Fan!
content: I waited a long time to write this review. I’ve been using Goodbudget for a couple of years now, and with any new thing it takes time to discover how best to apply it to your life.  I’m a huge fan of Dave Ramsey, and would love to live in an all cash world, but for me that’s unrealistic. I like to swipe the cards, and I love the rewards. Credit Cards are not evil, the lack of self control is. Remember that.  Anyway, with Goodbudget I can have my credit cards and still be financially free! With the accounting system this provides, my credit cards essentially take the role of debit cards in my wallet. I plug in what I’ve bought, everything subtracts, and I pay my bill at the end.  No more complicated spreadsheets. No more writing transactions down twice (out of the checkbook and out of the budget), no more spending hours and hours looking for .22 cents  No more, no more, no more. The little Goodbudget bots do all that number running around for me! Literally, I’d take an entire day managing out what is basically Goodbudget on paper. AN ENTIRE DAY.   Now that same work takes 10 minutes. No sh*t. TEN MINUTES.   I even print out reports weekly and have a sit down with my hubs so we can talk about where we are doing great and where we can improve.   I’ve been able to get myself from living DAY to DAY to living MONTH to MONTH and now YEAR to YEAR.   That’s right people... from Valentines Day to Christmas...all paid for, waiting in their happy little envelopes.  I will scream it from every rooftop around, the person who laid in bed and said at 2am “there should be an app for this” ...you’ve changed my life. I love you to the moon and back.

title: Good, but need to understand functions.
content: Goodbudget offers a traditional approach to spending, while implementing the method in a conveniently-functioning app. Its envelope system allows you to fill set amounts of money into a virtual envelope, in which can be labeled and directed towards different areas of spending. Reports are provided so often on said areas, and visual aids are included with these reports so that tracking spending is easier to conclude.   There are several benefits of using this app, one being that setting goals of spending are manageable and uncomplicated. With this, a threshold can be recognized and spending can be limited. Transactions of both expense and credit can be made anytime. Virtually anything can be set to an amount - the amount spent, the goal to save, transactions, income, and even balance.   Some downfalls came to the app, however, when noticed that only a set amount of envelopes were allowed to be created, and transaction history was automatically deleted over time. This could only be changed after paying a subscription to enable the additional functions. Along with that, the envelope concept is an unfamiliar term today, and likely requires some context or beforehand understanding in order to utilize its functions efficiently and correctly.   Overall, Goodbudget serves as a reliable app to track and limit spending, but requires some preliminary learning or understanding as well. To improve their app, I would suggest that they include a sort of tutorial to help new users better understand the interface and functions of the app, and possibly include more visual aids along with that.

title: Excellent App

content: Pretty good. Wish it was a little more customizable,  though I’m a college student and my budgeting needs are different than most. My main issue is that I keep getting a pop up that it has trouble syncing and it will try again later but it fixes itself instantly. Annoying.

title: Budgeting done!
content: I have been using the app for one year and it has helped me do a complete 180 with my finances. I use to always be broke living one paycheck to another and now I have money saved and bills paid the second they arrive. The app helps you see where all of your money is going as long as you input everything you spend. The app is super easy to input the expenses and only take a few seconds once you have all your categories set. I don’t have my accounts linked because I like to only work out of good budget and then go back and balance it once I get my bank statement. This has worked so week for me that I am debt free minus the house of course and now I don’t stress about where all my money goes. It has taught me how to live within my means and how to save for the things I really want to do. Over the years I have tried other apps and never could commit to them because they were to complicated. Good budget has changed that completely, thank you!

title: Super Ap for Free!
content: Love this app. Have used it for years. I like how they’re not all up in my business. I just want to track my expenses by my self-inputted budget. Doesn’t get into my checking account, or CC’s. It’s not linked to anything, doesn’t sell me anything. Love it! ✊🏻 Budget on!

content: This app has saved my budgeting life.  I even used it when I was unemployed and making $500 per month. It can be tailored to any salary. I live the new debt feature as well. Now my teen aged son, who is working now,  is using it. He loves it as well.

title: I highly recommend this app!
content: Love this app! It helps me stay on budget in real time. I also appreciate being able to keep track of purchases I make that I need to get reimbursed.

content: I LOVE the App. But what would make it 5 stars, and what would make a SIGNIFICANT difference in my user experience is having a "status" column in the transactions. Right now I am having to date uncleared transactions as "12/31/17" just so I can keep track of my uncleared items. Then I have to scroll over and over again for each transaction to change the date to the date it posted just so I know which transactions have cleared, also to make sure I didn't forget to log any transactions. title: Keeps you very accountable!!

title: A truly simple visual budget
content: I’ve been envelope budgeting for years in paper, then excel and now w Goodbudget. I tried two others before Goodbudget. A  downfall is its Report feature;  not as adaptable as Quicken (fancy checkbook) and so I use both (double entry) to get the report info for taxes and budget creating I want. I think overtime Goodbudget will improve its Reports and grow up its user interface. Highly recomend.

title: Goodbudget
content: It allows us to put in info about our spending as it happens. That makes it effective in maintaining our budget. This is because it allows info to be entered on different devices and then syncs the devices. I could not find another budget app that did this. title: Grow Up, Goodbudget
content: Everything about this app (from a functional standpoint) is 5-star. Easy to use, clear, no pesky bugs. It performs exactly as advertised. This 1-star review is only for the interactive element of Goodbudget, namely the anthropomorphic envelopes. What lunatic asylum design group thought it a good idea to create an emoting face that reacts to your spending? The feeling of being judged by this app is one hundred percent real for crossing the spending line established. When I went over budget on a particular line, I was honestly surprised to see the envelope figure not hanging from a noose. I use this app to track basic family spending items like groceries, restaurants, personal purchases, &c. I can’t imagine what it would feel like to use this app and go over budget on purchasing diapers or medical care for my child when every penny is already spent on other bills. Goodbudget - grow up, get rid of the emotive envelopes, and let people use your app judgement free like we all deserve in life.

title: Best budgeting app!!
content: We have been using Goodbudget for several years now and continue to be extremely happy with it. The yearly cost of it is absolutely worth every penny! I couldn't have done it all without the Goodbudget tool to manage my money (instead of it managing me). My favorite features include: real time updates to envelopes so my hubby and I are always in synch, the progress bar that helps you make decisions on if I should really go out to eat or not, easy imports/balancing of all of my bank accounts. title: Awesome App
content: My wife and I struggled for years seeking the best way to communicate our budget.  I manage the accounts, she does most of the spending.   We don’t like cash because so much is spent online, and cards are just more convenient.  Without cash, the envelope system was not an option.  Our budgeting turned into me accounting where the money was already spent each month.  Your app changes all that.  Thank you so much!  The only reason I don’t close my excel sheet permanently is that your system doesn’t seem to have future projections.  It would be awesome if I could track future income and expenses in here, to see that my account balances will not dip too low in the coming 12 months.  Add that feature and I will insist that all my friends and family start using Goodbudget.  I’d love to have a direct email to communicate other feedback and recommendations as they arise.  I love budgeting and would be glad to know you are interested in ideas to keep developing and improving what you offer.  UPDATE:   Since I don’t know where else to share my ideas.  I just reviewed my excel sheet and found these additional features which may not translate over to Goodbudget yet.   1. Calculate goals for charitable giving to multiple organizations, as a percent of gross income 2. Compare actual giving to goal percents in order to make any needed adjustments in actual giving.  *Points 1 and 2 could be applied to savings in the same way.   3. Track gross income and paycheck withholdings 4. Allow a better catch-all for bills and income which do not need envelopes.  Currently I cannot move funds from an envelope to unallocated.  I had to create an envelope for that purpose, which complicates some of the sweep and schedule features.   5. Group envelopes together for subtotals other than the current monthly or annual distinction 6. Ability to budget for expenses that don’t need an envelope, like income, and bills with due dates.   7. Ability to compare budget projections to actual spending history 8. Ability to see budget projections for coming 12 months, as I mentioned above, including ALL anticipated income and expenses 9. Display future account balances based on those projections, at least on a month end basis, if not daily, to avoid overdraft. Maybe give two projections, with or without the envelope money, to give sort of a high and low water mark.   10.  This is redundant to a couple previous points, but distinguish between bills that have due dates, and envelopes which are spent over a month or year.  I guess you’d have to distinguish between monthly bills and less frequent or irregular bills that may still require an envelope.   11. Allow positive and negative entries everywhere.  They are always possible on the browser version, but sometimes negative entries can’t be entered in the app.  There is sometimes a “credit/expense” field, but I know I’ve seen places where even this option does not appear in the app.    Thanks

title: Best budget app!
content: Goodbudget has been my go-to budget app for years. It's the best, easiest, and simplest replacement for the old cash envelope budget system. I use the free version, so I don't have bank account syncing, but I've always been diligent about tracking my transactions and checking my bank account to make sure everything lines up, so I don't feel like I'm missing anything. On payday I simply go in and fill the appropriate envelopes and it keeps me on track with all my bills and living expenses. I love that the app has an "Annual/Irregular" feature, which I use to track my "sinking funds" like car maintenance and pet bills; things I might not spend money on monthly, but I still budget for. I use the 10 monthly envelopes to track my monthly bills and daily spending like groceries and gas in my checking account and the annual/irregular envelopes to track my sinking funds in my savings account. I love this app and will continue to use it as long as it's around!

title: See where your money goes
content: My wife and I love this app. We do a yearly subscription (and it has its own envelope) and it is well worth it. We each have an allowance so big goofy purchases don’t need to be explained. I just safe up my allowance. When bills are due the money is there and our savings is building faster than ever. We both have the app on our phones so both can see where our money is any time. We never argue over finances and that is huge. And I have it set when we get paid to automatically distribute to each envelope. A one-time purchase I could understand, but a subscription? No. Don’t waste your time. Use excel or a free printout and do your own budgeting.

title: Needs a couple features, but great app!
content: I’ve been using this for five months now, and this is the best app for a digital version of the old cash envelope system, a la Dave Ramsey. It’s great because some budget categories get spent completely every month to a zero balance, whereas other categories may accumulate over time, like savings, and this app accounts for these growing “envelope” balances - something that every budgeting app I’ve tried lacked. As long as you, and your spouse, enter EVERY transaction, it’s a dream to use. And with the accounts feature turned on you’ll know exactly how much you have at any time. I have bank and credit accounts entered, so I always know their balances at a glance. WHAT IS LACKING: There needs to be a RECONCILE feature in the app for when you need to compare what’s in Goodbudget versus your bank or credit card statements - like a checkbox next to each transaction in the transaction list. It’s frustrating sometimes to try and make sure you’ve got everything entered but have no way to mark what you’ve already verified. Ugh! Also, there needs to be a SEARCH feature in the app to search for specific transactions. There is one for the website but not the app. ——- Get the app! Keep up the good work, Goodbudget!

title: Great App!! Use it!
content: This is a life saver app! Only advice is to set up on a desktop first as it is easier to navigate but overall a good app!

title: Don’t waist your time

At that point your happy to subscribe but the whole process is pointless because their subscription platform is not set up yet! So essentially you have a non functioning app for download. Misleading! You should take down or warn people the max is 10 envelopes (bills). Saves us 5 minutes of our life.

title: Detailed enough without being overly complicated.
content: I tried out several apps and online programs for budgeting until settling on Goodbudget. Those include You Need a Budget, Mvelopes, Every Dollar, and Mint, and perhaps others that I’m not thinking of. My preference for Goodbudget is probably very much a personal preference as far as how I like to see accounts and information displayed. In the paid version, there is plenty of room for detail and keeping your different expenses and accounts separate without being overly complicated and technical. I like having an “unallocated” fund to keep excess funds before we have determined what they will be used for or in case our expenses are less for a particular month. I also like that it does not link to my bank account. Some may prefer that option, but I find that I am more aware of my expenses if I’m being forced to enter each one, and it helps force the habit of entering transactions as soon as they are made. The app and online site sync easily, and the expense entry system is intuitive and simple. In the app, entering deposits and merchandise returns requires a different series of operations from an expense, which is a little cumbersome but not awful. I also would love to have the option to take a picture of the receipt and store it with the transaction. All in all, it’s an easy app to use and provides the information I need at a glance. I think it’s definitely worth the money for a paid subscription. I started out paying monthly, but I’ll be upgrading to a yearly payment to save money.

title: Goodbudgeting for 6 years and still loving it! :)
content: Goodbudget has been there for me through all my life and job changes as an adult! I started using Goodbudget when I graduated from college over 6 years ago, back when I was single and had two part-time jobs. Today, I am married and my partner and I each have a full-time job. We have the paid version and track everything in our budget, from birthday gifts to haircuts—we have 40 envelopes. Goodbudget has helped us save for a car, take multiple vacations abroad, and budget for emergencies (car break-ins, flat tires, parking tickets—the Emergencies envelope saved us!) and save for a future home renovation. Here are my favorite things about Goodbudget: 1) Great flexibility in tracking multiple paychecks – I used to have two incomes; one was once a month and one was every Friday, now I get paid twice a month and my husband gets paid every other Friday. We schedule our paychecks to post on the days we actually receive them and fill our envelopes at the beginning of the month using our cushion. Works great. 2) The envelope faces are cute and kind of sassy. Wish I could use the shocked one as an emoji! 3) I just got access to the new debt features and now we can start tracking our mortgage paydown—it’s great that it even calculates the interest for me! There’s a report that shows me my projected payoff date based on my monthly payments. 4) We have monthly meetings to go over our spending and saving goals, and it's really easy to pull up our Goodbudget reports to see our data, organized in a way that makes sense to us. Thank you, Goodbudget!

title: Honestly saved me from losing my car
content: I have been using Good Budget for over 4 years. I first downloaded it and started using it a tiny bit before that, when it was still called EEBA (Easy Envelope Budget Assistant), but I didn’t fully commit to using it until after I went through Dave Ramsey’s Financial Peace University with my church. Dave Ramsey is all about CASH CASH CASH for everything, but I can’t keep track of things like that. With Good Budget though, I was able to start following Dave’s concepts of assigning every dollar a job, pre-planning where you spend things, and not overspending. Mathematically speaking, I couldn’t pay rent, eat, and make my car payments all at the same time, but somehow through careful planning, following the budget, and putting God first in all of it, I paid off my car 4 months early.  As an app, it works really well. I love the convenience of being able to input transactions as I go. It interfaces with the website, and I really like how it all runs.  A lot of people tell me they couldn’t use it because it’s all manual. GB doesn’t download your transactions for you. There’s no interfacing with your bank, they don’t check your credit score, they don’t offer you pre-approved credit offers, or any of that. It’s entirely dependent on you doing it yourself. I like this because it forces be to stay very actively involved with my money.   There’s a few things I don’t like about it. The app interfaces with GPS so it knows when you’re at the same store it’ll pull up that store again when you go to input a new transaction. If that store has multiple locations, it doesn’t pull up easily.   I also don’t like that there’s no way to store actual receipts. Photos or halftone scans or some such.   The user interface could use an update, it hasn’t changed much in the last 4 years.

It’s quick and convenient to enter expenses right after spending and keeps us synced up. We’ve been using it for a few years now and have no plans on switching.

title: Easy!
content: Love how easy this budget app is! I’ve looked at others and they get complicated quickly. If you use an envelope system then this app is for you. I went from writing on an envelope to this seamlessly. I love how you can add and subtract envelopes as the month needs.

title: So Helpful
content: I have had so many financial issues in the past.  Bad decisions led to foreclosure, repo, late and unpaid bills, etc.  Then I started using Goodbudget.  Now I’m up to date on all my finances, and I’m even able to be charitable.  Love it.

title: Awesome app!
content: Good job developers! I just wish there was a way when starting off the app, if you’re going to make 1000 over the course of the month for it not to try to allocate the money you do not have yet :/ Also, if you could implement a PIN number that would be awesome to. Other than that, it is a great app!

title: Love it
content: Have used this everyday for several years and love it! Wish it had the ability to search.

title: Hits the mark
content: Does what it needs to. I like that it syncs with my wife’s phone so we both are up to date.

title: Great budget app!
content: Budgeting with Goodbudget is better than anything else I’ve ever tried that utilizes a bucket style system for budgeting.

title: Keeps me honest!
content: My wife and I started using this for our household budgeting and if we are committed and actually enter our money it has really helped keep us on track and get back out of debt. The only thing I wish It could do was cut off my debit card for me when I’ve spent all of my monthly allowance :-)

title: Great tracking app...but
content: This is a great budget app to track daily spending. The only thing that would make this app even better is daily spending totals with a total for everything combined for the day and daily total for each envelope.

title: Budget app that puts me in control!
content: I absolutely LOVE GoodBudget! It’s changed my life! I love that I can make so many envelopes that fit my specific bills and spending categories/goals. And the fact that it doesn’t link to your accounts is not a detriment but a HUGE advantage for two reasons: 1) Causes you to have to stay aware of your spending at all times, 2) You never have to worry about it not syncing and being inaccurate. I am more aware of my finances than I have been in my entire life. I really can’t say enough good things about the app. Never any problems, and transitioning from mobile app to computer is seamless.

title: Great app
content: This budget app has been extremely helpful for my family and I. Everyone get this app

title: Easy to use, staying on track!
content: This is the first time in 20 years I’ve ever successfully stuck to a budget!  My husband and I are using this along with another app called “debt free” to reduce our debt and stay on plan.  We both know where we stand and how  much we have left.  It helps to look at this app vs. the bank account which looks like we have a lot of money in it.   But that money is in specific envelopes and “spoken for”.  I have recommended it to many family members and friends!

title: Great for first time budgeters, could use some improvement.
content: Easiest user interface I've seen among envelope budgeting apps that cover basic needs in budgeting, and it's nice that they don't put a time limit on the free version while you're first getting your finances under control (though the paid version is definitely worth the unlimited envelopes!). Mobile version is clean and functional. Reports are decent too, though some other apps allow you to get more detailed analysis.  Reason for only 4 stars is that they're are a few random annoying glitches, most notably that if you edit am existing budget, you can NOT see what your total budget is adding to as you edit, so I have to budget in a spreadsheet first then copy it all manually into the app to ensure I'm not budgeting myself into a deficit. It would also be nice if they added the ability to link directly to accounts like mint does in case I miss a transaction, though there are pros and cons to enabling people to be less hands-on in their budgeting.

title: Eh it's ok
content: No automatic bank syncing??? Almost good but with all the competition that does offer that feature I'll look elsewhere

title: Love the App - Please update for iPhone X
content: I absolutely love this app because it has saved me thousands of dollar. Please update app for iPhone X and possible offer the app for iPads.

title: Filling Envelopes a Pain
content: So complicated to create a new envelope. Had to go through many complicated steps just to add money to the budget amount. Not intuitive.

title: Bugged
content: Showed promise but I’m not paying $5.99 a month for a buggy app.

title: This app is not for beginners
content: I am a novice at budgeting using technology. After years of pen and paper I decided to get started with this app and soon found out this is not for beginners. I kept getting negative amounts when trying to allocate funds and just in general not being able to figure it out.  Maybe someone with more experience would breeze through this app but a novice like me will have a hard time

title: Started off great...
content: ...and then I reached my envelope limit. I was willing to pay for more, but it said unavailable. Deleted and moved on to another app.

title: Cumbersome and frustrating.
content: This complicates something that should be simple.  Fill envelopes and pay out of them. It tries to be cute or clever and just ends up being hard to use. I had several people try to use it and they felt the same way.  Subscription cancelled after 2 days.   Don’t bother.

title: GUI Needs Improvement
content: I used Goodbudget back when it was EEBA and after 5 or 6 years I came back and the GUI is still the same. I would love to see an upgrade to make it look more modern. Also, setting up envelopes by category and having them displayed in categories on the main screen will be a plus. I suggest to take a look at Dave Ramsey’s EveryDollar app and learn a bit from them. He has all the things that I am saying, but I still like GoodBudget better. If GUI/Categories change then I will give 5 stars. Thanks!

title: Glitchy for envelope fill
content: It will not let me sync to add my monthly envelope fill, so I guess I’ll be penniless forever...

title: Needs a lot of improvement
content: Great concept but alot of issues. When adding an annual item it shows how much you need to save each month to meet that amount, but the minute you back out of it, you cannot see the amount you need to save each month. Monthly budget amount and what you have left to budget only shows on the edit screen.  Makes no sense.    The hunt for a budgeting app continues

title: A little confusing
content: I just got it no more than five minutes ago and it somehow says I have 400 in my account but I know I typed 160? Maybe it’s calculating what I’ll mark by the end of the month?? I don’t know; I’m just confused.

title: I’ve tried everything! Finally!
content: Finally i found an app with a budget that can be adjusted the way I need it! I’ve searched high and low for a budget that can be set to start on a certain day of the month, because our income is not on the first, and this app has that feature!!   Also love the envelope system...we tried going all cash so we could budget with envelopes and it just doesn’t work for our lifestyle, but this app lets you budget with envelopes electronically which is awesome!  Very helpful tutorial videos help you get everything set up, and very pleased that the free version is everything I need!   Only suggestion or complaint (which is really lame...but hear me out) is the little smiling/frowning envelope faces on my budgets....sometimes I can’t help that my envelope has run out, and those little faces seem to be reprimanding me for no good reason. Wish I could edit them a little per envelope to be more neutral when I need them to be. Otherwise, love that they’re telling me when I’m “on track” or to “stop spending for a few days”  Overall, I definitely suggest trying this app.

title: Can’t use emojis in the envelope name
content: Can’t use emojis in the envelope name. Whenever I place an emoji in the envelope name and save it, the name either doesn’t save the emoji or, if the emoji is at the beginning, it deletes the entire name of the envelope.

title: Too much money
content: After you put so many things on your list it requires a subscription. I could understand a one time purchase but a subscription? The point is to save money not spend more a month on an app.

title: Crashes constantly
content: Any time I hit the tab to edit transactions, the app crashes. It’s unusable in its current state. I’ve emailed the support team several times; no response.

title: All good.
content: The app does what it I wanted. I request just one feature. Can you add a functionality to save the receipt of the expense? That would be really helpful.  Thanks.

title: Great, but...
content: This app is great, but one thing that drives me crazy is not having a way to distinguish transactions that have cleared my bank and those that have not. I love everything else, but that is a feature that would be extremely helpful.

title: Best budget app there is
content: I have tried them all, and this one is the best hands down.  I am a Dave Ramsey nut so I tried his Every Dollar app first.  This one has so much more to offer and is a lot easier to use.

title: RDA
content: Extremely difficult to make changes with your account. I tried starting over and deleting mine twice— the third time I gave up 😠

title: Best budgeting app of all time
content: Yeah ... it is . Even though it’s manual, it’s much easier to use than Mint.   The only feature I am wanting right now is the ability to see all transactions of a specific type during a certain period. Right now it just shows all transactions so while it’s good to see the pie charts of where your money went, you can’t really see exactly what you spent it on for that period of time.  Other than that, amazing app, has actually helped me and wife stick to a budget for once. Nothing else worked

title: Not user friendly/too complicated
content: I really like the whole idea of this but it’s overly complicated with no instructions.

title: Frustrating to work with
content: At first I really loved Goodbudget. I love the digital envelope system, how easy it is to input expenses, the recurring payments/income feature, etc. More recently I’ve found some of the processes more cumbersome than helpful. When I set a recurring income, including specifying which envelope the money goes into, it resets the envelope at the base amount set rather than adding to what’s already in there. It takes the excess and sweeps it into “Unallocated” rather than keeping it where I very deliberately put it. Then I have to go through the process of figuring out how much was in each envelope before my income hit, and transfer from unallocated into the various envelopes (each transfer happening separately).  All in all, this program is pretty good, but only if you’re budgeting and living paycheck to paycheck, especially since it’s free. If you are saving up for something or want to have extra money in a few of your envelopes, this program becomes more of a headache than it’s worth.

title: Great app, but no iPhone X support
content: Goodbudget is an extremely useful app, but it hasn’t been updated for four months, and still lacks iPhone X support (literally the only app I have that doesn’t yet support it). Such a slow update cycle doesn’t bode well for this app, and I’ve begun to look for alternatives.

title: This app ruined my life
content: Ever since I started using Goodbudget, my shopping has plummeted down to essentials and a small splurge once in a big while, I pretty much eat out only when dining with friends, and now I have all this money left over to build my savings and even make a donation, all because of this stupid app. I don’t even know who I am anymore.   The set-up takes some time, but once you get past that, the app makes it easy to manage your budget. I manually enter every purchase or bill, but the benefit of this is that I’m more consciously aware of every time I spend money. Get this app, and ruin your life. Or change it for the better. It all depends on which way you look at it.

title: Financial Must
content: My wife and i have paid off all our debt and are staying dept free with the help of this app. It truly is amazing. It's as simple or complicated as you like. I don't link my bank accounts and use the free version. My wife is android and I'm iOS.   I recommend this app to everyone, everyone i have a conversation about finances. Quite literally.

title: This is not the year 2020
content: and yet the app sets the year to 2020 and cannot be changed. This means every month you have to manually re-enter your budget - because the app won’t auto refill until 2020. Mind boggling.

title: Optimize!
content: Hey GoodBudget Team, for the money that is being spent on this app by thousands you need to step up your game and optimize the app for the X, add frequently requested features, and actually respond to your ratings. I could optimize this app in less than a day, so please, pay for a developer and get this train moving again.

title: Confusing
content: I wanted to love this app but it makes no sense!!

title: Loved it
content: We loved this app and would love to use it again but it needs to be updated.  Please...please...please.

title: Frustrating
content: I'm sure this app will be great when I figure out how to use it. It's not very intuitive and the video tutorials are only for the. Computer based version. Not mobile. I think i did something wrong because no matter what I do I get a red bar. I'm guessing I have to wait until the next month for it to reset. If I takes me more than 2 days I'm bailing and trying a different app.

title: Love it
content: This app has helped me and my wife track our spending so much better! The overspending problem due to lack of planning and tracking is gone. The graphics are fun too.  We do not use the bank features, we only use the envelope budget feature and we manually enter in everything.

title: Good...but could be better
content: This is a great program for a virtual envelope budgeting system.  Nothing else out there really compares to this format, and I’ve looked.  However, I keep looking for one specific reason.  There’s no option to automatically download financial transactions.  They will tell you it’s so you pay attention to your finances more by having to manually enter, but in my experience the time it takes to manually input means I often get behind, then my envelopes aren’t balanced and I still don’t know how much I have to spend.  Honestly, it just seems like laziness at this point on behalf of the developers.  Would be nice to just open the app and quickly categorize my transactions that are already downloaded and waiting for me.  All in all though, this is still the best setup for budgeting.

title: Difficult to use
content: This app isn’t intuitive. It is hard to figure out how to add money, how to increase your envelope amount, etc. I tried Goodbudget after leaving a great budget app that was completely intuitive to use, but charges after 2 months worth of budgets...I guess it’s time for me to put my money where my mouth is!

title: Too expensive
content: This app is exactly what I need but it would ironically be the most expensive reoccurring software payment in my budget. I love it because the categories (envelopes) are fully customizable, but they make you pay $17.99 every 3 months for more envelopes. That is ridiculous. It also doesn’t link to my bank account, which would have made the insane $17.99 slightly more tempting, but in the end I’m deleting the app simply because it’s just too expensive. I’m bummed because this app is exactly what I need.

title: EXACTLY what I needed
content: This app is amazing. I used the paper-envelope method successfully for years, but then started to get lazy & too addicted to my smartphone for all the paper. My finances became a total mess. I was in desperate need of something that emulated a style of budgeting that made sense to me, that was easy & simple, & that didn’t force me to link an app to my checking account (which I absolutely refuse to do). This app is all of those things & has been exactly what I needed to get back on track with my budgeting! I will say: the interface is a little counterintuitive & takes a little getting used to, but once you’ve got it it’s incredibly simple. It’s definitely not enough to give only 4/5 stars, in my opinion (which seems to be the only reason many other reviewers do). I am so grateful for this app & can see myself using this for years to come.

title: Envelopes?
content: 10 mins into using this app and I got lots of questions and still haven’t start budgeting. I feel like it’s adding extra frustration on top of managing my finances just trying to use/understand this app. I don’t get why everyone is so crazy about this dumb app.

title: Waste of time
content: Overly complicated design and layout. After hours of tediously entering everything in, it just crashes. I can’t access half the app. It’s simpler to just use notepad.

title: Still waiting for iPhone X update
content: So far, so good... there are some things I’d do differently.. this I like and don’t like but overall it’s nice to be able to categorize everything by envelopes. I’m still learning how it all works so I don’t want to be critical but I don’t want to get to into it if the app doesn’t update regularly. I should be able to log into the app via Face ID and it should be full screen on an iPhone X... at least. Hope/need to see this soon. Thank you.

title: Spend Time With It
content: It’s a pretty good app. You may have to spend some time with it to familiarize yourself with how to work it at first. I wish there was a bit of a tutorial to get started. Aside from that, I would like an option to add a picture of my receipt for a transaction/email receipt attachment. Solid choice for a budget app nonetheless.

title: Only allows 10 items before they charge you
content: Will only let you add in 10 items into your bills/expenses before you have to pay for more. Also, don't add your personal info.

title: Useful
content: Easy to use App. Simple and very useful.   Allows me to take my bi weekly income, and divide it into different “envelopes”, where I designate a budget to each envelope.

title: Great until it’s not
content: This app was just what I was looking for until I needed additional envelopes.  If there was a set price, I would have paid but I have no interest in paying a monthly fee.  The entire point of this is for the budget.  You’ve now added an extra line item to every month.

title: Great at first, but not practical long term
content: I'm not sure if I'm missing something but it seems as though the envelopes don't reset each pay period. I've set my budget period as semi-monthly but it doesn't seem to have any impact. I had assumed my envelopes would reset at the dates I set but nothing happens (leading me to question why it asked me to set dates in the first place).

title: Neat concept
content: I wish this could work but not enough free envelopes for this to work for me. I might consider paying one fixed amount to unlock the app but not interested in this expensive subscription. People looking for a budgeting app are trying to stop spending, not looking for $5+ a month subscriptions to keep track of.

title: Nice idea, but not intuitive...
content: And when I visit the help center to clarify terminology and usage, I receive instructions such as “ before you do anything take a deep breath...”. “ it’s best to start… With the information you already know”.   If that type of information is useful,  there are many other similar platitudes shared. I want to figure out why my budget for each “envelope” doubled and how to change it?  Will the same budgeted amounts repeat and or rollover next month?  I suspect the information is somewhere, but it’s like reading the small print to locate it.

title: Wasn’t a fan
content: I’m in college and desperately needed to manage my money. Started using this a few months ago and it was doing the trick but it’s very confusing to add money and it says your in the negative even though there still is money in the ”envelope” Not user friendly

title: Very Convenient
content: Makes setting money aside very easy. Never worry about having enough money for infrequent expenses or random gifts; just make an envelope for it.

title: Garbage
content: You can only put 10 lines in this budget before they want you to buy more space.  Save your time and find another budget app.

title: Wish it would compare to income
content: I only went through the setup which was pretty easy. It never had me enter my income. So what’s the point if it would let you know what’s left from overall income instead of what’s in the envelops. So I’ve deleted and will look for something complete.

title: Very confusing app
content: I can’t figure out how to do anything. I’ll stick to the pennies app.

title: Looks good
content: Under the hood is another story.   $30 / 6 months for more accounts and envelopes?!? Just wow!!!

title: It helps!
content: This Good budget app is awesome. When I got paid, I knew what bills had to be paid. If i had Extra money above my budget like overtime pay or extra work. I knew I could put that money towards debt or savings. Both your spouse and you can manage with the same app and budget. You both know how much to spend on groceries, date night, etc. You only get ten monthly envelopes and 10 yearly envelopes. It was manageable if you put gym membership and car insurance in yearly. Awesome!

title: Very good app!
content: Good Budget was kind of confusing to learn at first. Now that I’ve been at it for a couple weeks, I REALLY like it. I was looking for a very simple system that emulated an envelope system that is familiar to a lot of talk radio fans. I never wanted to carry physical envelopes. That seems archaic to me and very inconvenient at times. I also wanted something I could set up to automate my weekly budget allotment deposits into those envelopes. Also important was that it be as close to free as possible. This app did all of that for me. I didn’t want to over complicate the number of envelopes, so I only have four. That makes this completely free for me. Like I said, it wasn’t user friendly to learn and some of the controls of the envelopes aren’t very intuitive, but now that I’ve learned the system, I have automated it to do exactly what I want. I figured it out quickly, but it did take a bit of effort on my part. I’m glad i did. I really like the user interface, too.

title: Needs an update
content: I have used good budget on Android for two years and I loved it! I recently switched to iPhone and so far I have one major complaint. When I go into an envelope or account, why doesn't it list the running total next to the transaction total? I use that feature to keep track of my expenses and make sure I pay from the correct sources and this app is half as useful to me without the running total listed out. If they fix this one issue I would happily keep paying the premium price and give it five stars for sure!

title: Switched from YNAB
content: Was looking for a YNAB alternative because I wanted the ability to create a budget using  my take home pay for the month. Goodbudget allows me to plan for  what I know I will spend and plan for how I am going to use the money I have but also to plan for money I will get later in the month.   I like seeing the bar graph fill and the envelope’s expression showing if I am on target for that particular envelope or I am ahead of schedule.  Also the website app is clean and not cluttered

title: Could be awesome......
content: This app has great potential! Want to love so bad but why are the calculations so off? And the negative money in the unallocated envelope? Still needs much work..... hope these odd bugs get fix and it continues to improve!

title: Confusing for new user (and I'm 25!)
content: Read all about these great reviews but after an hour of messing around I'm so confused on how it works and what it means to fill an envelope vs adding. I'm in my 20s and good with technology but this is waaayyyy too complicated. Guess that's why people like it, I'm sure once you know what's going on you can personalize it. But not worth my energy to figure out..

title: Please Fix 4.0 or send it back.
content: New 4.0 version runs slow on 15Pro running on iOS 18.5. Lags and bugs to be addressed. Won’t auto switch themes.

title: Awesome, few suggestions
content: This is a great app to track expenses and budget with a lot of features! Just a few suggestions for improvement: -Adding a search bar somewhere so I can quickly find a transaction. Can’t seem to find a search function anywhere… -Under each account, a way to group the transactions by day (instead of each transaction on the same day listed separately so easier to see at once). Right now there’s only the option to descend or ascend transactions by price.  -Maintain the last opened view on the reports/statistics page. I like to open up to the Tags page with All chosen. Unfortunately whenever I reopen the app, this does not remain state and I have to scroll back to tags then click All again each time - a clearer way to show balance that considers pending vs cleared expenses. For example I have transactions that are coming up such as a refund for an item later in the month, but it gets confusing the current balance vs future balance. Maybe highlight the current balance somehow?

title: The best personal budget app
content: This is the best personal budget app that I had used among the various similar app. It has the most modern and beautiful UI and multi functions for you to tackle your money and budget.

title: 非常好用的記帳app, 是MOZE讓我養成記帳的習慣
content: 希望可以增加一些其他國家銀行的icon，像是美國、日本、加拿大等
這個是有史以來最好用的記帳app

title: 用了一年，很喜歡
content: 從一開始就買專業版，用了一年很喜歡！所以再續約下去，推推！

title: 希望增加买断制
content: 各项功能都比较完备，不过有些操作不太简洁，例如要修改某个支出，弹出的画面感觉是按照桌面系统设计的。另外希望增加买断制。

content: Crush after updating 14.2.1, I cannot reinstall cuz I did not backup, plz fix it ASAP

content: I use this app for almost 1 year and love it very much. The only improvement suggestion for now is whether it’s possible to add a searching for choosing categories when record an expense. Since I added a lot of sub categories and sometimes forget where the categories are, it will spend a lot of time to check each category. If there is a searching when adding a new record, that would be very helpful

title: 是想要的记账软件
content: 之前陆续使用了两款记账软件，每款使用都在一年左右。第一款非常强大，但价格很贵，而且交互很差，功能复杂概念太多；第二款款 UI 一般，价格便宜但是功能薄弱，很多操作需要好几个步骤才能解决，但是好在概念比较简单  打开 Moze 第一眼就决定订阅并且迁移过来，几乎满足了日常所有的记账需求  功能强大而且学习成本较低，UI 非常的舒服，各种提示/默认值也非常贴心  希望官方能给一些场景化的引导，方便能够最大限度发挥 App 的功能

title: Phenomenal for everyday money management
content: This app is exactly what I needed to keep on top of my money, and was the only one I could find with the functionality i needed.   This being said, a few minor details would make this app even more useful. Firstly, being able to edit the names and icons of sub-budget categories would be ideal. I don’t often use many of the preset categories, and it would be convenient to be able to budget for individual items inside of a project without having to use the preset categories and simply remember which category represents which item.  Additionally, another feature I would use if it was available would be the ability to allocate only a selected amount of an income into a budget project. It can be quite a hassle trying to separate an income into multiple parts if I want to put some of it away, especially if the income was not recent. I understand this capability may be available via the split payment premium feature, however, I am unsure of the exact specifications of this feature given that I use the free version.

content: Want to be able to change the order of category in the widget

content: Widget shows ‘unable to load’ after upgrade to IOS 13  Thanks

title: Great APP
content: Very straightforward to use. And the community is healthy. Well done!

title: 最好用的记账软件！！
content: moze是我目前用过记账最爽快的记账app，尤其是更新3.0后，简直爱不释手，闲着没事都想打开划一划。现在唯一的遗憾就是还没有共同记账的功能了，期待！

title: 很棒的記帳軟體
content: 介面清楚、簡單好用！

title: Moze 3.0 is so great!
content: The best finance tracker I’ve ever used.

title: 感谢让我养成了记账的习惯

title: Amazing so far!
content: I just started using the app and input all of my transactions since the start of 2025. It took me a bit to clean the data for uploading, but now that I have, I’m enjoying exploring the app! The highlight for me is that it doesn’t force you to start with a budget. I really just want to see where my money is going and this app does exactly that. You CAN set budgets, but it’s not like most apps where that is the primary feature. The interface is amazing. It fits right in with the UI of standard Apple apps (gives me reminders vibes). There are a lot of things I love about it, but I also want to suggest a couple improvements to make it even better!  1. Give us a chance to set a starting balance on a certain date. All my transactions start 1/1/25 so the balances were off and when I did manual adjustments to get them right it marked the date as today. Which puts it in the middle of the year since I imported old transactions.   It just makes things kind of wonky. It would be great if the app let me say “here’s what my balances were on 12/31/24” and go from there.   2. It would be nice to be able to change the color/icon for all categories in a folder at once. I wanted to change up the colors and it was kind of time consuming to do it individually. I have a feeling I’ll want to do it again eventually because I love the customization options!

I came across Budget Flow earlier this year and it was so close to being what I needed. Fast forward a few months and 2.0 was released and it hits 99.99% of what I need. It is an AMAZING app and I’m surprised it hasn’t gotten more traction yet.   Expenses are easy to enter and it allows for recurring transaction which makes it easy to set up for typical monthly expenses. You can configure notification reminders for expenses, set up budgets and look at forecasts. Planned transactions are simple to incorporate into accounts and tagging covers the last mile not covered by the really good payee and category support. I haven’t fully exercised the reporting capabilities and will evaluate that more in time.   The transaction view is a little non-traditional but it easy to get used to. The app interface is very thoughtful and carefully considered. It has optional settings for the few things that it should. The great part is that the app is available on iPhone and is as carefully and masterfully crafted on that platform as well.   Small improvements for some might be in better transaction import features but that’s about the only thing I can think of.   This will definitely replace my Numbers spreadsheet and the developer seems fully engaged with this product and users. I HIGHLY recommend this for someone needing to keep track of personal, family, or even small business expenses and account statuses.

title: The Most Practical Way to Budget AFAIK
content: It was unusually difficult to find an budgeting method that didn’t require an online account or - at the other end of the spectrum - required me to basically be my own accountant in the worst way. This is the best mix of detail, privacy, and accessibility that I’ve ever seen in a budget tracking or data utility app in general. I spend very little time thinking about money now, while I’ve saved and invested more than ever since using this app. It gives me the information I need about my spending and gets out of my way otherwise. There is actually a lot of room to budget in different and dare I say creative ways here.   In my case, I’m meticulous but lazy. I track every novel purchase, rounded up to the nearest dollar, but I’ve added regular costs that fluctuate as fixed monthly costs based on their average e.g. a tank of gas every two weeks. That makes my cost of living more or less built in to the budget, so my balance is 100% for food and leisure barring emergencies and other surprises. Psychologically this does wonders; knowing that your needs are financially accounted for makes you feel almost like a kid saving up 10s and 20s for the thing you want. Even if it’s what you would consider pocket change after the bills are paid, you have a clear idea of what you can spend freely. Granted, this is an aspect of household budgeting when done right anyway, here it is achieved with very little effort.
